suggestion.title: Adform Script Integrity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes poisoning of Adform script. Pipeline should detect unauthorized modifications to ad-tech vendor scripts before deployment to customer sites. Article phrase: 'Hackers Poison Adform Script'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to Adform script files or delivery infrastructure (checksum mismatches, signature validation failures). Alert on unsigned or newly-signed script variants. Track script parameter changes that modify behavioral flow (particularly wallet address substitution patterns).

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Substitution in Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: swapping legitimate wallet addresses for attacker-controlled ones. Article phrase: 'Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites'. This is DOM manipulation and content injection detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript execution that modifies wallet address fields or transaction destination values at runtime. Flag scripts that search-and-replace blockchain addresses or inject new wallet identifiers into payment forms. Correlate with outbound crypto transactions to non-whitelisted addresses.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Script Source Verification Failure
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks depend on bypassin script authenticity checks. Pipeline should surface detection around ad-tech vendor script validation. Article phrase: 'poisoned Adform script to swap...across customer sites' implies compromise of trusted vendor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate script source origin via certificate pinning, SRI (Subresource Integrity) hash mismatches, or CDN route anomalies. Alert when Adform script is served from unexpected IP ranges or with modified Content-Security-Policy headers.

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Behavior: Outbound Crypto Address Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious script must communicate or store attacker wallet addresses. Detection should catch scripts making unusual DNS queries for crypto exchanges, wallets, or C2 infrastructure. Article implies script knows alternative wallet addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scripts generating DNS queries to cryptocurrency service domains (exchanges, wallet providers, block explorers) from ad-tech context. Flag inline scripts that construct or encode hex-encoded Ethereum/Bitcoin addresses. Detect WebSocket or HTTP exfil to crypto monitoring services.

suggestion.title: Ad-Tech Script Parameter Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned Adform script likely modified via injection into query parameters or script configuration. Detection should catch parameter tampering specific to ad-tech platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unusual query parameters on Adform script load requests (e.g., extra cryptographic material, obfuscated callback URLs, or base64-encoded wallet lists). Flag requests with syntax errors in ad-tech parameters or unexpected callback hosts.

suggestion.title: Crypto Wallet Address Exfiltration via Ad Network
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is to redirect payments to attacker wallets. Detection should catch collection and transmission of wallet data through ad-network infrastructure. Article: 'Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scripts encoding legitimate wallet addresses (via regex or DOM scraping) and transmitting them to attacker-controlled collection domains. Monitor for unusual egress on port 443 to non-CDN IPs from Adform script context. Flag Base64/hex-encoded strings matching known cryptocurrency address formats.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Wi-Fi Network Spoofing or Hijacking Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes hijacked hotel Wi-Fi as attack vector: 'Hijacked Hotel Wi-Fi Pushes Fake Updates'. Pipeline generated no initial-access detection. Should detect rogue SSID cloning, unauthorized DHCP serving, or DNS hijacking on enterprise/hospitality networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious Wi-Fi access points or network infrastructure changes. Look for duplicate SSIDs from unexpected BSSIDs, DHCP pools redirecting to attacker-controlled gateways, or DNS responses inconsistent with legitimate ISP authoritative servers. Correlate with user device connections to rogue networks.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Delivery and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'Pushes Fake Updates to Deliver Surveillance Malware'. Pipeline generated zero execution detections. Should capture fake update prompts, out-of-band update initiation, unsigned or mismatched signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for update prompts or installers originating from non-standard sources (hotel guest networks, ad-hoc HTTP instead of HTTPS, unsigned binaries). Detect process execution of update-related files downloaded from untrusted network segments. Correlate unsolicited update UX with eventual surveillance malware execution.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware C2 Communications from Hotel Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Surveillance Malware' payload but pipeline generated no C2 or collection detection. Should detect outbound C2 beaconing, encrypted exfiltration, or keylog/camera capture traffic from guests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 beacons or exfiltration patterns from endpoints connected to hotel guest Wi-Fi: unusual outbound HTTPS to low-reputation IPs/domains, beaconing intervals inconsistent with legitimate software, DNS queries for suspicious subdomains, or encrypted payloads to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting or Keystroke Logging via Guest Wi-Fi
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Surveillance Malware' but pipeline produced no credential-access or collection hypotheses. Typical hotel Wi-Fi attacks harvest login credentials or capture sensitive input from guests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for keylogger/screen-capture library loading (e.g. user32.dll hooks, directx input interception), unusual input-device drivers, or clipboard access from low-integrity processes. Correlate with process execution from hotel Wi-Fi-delivered installer.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware requires persistence, but pipeline generated no persistence detection. Attackers typically install scheduled tasks, services, or registry runkeys from hotel Wi-Fi compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks, Windows services, or registry HKLM/HKCU Run keys by processes spawned from the fake-update installer. Look for tasks executing from suspicious locations or with unusual intervals. Cross-reference task/service binaries with malware families.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Behavior Post-Wi-Fi Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies widespread guest infection risk but pipeline generated no behavioral anomaly detection. Surveillance malware on hotel guests' devices will exhibit increased CPU, network, or battery drain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify spikes in network egress, sustained CPU/memory by suspicious processes, or unexpected wake-locks on mobile/laptop devices shortly after guest Wi-Fi connection. Correlate with known malware process names or suspicious network destinations.

suggestion.title: PATCH request with JSON body containing $pullAll operator to ApostropheCMS API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'authenticated editor to write arbitrary values to Object.prototype via the $pullAll patch operator.' No UC inspects request body for the actual payload structure (JSON with $pullAll key). This is the definitive attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* where Content-Type is application/json and the request body contains the JSON key '$pullAll' at any nesting level. Correlate with authenticated user session context to identify legitimate vs. malicious editor activity.

suggestion.title: Successful data access to protected ApostropheCMS endpoints post-PATCH without re-authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'process-wide authorization bypass.' A successful PATCH pollutes Object.prototype globally; subsequent requests from different users/sessions should still succeed if auth bypass persists. No UC detects cross-session authorization failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cases where a PATCH request from one user is followed by successful GET requests to protected endpoints from a different user/session ID within seconds, without corresponding re-authentication events. This signals auth context pollution.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS API error responses or exceptions containing '__proto__' or 'constructor' strings
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'confirmed gadget' implying the vulnerability has known error signatures or exceptions. Application error logs or HTTP error responses may leak evidence of failed prototype-pollution attempts or gadget invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ApostropheCMS application error logs or HTTP error response bodies for JavaScript prototype keywords (__proto__, constructor, Object.prototype). These may indicate attempted or successful prototype-pollution exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS authenticated user session generating PATCH then immediate administrative API actions from same session
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the attacker as 'authenticated editor' but the impact is 'process-wide authorization bypass.' After exploiting, the same editor session may gain elevated capabilities (reading/modifying admin fields, accessing user data). No UC detects privilege escalation within a single session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PATCH requests from an authenticated editor account with subsequent API calls to protected/admin-only endpoints from the same session. Compare called endpoints against the editor's baseline privileges; flag unauthorized cross-privilege calls.

suggestion.title: Multiple failed PATCH requests to ApostropheCMS API from same source within short window (exploitation attempts)
suggestion.rationale: Article states the gadget is 'confirmed,' implying attackers may probe multiple payload variations. Rapid PATCH attempts with varying payloads are unlikely in legitimate use and suggest exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* from the same source IP within 60 seconds where HTTP status indicates errors (4xx, 5xx). This pattern suggests payloads being refined or multiple gadgets being tested.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) Session Proxy Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes AiTM as core technique: 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' is listed in schema keywords; common in Midnight Blizzard traveler-targeting campaigns to intercept and relay authentication sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect proxy-based credential interception by identifying authentication requests passing through attacker-controlled infrastructure, unusual token issuance patterns from non-canonical IP geographies, or simultaneous session logins from geographically disparate locations for the same user within subsecond intervals.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Execution via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Schema explicitly tags 'ClickFix' and 'social engineering'; ClickFix is Midnight Blizzard's known technique for driving malware execution through deceptive browser notifications and fake warnings to travelers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on users executing files or scripts within minutes of clicking suspicious browser-popup links, especially from hotel/airport networks (GeoIP or SSID correlation). Flag parent processes matching known browser vendors spawning unexpected child processes like cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl.

suggestion.title: Captive Portal Spoofing and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: CaptiveCrunch campaign name and 'credential theft' keyword indicate spoofed captive portals at travel hubs; no use case covers detection of fake login pages or harvested travel-related credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic to lookalike travel-provider domains (hotels, airlines, airports) from public WiFi networks, especially with traffic volume or certificate anomalies. Correlate user credentials reuse across non-travel platforms post-event. Monitor for email alerts about suspicious login attempts on travel-linked accounts within 24–48 hours of portal interaction.

suggestion.title: Midnight Blizzard Malware Delivery Campaign Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title and actor keywords ('Midnight Blizzard', 'malware delivery') establish malware as primary payload; pipeline failed to generate detections for malware staging, C2 beaconing, or post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .exe, .msi, .dll, or script files downloaded from travel-related URLs (airlines, hotel booking sites) or email with headers spoofing travel providers. Correlate with process execution anomalies (parent process mismatch, unsigned binaries, living-off-the-land execution from temp directories).

suggestion.title: Token and Session Cookie Theft Post-AiTM
suggestion.rationale: Schema lists 'token theft', 'credential theft', and keywords imply session hijacking; no use case specifically detects token/cookie exfiltration or downstream token reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect stolen tokens by identifying OAuth/session tokens used from non-canonical IPs or user-agents within minutes of credential entry, especially tokens reused across multiple cloud services (Azure, Microsoft 365, AWS) from geographically distant locations in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Geographically Anomalous Travel-Related Authentication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets 'travelers worldwide'; no use case captures impossible-travel or geographically improbable access to travel-linked accounts or services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts to travel-linked accounts (airline loyalty, hotel chains, airport systems) from IPs >2000km distant within <2 hours, or from VPN/proxy IPs correlated with Midnight Blizzard infrastructure. Correlate login geo with user's last-known location.

suggestion.title: NightLedger DLL Hijacking via AppVShNotify.exe Sideloading
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes signature technique: 'NightLedger masquerades as SspiCli.dll and is designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is the core execution mechanism and should have immediate coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for AppVShNotify.exe spawning or loading unsigned SspiCli.dll from non-system paths, especially alongside RPCRT4.dll imports. RPC API calls to methods requiring authentication should precede SspiCli loading. Cross-reference creation timestamps of SspiCli.dll against AppVShNotify.exe execution; mismatches suggest sideloading.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneling Activity (BridgeHead/ArcBridge Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes two custom WebSocket tunnelers ('ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling') deployed during post-exploitation. 'BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) initiated by unexpected processes, particularly from engineering/security-focused endpoints. BridgeHead/ArcBridge show anomalous patterns: inbound tunneling operators controlling victim networks through WebSocket channels. Correlate with NightLedger indicators and aerospace/defense targeting profile.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing with Third-Party File-Sharing Redirects (Recruitment Lures)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector in detail: 'lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services. These lures included recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms.' This is documented initial access but has no detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email clicks leading to lookalike videoconferencing domains followed by redirects to third-party file-sharing services (Mega.nz, file upload sites). Correlate with recruitment-themed subject lines and aerospace/aviation/defense company employee targeting. Flag downloads of .zip/.rar archives from these redirects.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Post-Compromise Reconnaissance (Process Discovery & Screenshot Capture)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies backdoor capabilities: 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture.' These post-compromise behaviors are signature indicators for NightLedger activity but lack detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 10-60 seconds of process execution, detect suspicious query patterns: Get-Process calls, tasklist.exe, wmic process listing, or registry enumeration of running services. Correlate with ScreenCapture API calls or GDI+ image buffer operations. NightLedger discovery pattern: enumerate → capture screen → exfil.

suggestion.title: RPCRT4.dll Delay-Loading SspiCli.dll Authentication Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article technical detail: 'AppVShNotify.exe imports RPCRT4.dll, which can delay-load SspiCli.dll when it invokes an RPC API that requires authentication.' This is a forensic and behavioral indicator unique to NightLedger's implementation approach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AppVShNotify.exe → RPCRT4.dll → SspiCli.dll load chain where SspiCli is unsigned, resides outside System32, or has mismatched timestamps. Authenticate via code signing certificates; legitimate RPCRT4 SspiCli chains use Microsoft-signed DLLs.

suggestion.title: Masquerading Backdoor File Names (SspiCli.dll Impersonation)
suggestion.rationale: NightLedger 'masquerades as SspiCli.dll' — a legitimate Windows authentication library — to evade detection. This masquerading technique should trigger when unsigned DLLs use system library names outside proper versioning paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or loading of SspiCli.dll outside C:\Windows\System32 and C:\Windows\SysWOW64 with version info mismatches (missing or false Microsoft signature). Cross-check against NIST/MS libraries; malicious SspiCli often lacks proper version strings or certificate chains.

suggestion.title: FMC Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states FMC vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker' — indicating public-facing exposure. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure hunt despite template explicitly referencing _TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20316 on Cisco FMC devices. Cross-reference exposed management IPs against internal asset inventory; flag FMC instances reachable from untrusted networks or with direct internet routing.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — indicates credential-based access. No credential_access phase detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded account names (often 'admin' or vendor-default accounts). Correlate with failed login attempts prior to success. Flag logins from non-standard timezones or IPs outside known corporate ranges.

suggestion.title: Low-Privileged Account Accessing Sensitive FMC Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account to access sensitive data' — indicates privilege escalation or lateral data access after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on low-privileged FMC user accounts querying, exporting, or accessing configuration data, policy definitions, or firewall rule sets that should only be readable by high-privilege roles. Track data exports via API, GUI, or configuration backups.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Access from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerability enables remote unauthenticated access to management interface. No detection for unexpected source IPs or geographic anomalies in management plane access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate FMC management access locations (expected admin IP ranges, VPN gateways, secure admin networks). Flag login attempts to FMC management interface from IPs outside baseline or from known public internet ranges; particularly logins followed by API calls or config queries.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration or Policy Manipulation Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains FMC access via hard-coded password, article implies sensitive data access — potential stepping stone to firewall policy tampering, rule disabling, or traffic redirection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit FMC configuration change logs for modifications to firewall policies, access control rules, logging rules, or threat intelligence feeds made by low-privileged accounts or during windows inconsistent with change management schedules. Alert on mass rule deletions or logging disablement.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from FMC to Protected Firewall Assets
suggestion.rationale: FMC is the management plane for Cisco firewalls; compromise provides vantage for lateral movement to managed perimeter devices. Article does not mention this, but is implicit in 'FMC contains sensitive data'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FMC compromise indicators with subsequent unexpected API calls, SSH sessions, or management-plane logins from the FMC to managed firewall devices outside normal admin activity patterns. Flag new admin account provisioning on managed devices shortly after FMC access.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access possible, indicating network exposure. Pipe scanner output for FMC instances visible to untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances reachable from internet or non-corporate IP ranges. Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 detections and correlate with network-reachability scan data. Flag any FMC instances responding on standard management ports (443, 8305) from public IPs without documented proxy/VPN enforcement.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication: Low-Privilege FMC Logins
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Detect authentication using known default/hard-coded FMC credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins by documented low-privileged default accounts (e.g., 'admin', service accounts with known weak passwords). Alert on: first-time logins from untrusted geographies, login anomalies (time-of-day, source IP patterns), and account lockout recovery after failed login bursts. Baseline legitimate administrative access and flag deviation.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Query and Export by Suspicious Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—policies, credentials, topology. Detect queries or bulk exports by compromised low-privileged account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query FMC audit logs for data-access operations (policy export, rule dump, config download, credential retrieval) by low-privilege accounts. Flag access to sensitive object classes outside normal change-control windows. Correlate with failed-login or suspicious-login events preceding data access to isolate compromised-credential scenario.

suggestion.title: Patch-Claim vs. Vulnerability-Scan Mismatch: CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'; federal due date 2026-08-01. Detect claimed patches that don't match actual vulnerability-scan results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare vulnerability scanner output (CVE-2026-20316 detections) against asset inventory patch dates. Flag any FMC instances claiming patch date ≥ 2026-08-01 but scanner still reports vulnerable version. Cross-validate with firmware/OS patch records from host agents to identify desyncs.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement: FMC-Extracted Credentials Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password grants access to 'sensitive data'—FMC stores embedded credentials (SNMP, API keys, SSH). Detect lateral movement after FMC compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-FMC compromise, attacker exports stored credentials or policy configs. Monitor for FMC initiating connections to infrastructure outside normal baselines (target firewalls, managed switches, threat intel feeds). Alert on SSH/SNMP/API authentication attempts to those targets using credentials or patterns consistent with FMC-embedded values.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Successful Auth from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device.' Pipeline missed detection UC for anomalous FMC authentication patterns by source geography, ASN, or frequency baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC access logs for successful authentications from IPs outside administrative baselines. Alert if preceded by ≥3 failed auth attempts within 60 seconds using low-privileged account names (e.g., 'admin', 'fmc_user').

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Brute Force Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline omitted detection for credential-stuffing or repeated-attempt patterns against known default/low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequential failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC using hardcoded or low-privilege account names, followed by successful login. Baseline expected failure rates per source IP; flag >10× normal rate.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication (Cisco FMC)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline missed collection-phase UC for policy exports, configuration retrieval, or credential dumps from FMC after successful low-privilege authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for policy exports, configuration backups, or credential queries initiated by low-privileged accounts within 5 minutes of failed-then-successful authentication or from new-to-site source IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public-Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies internet-facing FMC instances are prerequisite for active exploitation. Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' requires asset-level validation. Pipeline omitted vulnerability/asset correlation UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and scanning tools for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances. Cross-reference public IP address data to confirm internet exposure. Correlate with patch-management output to identify systems still running vulnerable versions post-due-date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Network Reconnaissance (Port/Service Scanning)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'currently being exploited in the wild' (CISA KEV). Pipeline missed early-stage UC for attacker reconnaissance: port scanning or HTTP probing against known FMC default ports (443, 8305).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequences of failed TCP connections to Cisco FMC default ports (443, 8305) from external IPs, followed by successful HTTP 200/302 responses (successful probing). Baseline external probe rates; flag >2σ deviations per source subnet.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access to FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — initial connection attempts to exposed FMC management endpoints must be first detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) from untrusted/external sources. Correlate unauthenticated connection attempts with authentication events to identify exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability leverages 'hard-coded password' to bypass authentication — detection must flag login attempts using known weak/default credentials documented in Cisco advisories or credential stuffing against FMC accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful or repeated failed authentication to FMC using low-privileged or default account names. Alert on authentication from geographically improbable or off-hours sources, especially from internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Within Compromised FMC Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-authentication — collection activity via compromised management interface is critical second-stage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual policy exports, rule queries, or credential vault access from authenticated but anomalous sessions. Alert on bulk config dumps or API calls targeting security objects outside normal admin patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes urgency ('patch due 2026-08-01') and active exploitation; asset inventory for exposed instances is remediation prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco FMC instances with internet-routable IPs or DNS; cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Identify instances without VPN/WAF access controls.

suggestion.title: FMC Administrative Session Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential abuse typically manifests as access anomalies outside legitimate admin behavior — logins from unexpected geographies, IPs, or outside operational hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate FMC admin access (time windows, source IPs, user agents). Alert on successful authentication outside baseline — especially low-privileged accounts accessing sensitive functions.

suggestion.title: FMC Security Policy or Firewall Rule Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated via hard-coded credentials, adversaries prioritize extracting security policies and rule sets — article specifies 'sensitive data' is target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for policy/rule export operations targeting multiple rule sets, triggered by non-administrative accounts, or followed by lateral data transfer to external networks. Flag bulk policy API queries.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit via hard-coded password; standard CISA KEV workflow requires asset inventory. Referenced template `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure` was never applied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and network telemetry to identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances exposed on internet-facing networks. Correlate against patch status; alert on unpatched FMC with listening ports 443/8305.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'use of hard-coded password' allows login. No UC captures failed/successful auth attempts with default/hard-coded account names against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs and firewall authentication events for login attempts using known hard-coded or default account names (e.g., 'admin', 'root', 'cisco'). Alert on successful authentication from external IP ranges; correlate with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability status.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No UC detects unauthorized reads of FMC configuration, policy, or credential repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual data retrieval from FMC after successful low-privileged login: bulk export of firewall rules, threat intelligence policies, or credential stores. Baseline normal admin activity and alert on out-of-hours access or high-volume reads.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model includes gaining access to 'impacted systems'; confirmed compromise would likely result in policy/rule modification to maintain persistence or evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new administrative accounts or modification of existing firewall policies/rules within 48 hours of initial login with low-privileged hard-coded credentials. Flag any changes to logging, alerting, or access controls.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states affected product is 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)' with known CVE-2026-20316. Standard asset-exposure hunt: identify vulnerable versions before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 findings against Cisco FMC assets. Cross-reference asset inventory for FMC versions pre-patch. Establish baseline of exposed FMC management interfaces (ports 8305/443) accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Remote Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' via hard-coded password. Detection should cover authentication attempts against FMC management interface from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for: (1) failed login attempts from external IPs, (2) successful low-privileged account logins from non-administrative networks, (3) login attempts immediately followed by privilege escalation attempts or configuration queries.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after low-privileged login. Should detect unusual query/export patterns on configuration, policy, or credential repositories post-login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal administrative queries against FMC sensitive data (policies, device configs, credentials). Flag low-privileged accounts or non-administrative sources querying sensitive policy/credential repositories, especially bulk exports or unusual command sequences.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Default Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly involves 'hard-coded password'. Should detect authentication using known/default credentials against FMC management services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication for use of known default account names (admin, root, cisco, etc.) from any source IP. Flag successful logins using default credentials or logins where password hash/attempt matches known weak/default values.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerability is only exploitable if FMC management port is accessible remotely. Article implies public-facing exposure by noting 'remote attacker' can exploit.
log_sources: Network asset scanning (Shodan, Censys, internal port scans)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal network for Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 8305, 443, 22) accessible from DMZ or external networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner to identify exposed+vulnerable instances. Flag any FMC management traffic from non-administrative network segments.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'public-facing application' and explicitly calls for asset-exposure hunt template. Phrase 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker' presupposes internet accessibility—exposure detection is the baseline hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 443, 8305, 8307) receiving inbound connections from internet-sourced IPs. suggestion.title: FMC Low-Privileged Account Privilege-Escalation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account'—if attacker gains such access, they will attempt to escalate. This phase-2 activity is a critical follow-on indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege-escalation attempts from low-privileged FMC accounts, including role-elevation requests, SSH/HTTPS tunnel creation, or execution of administrative commands (e.g., CLI access to backup config, snapshot export, or policy modifications).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—indicates publicly exposed management interface. No detection for FMC admin ports (8305/TCP, 443/HTTPS) visible on untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management service ports exposed to internet or untrusted ASNs. Cross-correlate with asset inventory to flag management interfaces outside approved jump-box / corporate network segments. Monitor shodan/censys for public FMC discovery.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Account Successful Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'hard-coded password vulnerability...log in to an affected device'—no detection for successful FMC logins using known default accounts or credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC admin console authentication using hard-coded or known default service accounts. Flag logins outside known change windows, or from IPs never seen authenticating before. Cross-reference with patch status—unpatched FMC + successful default-credential login = incident.

suggestion.title: FMC Policy & Topology Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—no detection for low-privilege or default-account downloads of firewall policies, rule bases, network topology, or credential stores from FMC database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk exports, database queries, or API calls by default/low-privileged accounts targeting access control rules, VPN configurations, managed device inventories, or stored credentials. Alert on config backups downloaded outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FMC Policy Injection to Managed Devices
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC can push malicious policies to managed firewalls—no detection for suspicious policy changes or command execution routed through FMC to compromise firewall fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC deploying new access control rules, disabling security services, or modifying VPN credentials on managed firewalls after detected compromise. Monitor for FMC exfiltrating managed device SSH keys, TACACS credentials, or snmp communities.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploit Attempt Signature
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV lists active exploitation—no signature or behavioral detection for known payload patterns, web request sequences, or bypass techniques targeting this specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy IDS/IPS signatures for CVE-2026-20316 exploitation attempts (e.g., hard-coded credential bypass payloads, authentication endpoint bypass, URL-based credential injection patterns). Monitor Shodan/public exploit repos for known attack signatures; correlate inbound traffic with FMC IP space.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC authentication with hardcoded/low-privilege accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—this is the exploitation vector. Must monitor FMC authentication logs for logins using known hardcoded service accounts from unexpected locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins with known hardcoded account names (service accounts, default credentials) especially from external/untrusted IPs. Alert on brute-force patterns (multiple failures) followed by success using same hardcoded account. Establish baseline of legitimate admin authentication sources.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and port scanning for exposed Cisco FMC management interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article's CISA KEV status ('observed exploited in the wild') implies active discovery campaigns. Attackers must locate exposed FMC instances. Monitor network for HTTP probes, banner grabbing, and version detection targeting FMC ports (443, 8305).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid connection attempts to FMC management ports across network ranges, HTTP HEAD requests or version-detection probes targeting Cisco FMC, SSL certificate fingerprinting matching Cisco Firepower certificates, or User-Agent strings consistent with reconnaissance tools scanning for FMC.

suggestion.title: Bulk data exfiltration and configuration theft from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat enables 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-authentication, attackers will extract firewall policies, rules, and logs. Monitor FMC for unauthorized data access and export operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit/API logs for bulk policy downloads, configuration exports, or unusual database queries. Alert on large data transfers from FMC to external IPs. Correlate data-access events with authentication anomalies (hardcoded account login immediately followed by policy export).

suggestion.title: Policy manipulation and lateral movement from compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC manages all deployed firewalls. Once compromised via hardcoded credentials, attackers gain pivot point into firewall infrastructure. Monitor for suspicious administrative actions and rule changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual policy deployments, rule modifications, or administrative commands from FMC to managed firewalls during unusual hours. Alert on rule changes disabling intrusion prevention, logging, or exfiltration controls. Monitor for accounts with FMC admin access performing actions outside normal change windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC fingerprinting and version enumeration attempts
suggestion.rationale: Attackers performing early-stage reconnaissance must fingerprint FMC versions to confirm vulnerability applicability before exploitation. Monitor for version-detection HTTP patterns and SSL certificate queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests with paths commonly used in FMC fingerprinting (/login, /api/platform/version, /admin/), SSL certificate thumbprint matches for Cisco Firepower software, or repeated connection attempts to FMC management interface with varying payloads suggesting version detection.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can 'log in to an affected device' via hard-coded credential; no detection logic was generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected network segments or geographies, or login attempts using default/hard-coded service accounts. Flag any remote access to FMC ports (8300, 8305) from non-trusted subnets.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'; no UC to detect suspicious data queries or exports from FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data retrieval operations from FMC (policy queries, configuration exports, security event log downloads) executed by non-administrative accounts or from unusual API clients/sessions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration or Policy Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Compromised low-privileged FMC account could be leveraged for lateral movement or persistence; article does not specify scope of 'low-privileged account' permissions but tampering is a plausible follow-on.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for unauthorized creation of admin accounts, modification of security policies, or whitelisting of malicious IPs by non-authorized users.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Service Anomalies / Process Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article implies remote code execution risk implied by 'access to sensitive data' after unauthenticated login; no UC for process-level or service-level tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Cisco FMC services (java, python) or suspicious command-line invocations from the FMC application directory; correlate with failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC C2 Beaconing / Network Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Once compromised via hard-coded credential, FMC could be commandeered for lateral movement or exfiltration; no UC for network-level detection from the FMC host itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from Cisco FMC hosts to non-sanctioned IPs (especially non-managed devices or external C2 infrastructure); monitor for encrypted tunnels or suspicious DNS queries originating from FMC.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit across the network—requires initial enumeration of exposed FMC management interfaces on standard ports (443, 8305, 8307).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances exposed on internet-routable addresses via vulnerability scanners and passive reconnaissance. Correlate exposed instances against asset inventory to identify systems not patched by federal due date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Exploitation—FMC Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—requires detection of authentication succeeding with known hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC auth logs for successful login attempts using default or disclosed hard-coded account credentials from non-whitelisted source IPs. Flag logins at off-hours or from geographic anomalies. Correlate with known exploit scanner signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Sensitive Data Access—FMC Configuration & Policy Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of abnormal bulk exports, database queries, or configuration backups following successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large data queries, rapid result-set exports, configuration backup downloads, or policy file exports executed immediately after successful authentication. Flag API calls to sensitive endpoints (device configs, firewall rules, user accounts) from newly-authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Brute Force / Credential Spray Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: While hard-coded credentials bypass standard auth, attackers will still probe exposed FMC instances—requires detection of high-volume login attempts indicating active exploitation campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts >5 per 10-min or >50 per 60-min against FMC login interfaces. Correlate source IPs against threat intel feeds for known scanners/mass-exploitation tools. Alert on credential spray patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerable Version Inventory Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article names Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center as vulnerable product—requires enumeration of installed versions across infrastructure to identify those needing patching by federal due date 2026-08-01.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner outputs, CMDB, and asset inventories for all Cisco FMC instances with version identification. Identify systems running versions prior to the patch release date. Flag systems past the federal remediation deadline for escalation.

suggestion.title: Adform Script Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: hackers 'poison Adform script.' No detection for malicious modifications to third-party ad scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP responses from Adform CDN for unexpected JavaScript payload modifications. Compare script hashes against known-good vendor signatures. Alert on response sizes or content structure deviations from Adform's published builds.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'swap crypto wallet addresses'—the actual theft mechanism. No UC captures wallet parameter tampering in page DOM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify and beacon cryptocurrency wallet addresses embedded in ad-tech scripts. Alert on wallet address changes within injected Adform payloads. Cross-reference with blockchain threat intel to detect transfers to attacker-controlled addresses.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Integrity: Ad-Tech Vendor Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromise of vendor infrastructure impacting 'customer sites'—textbook T1195.002. No kill-chain phase reconstructed for initial vendor compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSL/TLS certificate issuance for Adform-related domains. Alert on DNS infrastructure changes, IP geolocation anomalies for CDN endpoints, and unexpected CNAME/ANAME records. Cross-reference certificate transparency logs with threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Browser-Side Financial Redirection via Third-Party Script
suggestion.rationale: Attack redirects crypto transfers via injected script—browser-based fraud. No detection for late-stage script payload substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inline JavaScript execution following third-party ad-tech script loading. Monitor for unusual DOM manipulation targeting payment fields. Alert on script size/entropy anomalies in Adform responses.

suggestion.title: Subresource Integrity Bypass and SRI Stripping
suggestion.rationale: Article implies removal or bypassing of script integrity controls ('poison' implies replacing legitimate script). No detection for SRI header removal or validation failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on missing Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes for Adform script tags. Monitor CSP violations related to inline-script execution. Flag script-src wildcards or 'unsafe-inline' in Content-Security-Policy headers after ad-tech load.

suggestion.title: Multi-Site Blast-Radius Correlation: Shared Vendor Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes impact 'across customer sites'—single vendor compromise affecting many orgs. No correlation detection for simultaneous indicator-of-compromise at multiple organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Adform-related security indicators (HTTP 200 with anomalous script payload, wallet address detections, SRI mismatches) across organizations known to share vendors. Alert if 3+ distinct customer organizations report related anomalies within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Delivery from Untrusted Network
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector explicitly stated: 'Pushes Fake Updates.' Pipeline should detect update binaries or installers delivered over compromised network with mismatched signatures or non-standard delivery paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of update installers (Windows Update, browser updates, OS patches) originating from non-standard sources (guest Wi-Fi, non-official CDNs). Cross-reference signature validity and installation context against legitimate update vectors. Flag updates that bypass UAC prompts or run with unexpected parent process.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Installation on Hotel Guest Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Deliver Surveillance Malware'—a post-execution payload. Should detect characteristic behaviors: keyloggers, screen capture, camera/microphone access, or clipboard hooking from processes spawned after fake update execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malware-typical behaviors post-installation: unusual WINAPI calls to capture/input APIs, registry modifications enabling screen capture or input hooking, process creation with high privilege escalation artifacts, and nascent C2 beacon attempts. Baseline legitimate apps; flag anomalies in hotel/guest contexts.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from Hotel Network Guest Device
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware requires C2 channel. Article implies exfiltration but pipeline missed command-and-control as a distinct detection opportunity: monitor outbound C2 traffic patterns post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect post-infection outbound traffic anomalies: regular beaconing to non-standard ports, HTTPS or DNS tunneling to suspicious domains, or traffic to known malware C2 infrastructure. Apply behavioral baseline—hotel guests rarely establish persistent outbound connections. Alert on encrypted traffic volumes and byte patterns consistent with data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Man-in-the-Middle Interception of Software Updates on Compromised Wi-Fi
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked Wi-Fi enables MITM attacks. Article mechanism requires intercepting legitimate update requests and redirecting to malicious payloads—a network-layer attack invisible to endpoint logs alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSL/TLS certificate mismatches for known update endpoints (Microsoft, Adobe, browser vendors). Monitor for ARP spoofing, DNS hijacking, or HTTP redirects on guest networks. Correlate failed certificate validations with subsequent suspicious child process execution.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Initiation from Compromised Hotel Network
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked Wi-Fi can pivot to internal networks. Article describes network-wide compromise but omits lateral-movement use case—a typical post-compromise step from a foothold in guest Wi-Fi.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag attempts to scan adjacent subnets, enumerate services, or establish SMB/RDP sessions originating from guest Wi-Fi interfaces. Monitor for credential harvesting or pass-the-hash indicators following initial malware deployment.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation: auth-bypassed access to sensitive Apostrophe piece-types by non-editor
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated editor' performs prototype pollution, but impact is 'process-wide authorization bypass.' Hunt should detect accounts that lack editor role successfully accessing global/user piece-type endpoints after __proto__ pollution window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Web.user role (e.g., viewer, guest) making successful GET requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/user or /api/v1/@apostrophecms/global after the site-wide PATCH window. Pollution persists in Object.prototype, so subsequent unprivileged sessions regain bypass.

suggestion.title: Apostrophe application-level: Object.prototype property access anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes prototype pollution of Object.prototype; detection should capture application logs or traces showing unexpected inherited properties in prototype chain, or authorization routines accessing __proto__ unexpectedly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt application-level logs (Node.js debug, Apostrophe framework logs) for __proto__ or constructor property access in request handling, or errors indicating unexpected property inheritance. Look for auth middleware evaluating object properties that should not exist.

suggestion.title: Credential-dumping via polluted Object.prototype: session/token exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'gadget' exists in confirmed exploitation path. Post-pollution, attacker can read polluted Object.prototype fields. Hunt should detect unusual data flows (e.g., tokens, session IDs) being returned in HTTP responses after __proto__ PATCH.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After PATCH to @apostrophecms API with __proto__, monitor subsequent GET responses for unexpected fields (tokens, session IDs, secrets) in JSON bodies. Compare response schemas before/after pollution window to detect schema inflation.

suggestion.title: Captive Portal Suspicious SSL Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'CaptiveCrunch' as malware delivery mechanism via captive portals. Schema keyword 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' indicates SSL interception. No detection for forced certificate installation or suspicious HTTPS redirection chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of certificates from non-standard locations or untrusted CAs, especially in traveler hotspot IP ranges. Detect SSLstrip or proxy tool execution (mitmproxy, Fiddler) combined with suspicious browser traffic interception patterns.

suggestion.title: ClickFix False Error Message and Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Schema explicitly tags 'ClickFix' as attack vector. This is a social engineering technique that displays fake error dialogs to trick users into downloading malware. No detection for registry modifications enabling fake dialogs or child process execution from browser download paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation from %TEMP% or %UserProfile%/Downloads with suspicious parent processes (explorer.exe, chrome.exe) followed by registry modifications in HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or Winlogon. Monitor for popup window creation (T1036.004) paired with rundll32/regsvr32 execution.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via Fake WiFi Portal Login
suggestion.rationale: Article title and schema keywords 'credential theft,' 'credential access,' and 'AiTM' indicate phishing for credentials at compromised or fake WiFi hotspots. Travelers on public WiFi are primary targets. No detection for unusual authentication patterns or credential submission to unexpected domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential submission (POST requests with username/password fields) to domains not matching legitimate WiFi hotspot ISP profiles. Correlate with browser traffic showing HTTP->HTTPS redirect chains and self-signed certificate installation. Monitor for credential input via browser to unexpected IP addresses in RFC 1918 ranges.

suggestion.title: Abnormal OAuth Token Exfiltration Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Schema keyword 'Token theft' indicates attackers stealing session/OAuth tokens after AiTM interception. No detection for exfiltration of authentication tokens or abnormal token usage from compromised sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for OAuth tokens or session cookies written to local files after authentication to hotspot portals (compare timestamp of auth event to file write). Cross-reference token exfiltration (outbound HTTPS POST with base64-encoded JWT) with geolocation changes showing impossible travel patterns from last known user location.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Compromised Browser Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article title lists 'malware delivery' as core attack objective. Schema keyword 'Windows' indicates Windows platform. CaptiveCrunch likely downloads and executes malware post-compromise. No detection for suspicious executable download or child process execution from browser.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .exe, .msi, or .dll file creation in %UserProfile%/Downloads or %TEMP% with file path containing suspicious keywords (update, flash, adobe, chrome). Correlate with parent process chrome.exe or msedge.exe executing child processes with process names matching Windows system utilities (svchost.exe, explorer.exe spawned by downloads).

suggestion.title: Traveler VPN/Proxy Traffic Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'travelers worldwide'—users on VPNs and proxies are common targets. Schema includes 'Storm' keyword suggesting Midnight Blizzard's infrastructure. No detection for traffic patterns consistent with VPN bypass or proxy interception in hotel/airport networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN traffic from corporate networks being rerouted through hotel/airport WiFi ISP. Alert on clients connecting to multiple geolocated networks within 4-hour window (impossible travel). Monitor for DNS queries resolving VPN/proxy domains to local IP addresses (DNS hijacking indicator of AiTM).

suggestion.title: DLL Search Order Hijacking via AppVShNotify.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details NightLedger masquerading as SspiCli.dll with DLL hijacking targeting AppVShNotify.exe: 'masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SspiCli.dll creation in non-standard directories (outside System32). Monitor AppVShNotify.exe loading DLLs from unexpected paths. Track parent-child relationships showing unexpected process spawning AppVShNotify.exe with suspicious module loading via RPCRT4.dll delay-load.

suggestion.title: Recruitment Lure Spear-Phishing with Videoconference Domain Lookalikes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial access using 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with job posting or hiring lures impersonating LinkedIn, Indeed, or similar. Alert on clicks to domains mimicking Zoom/Teams with typosquatting indicators. Correlate redirects to third-party file-sharing services within same session.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Staging via Third-Party File-Sharing Services
suggestion.rationale: Article documents delivery chain: 'malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services' following phishing redirection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on archive downloads (ZIP, RAR) from Dropbox, OneDrive, WeTransfer in aerospace/aviation sectors. Monitor extraction of executables or DLLs mimicking Windows system binaries. Correlate download timing with phishing email open/click timestamps.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneling Traffic (BridgeHead/ArcBridge C2 Channels)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers, ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained outbound WebSocket connections to newly registered or rare IPs. Alert on WebSocket traffic with binary payload signatures from process trees rooted in legitimate system binaries. Monitor for protocol tunneling indicators in WebSocket frame inspection.

suggestion.title: Screenshot Capture and Reconnaissance via NightLedger Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Article describes NightLedger capabilities: 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on screen capture API calls (GDIPLUS, BitBlt) from child processes spawned by AppVShNotify.exe. Correlate process enumeration commands (tasklist, wmic, Get-Process) with screenshot activity and WebSocket traffic.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Discovery in Aerospace Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization' indicating active reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In aerospace/defense sectors, alert on discovery command execution (tasklist, systeminfo, Get-Process) following file extraction from archive. Monitor for discovery-to-C2 temporal correlation, particularly from injected process contexts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must generate scanner-correlated IOC detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Qualys, Tenable) identifying CVE-2026-20316 on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Prioritize unpatched systems exposed to internet or untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patch-management records.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies FMC is public-facing (T1190). Must hunt for exposed management interfaces: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC instances (TCP 443, 8305, typical management ports) reachable from the internet. Verify network zone assignments and firewall rules permit management traffic only from legitimate admin sources. Flag instances in DMZ or untrusted zones.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Account Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Must detect authentication with known hardcoded credentials or anomalous login patterns post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Cisco FMC login from unexpected source IPs, especially from internet-routable addresses. Baseline normal admin login patterns. Flag repeated failed logins followed by success (credential guessing). Monitor for logins using known default or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Attacker exploits hardcoded credential to read policies, configs, or security posture data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk exports of firewall policies, rules, access-control lists, or threat-intelligence configurations executed by low-privileged or service accounts. Flag data exports not preceded by known maintenance windows or change tickets.

suggestion.title: FMC Policy Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: While article focuses on data access, hardcoded credential access could enable persistence via rule/policy injection or account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on security policy modifications (firewall rules, NAT rules, access controls) in FMC made by service or low-privileged accounts. Flag creation of new admin accounts or API credentials in FMC during the CVE exposure window (before 2026-08-01 patch due date).

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication with Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline missed detection of authentication attempts using known Cisco FMC default/hardcoded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentications to Cisco FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305) with known hardcoded service account credentials or anomalous low-privileged account logins from external networks. Correlate successful auth with sensitive data access within same session.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Access from External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker.' Pipeline ignored network-level detection of attempted/successful access to FMC management ports from internet-facing or unusual sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to FMC management interface (TCP 443, 8305, typical ports) from non-corp networks. Baseline against expected admin access patterns. Flag any successful establishment of TLS sessions followed by HTTP/HTTPS data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Low-Privileged FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' and 'low-privileged account.' Pipeline omitted detection of privilege-mismatch activity (low-priv account querying configs, policies, credential stores).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect database queries or API calls from low-privileged FMC service accounts accessing sensitive resources: firewall rule sets, VPN credentials, IPS/IDS policies, network configuration exports. Establish baseline of normal low-priv queries and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Export or Configuration Dump from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker with FMC access has ability to exfiltrate all managed firewall policies, VPN configs, and threat intelligence. Article emphasizes 'access sensitive data'—pipeline missed collection/exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large exports or API calls requesting full policy/configuration backups from FMC, especially when initiated by low-privileged accounts or outside change-control windows. Monitor for outbound SFTP/SCP transfers of .zip/.tar config bundles from FMC.

suggestion.title: FMC Brute Force Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Given hardcoded-password vulnerability, attackers may attempt credential guessing or brute force against known weak accounts. Pipeline did not generate auth-failure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-sequence failed authentication attempts against FMC admin/default accounts (admin, fmc, service accounts) within 5-minute window. Threshold: >5 failures from single source IP should trigger alert.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC typically has trust relationships with managed firewalls, switches, and other infrastructure. Article does not explicitly state this, but 'access sensitive data' implies ability to move laterally. Pipeline omitted trusted-relationship exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for unusual outbound connections to managed devices (firewalls, IPS, switches) outside scheduled sync windows. Detect SSH/Telnet attempts from FMC to administrative interfaces on managed infrastructure, which may indicate attacker attempting to pivot.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cisco FMC Authentication via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' and 'hard-coded password vulnerability' — establishes the primary attack vector; pipeline generated zero credential-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag failed-then-successful authentication sequences to Cisco FMC within short windows. Alert on authentication from non-allowlisted IPs or geolocations. Baseline admin/privileged account login times and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Sensitive Data Access on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — direct indicator of post-exploitation behavior; pipeline generated zero collection detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for low-privilege accounts (serviceaccount, guest, default users) querying or exporting sensitive configurations, credentials, or policy data. Establish baseline of what data each privilege tier accesses and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Access from Unexpected Network Segments
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' against internet-facing FMC; no detection for anomalous network access patterns; suggests attacker origin discovery is missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FMC authentication success/failure with source IP geolocation, ASN, and historical access baselines. Alert on logins from Tor, VPN, or high-risk geographies. Flag access from IPs not in allow-lists within 24 hours of exploitation window post-KEV publication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration or Credential Modification by Low-Privilege User
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sensitive data access leading to potential persistence or lateral movement; no detection for unauthorized system modifications by low-privilege account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to FMC users, firewall policies, or export of rule sets when initiated by low-privilege accounts. Correlate with successful unauthorized authentication events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Brute Force or Dictionary Attack

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FMC-authenticated sessions that suddenly deploy new firewall rules, modify device configs, or push policy changes inconsistent with normal baselines. Detect lateral movement via FMC's management access to deployed firewall/IPS sensors.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center — CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scan Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center / Firepower Management Center instances with positive detections for CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize externally-facing systems, as the vulnerability requires only unauthenticated remote access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC — Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts

Hard-coded credentials are static; multiple successful logins to the same account from different sources indicates exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC — Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privilege Accounts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Cisco FMC audit logs for policy downloads, configuration exports, certificate/key material access, or bulk system information queries initiated by low-privilege or default accounts. Unexpected data read operations from these accounts strongly indicate active exploitation.

suggestion.rationale: Article describes FMC vulnerability as affecting public-facing instances exploitable remotely. Network-level detection of inbound connections from suspicious origins indicates reconnaissance or exploitation attempts against vulnerable assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search network logs for inbound connections to Cisco FMC instances (HTTPS port 443, SSH port 22 if exposed) from external/untrusted IP ranges, known malicious IPs, or during off-hours. Sustained connection attempts or multiple failed/successful login sequences suggest active scanning or exploitation.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center internet-facing instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker' and references '_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure' — pipeline generated zero hunts despite this explicit guidance.

suggestion.title: Authentication with hard-coded credentials to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly enables 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account' — no detection for credential-based access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful authentication to Cisco FMC with known hard-coded username patterns (if disclosed by Cisco) or brute-force attempts against FMC login endpoints. Flag unusual geographic or timing patterns for FMC admin access.

suggestion.title: Sensitive data access from Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center

Monitor API calls to sensitive endpoints (policy/rules, threat data, system configuration) immediately after login, especially from newly-authenticated low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Failed baseline: CVE-2026-20316 presence in vulnerability scanner
