Baseline typical access patterns for legitimate operations; alert on bulk reads or access to sensitive object classes (credentials, threat feeds).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—requires detection of authentication success via hard-coded credential. Pipeline generated zero auth-based use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using low-privileged service accounts from untrusted source IPs or geographies. Establish baseline of legitimate admin access and alert on deviations, especially from internet-routable networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Export Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of configuration/credential exfiltration following compromise. Pipeline omitted collection-phase detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authenticated sessions to Cisco FMC that query, export, or download firewall policy configurations, access control lists, or stored credentials. Alert on bulk API calls to retrieve sensitive objects, especially within 1-4 hours of suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implies FMC is internet-facing or accessible without VPN. Pipeline did not generate asset-exposure or network-reconnaissance detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management interfaces (TCP 8305, 443) exposed on public-facing segments. Correlate CVE-2026-20316 patch inventory against network telemetry showing external HTTPS connections to FMC ports. Alert on repeated connection attempts across multiple source IPs.

suggestion.title: Brute Force Against Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Account
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password is a known value; attackers can enumerate the account name and systematically attempt login. Article does not rule out reconnaissance/brute-force prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for >5 failed login attempts to the same account within 10 minutes, especially from a single source or distributed sources (indicating coordinated brute force). Flag patterns matching known FMC service-account naming conventions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Authentication Using Hardcoded Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—this is T1078 (Valid Accounts), not just generic exploitation. Core attack step completely undetected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC from non-admin source IPs using the documented hardcoded low-privilege account. Hunt for failed-then-successful authentication sequences from external or unusual ASNs to FMC management interfaces within hours of patch miss.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data or Credential Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—implies collection of firewall policies, VPN credentials, and pre-shared keys stored in FMC config. This data access step missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for bulk policy downloads, credential backup exports, or VPN configuration retrieval from FMC via REST API or CLI shortly after anomalous login. Look for temp files containing encrypted secrets or plaintext pre-shared keys.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC as Lateral Movement Pivot to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC is a control plane—attacker gains config write access to all managed firewalls. Article's 'sensitive data' includes keys needed for VPN/tunnel compromise into protected networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious FMC login (T1078) + config export with subsequent unauthorized policy pushes to managed devices. Look for new ACL rules, VPN tunnels, or route additions appearing seconds after FMC compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Validation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires network access to FMC management ports (443, 8305). Article: 'remote attacker'—implies exposure. Pipeline correctly referenced asset-exposure template but generated no concrete hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco FMC instances; flag any accessible from internet-routable IPs on management ports. Cross-reference BGP leak/internet IP scanning data (Shadowserver, Censys) for unexpected FMC exposure in your IP ranges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active in-the-wild exploitation. Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'—scanner-based detection of unpatched instances is immediate, tangible hunt. Pipeline omitted this entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for any FMC with version pre-fix release. Authenticate to all known FMC instances and retrieve 'show version' output; flag those not on patched train. Daily alert if any unpatched instance remains after 2026-08-01 deadline.

suggestion.title: Adform Script Hash Anomaly – Supply Chain Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers poison Adform script' — Adform is a widely-embedded third-party ad network. Detection must identify when cached/served Adform scripts deviate from known-good signatures. Phrase: 'poison Adform script to swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare SHA256 hashes of Adform script payloads against vendor-published checksums. Alert if production Adform script on CDN or in customer logs differs from baseline. Correlate across multiple customer sites to detect blast radius.

suggestion.title: JavaScript-Based Payment Form Hijacking – DOM Mutation for Wallet Address Substitution
suggestion.rationale: The core attack is 'swap crypto wallet addresses' via injected script. This requires real-time DOM manipulation targeting input fields or JavaScript variables holding payment destinations. Phrase: 'swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript patterns that replace/override wallet address variables or input field values. Look for regex-based string substitution of common cryptocurrency address formats (0x..., bitcoin addresses, etc.) or API calls that POST wallet identifiers to unexpected endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Inline Script Injection in Third-Party Ad Frames
suggestion.rationale: To inject wallet-swapping logic into Adform's script execution context, attackers must inject new inline <script> tags or modify existing script code. Phrase: 'poison Adform script.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inline <script> tags within ad network iframes (Adform domain) that were not pre-approved or that execute wallet-related function calls. Compare Content-Security-Policy headers and detect CSP bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Crypto Addresses and User Payment Metadata via Malicious Ad Script
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned scripts likely exfiltrate original wallet addresses or private key metadata before substitution. Phrase: 'swap crypto wallet addresses' implies capture of victim data before replacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected HTTPS POST requests originating from Adform script context to domains outside the ad network's approved C2 or data collection allowlist. Flag requests containing cryptocurrency address strings or key-like hex/base58 patterns.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Blast-Radius Correlation – Adform Customer Site Inventory
suggestion.rationale: The attack affected 'customer sites' (plural, wide blast radius). Detection must correlate Adform script compromise across all organization domains to measure attack scope. Phrase: 'across customer sites.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build CMDB inventory of all internal + customer-facing sites that embed Adform scripts (grep for adform.net, adform.js patterns in HTML). Cross-check against list of sites known to have displayed poisoned script. Calculate blast radius and mean-time-to-detection for each affected site.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Replacement Pattern – Regex Substitution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Wallet-address swapping is a deterministic string replacement attack. Detection can pattern-match against known attacker wallet addresses or identify substitution logic in minified/obfuscated Adform script. Phrase: 'swap crypto wallet addresses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deobfuscate Adform script and search for regex patterns or hardcoded wallet addresses. Compare against known attacker-controlled wallets (via blockchain forensics or threat feeds). Alert on match to any customer site serving that script version.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Delivery via Network Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi pushes fake updates.' Pipeline missed the supply-chain-like delivery mechanism where attacker-controlled network serves counterfeit update packages to connected clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for update process execution (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, svchost.exe, updater.exe) spawned from unusual parent processes or initiated over non-standard update server IPs. Flag update binaries with mismatched signatures or unexpected code-signing timestamps.

suggestion.title: Man-in-the-Middle Attack via Wi-Fi Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi'—this is network compromise and traffic interception. Pipeline did not reconstruct this critical initial access vector or suggest detection for ARP spoofing, DNS poisoning, or rogue AP beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal Wi-Fi AP announcements (same SSID, different BSSID/MAC), traffic to unexpected gateways, or ARP spoofing patterns. Correlate client DNS requests to attacker-controlled resolvers or certificate validation failures during update checks to known-good update domains.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Execution and Collection from Compromised Devices
suggestion.rationale: Payload described as 'surveillance malware' but pipeline generated no detection logic for post-execution behavior—screen capture, keylogging, camera/microphone access, or data staging for exfiltration typical of surveillance payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unsigned or anomalous child processes spawned by the injected update binary accessing sensitive APIs (BitBlt, GetDIBits for screenshots; SetWindowsHookEx for keylogging; IAudioCaptureClient for mic access). Monitor for new kernel drivers or DLL injection into explorer.exe, svchost.exe, or dwm.exe.

suggestion.title: Masquerading Update Process from Suspicious Network Origin
suggestion.rationale: Article implies fake updates are indistinguishable to users ('fake updates')—this is masquerading. Pipeline should flag update processes executed with forged digital signatures, mismatched publisher metadata, or served from non-official update CDNs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate digital signatures on all update executables at runtime. Flag processes claiming to be system updates but originating from non-standard paths, launched by network-connected processes, or with code-signing certificates issued by unexpected CAs or with invalid timestamps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Certificate or TLS Traffic During Update Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Man-in-the-middle Wi-Fi hijacking would require SSL/TLS interception or HTTP fallback. Pipeline did not suggest detection for certificate pinning bypass, self-signed update-channel certs, or downgrade attacks from HTTPS to HTTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS connections to update domains with untrusted or self-signed certificates, HTTP-to-HTTPS downgrades in update checks, or repeated certificate validation failures followed by retry on alternative protocols. Correlate with client connecting to non-standard Wi-Fi SSID within 5 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from Surveillance Malware
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware must exfiltrate data; pipeline generated no detection for C2 callbacks, beaconing patterns, or data exfiltration. No mention of monitoring for encoded/obfuscated command channels typical of hotel-targeted spyware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect beaconing patterns from devices post-update: regular outbound connections to uncommon ports (non-80/443), DNS queries for suspicious domains, or data transfer volume spikes to unexpected ASNs. Flag TLS connections to IP ranges hosting known C2 infrastructure or hosting provider bulletproof hosters.

suggestion.title: Failed then successful authorization on same protected endpoint from same source
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'leads to process-wide authorization bypass.' Attacker likely probes protected endpoint (fails 401/403), then after SSPP exploit succeeds, retries same endpoint (gets 200). This two-stage pattern is the smoking gun.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate same source/endpoint pair with HTTP 401/403 followed by HTTP 200 within 2–5 minutes. Verify user field changes from authenticated to unauthenticated between attempts. High confidence if endpoint is known-protected (e.g., /api/v1/@apostrophecms/admin-*).

suggestion.title: Multiple PATCH attempts to same piece-type endpoint with $pullAll variations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '$pullAll patch operator' as exploit vector. Attacker likely iterates on payload syntax ($pullAll with different __proto__ paths, constructor chains) until one succeeds. Rapid-fire PATCHes indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sources issuing >3 PATCH requests to same ApostropheCMS piece-type API within 60 seconds, with request bodies containing `$pullAll` and `__proto__`. Threshold accounts for legitimate batch operations but catches automated exploitation tooling.

suggestion.title: Prototype pollution side-effect: unexpected property access in application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as writing 'arbitrary values to Object.prototype.' This causes unusual permission/property errors in Node.js runtime. Look for error logs indicating prototype chain corruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Node.js/ApostropheCMS application error logs for patterns like 'Cannot set property [__proto__/constructor/prototype]', unexpected permission denials on built-in objects, or 'Object.prototype is not [expected type]'. These indicate successful SSPP mutation.

suggestion.title: Data read-access to protected resources immediately after PATCH to piece-type API
suggestion.rationale: The exploit chain: (1) PATCH with __proto__ pollution → (2) authorization bypass → (3) attacker can now read/write protected data. Detect GET/POST to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/[user|global|admin]/* from unauthenticated source within 1–2 minutes of PATCH.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PATCH to ApostropheCMS API with subsequent GET requests to protected endpoints (user, global, admin) from same source as unauthenticated. Measure data volume to detect bulk exfiltration.

suggestion.title: HTTP 500 errors during PATCH attempts before subsequent auth bypass success
suggestion.rationale: Malformed __proto__ payloads may cause server errors (500) before attacker crafts correct syntax. Sequence of 500 → success suggests iterative exploitation and final breakthrough.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sources that issue PATCH to ApostropheCMS APIs with HTTP 500 responses, followed within 5 minutes by successful (200) GET requests to protected endpoints as unauthenticated user. 500→200 pattern + endpoint type change = exploitation + bypass.

suggestion.title: Authenticated user PATCH followed by different source performing unauthenticated access
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may use stolen credentials to exploit (PATCH from one IP), then access from different IP to avoid detection. Prototype pollution is process-wide, so exploit and abuse can be from different sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH from authenticated user (e.g., editor account) to ApostropheCMS piece-type API, followed by HTTP 200 on protected endpoints from a different source with unauthenticated user field, within 10 minutes. Suggests attacker stole editor credentials, exploited, then accessed from separate C2.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll Targeting AppVShNotify.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states NightLedger 'masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is a core attack mechanism with high specificity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AppVShNotify.exe loading SspiCli.dll from unexpected paths (non-system), especially following process creation from spear-phishing artifacts or post-compromise activities. RPCRT4.dll delay-loading behavior is a secondary indicator.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneler Command & Control - ArcBridge / BridgeHead
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two custom WebSocket-based tunneling tools deployed by Mirage Kitten for 'covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling.' Clear C2 channel distinct from typical HTTP proxies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for non-browser processes initiating WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) to anomalous endpoints, particularly post-exploitation. Correlate with tunneling tool artifacts and network persistence patterns.

suggestion.title: Recruitment-Themed Spear-Phishing with Lookalike Videoconferencing Redirects
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.' Specific social-engineering lure pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment or hiring platform branding, shortened URLs redirecting to file-sharing domains (Google Drive, OneDrive, Mega), and archives with mismatched file extensions. Correlate with phishing-lure infrastructure pattern of lookalike videoconferencing sites.

suggestion.title: Process Discovery and Screenshot Capture by NightLedger
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists NightLedger capabilities: 'process discovery, and screenshot capture.' These are telltale reconnaissance activities for lateral movement and data exfiltration planning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process enumeration APIs (CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, EnumProcesses) and screenshot capture libraries (GDI+, DirectX) execution within seconds of DLL hijacking or post-exploitation indicators. Correlate with file writes to suspicious temp locations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Tunneler Deployment in Aerospace/Aviation Organizations
suggestion.rationale: Article states BridgeHead 'being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.' Indicates secondary-stage deployment pattern after successful initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In aerospace/aviation networks, correlate BridgeHead deployment (WebSocket tunneler executables, configuration files) with prior spear-phishing delivery and DLL hijacking events within 24-72 hours. Monitor for tunneler binaries staged in temp directories or admin shares.

suggestion.title: RPCRT4.dll Delay-Loading SspiCli.dll for Execution Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article explains technical mechanism: 'AppVShNotify.exe...imports RPCRT4.dll, which can delay-load SspiCli.dll when it invokes an RPC API.' This indirect loading pattern evades static-analysis detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AppVShNotify.exe → RPCRT4.dll → SspiCli.dll load chains where SspiCli.dll originates from non-system paths. Pair with behavioral analysis of RPC API calls that trigger delay-load to distinguish legitimate from malicious chains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable FMC Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center as the affected product; federal patch due 2026-08-01 makes this immediately actionable for asset inventory validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Cisco FMC instance with version ≤ patched version in vulnerability scanner output. Cross-reference against network segmentation rules to identify public-facing instances at highest risk.

suggestion.title: FMC Successful Authentication from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account'—auth success from non-standard sources (external IPs, off-hours) should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface (typically port 443) for successful logins with low-privileged accounts from external networks or after hours. Hard-coded credentials create consistent auth patterns; anomalies in source geography/timing are high-confidence signals.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Export or Query Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' once authenticated—monitor for data collection activity from FMC console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC auth, watch for bulk exports, scheduled reports, or API queries for firewall rules, policy configurations, or logged traffic data. Hard-coded credential exploitation often precedes mass data pulls within minutes of access.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Account Credential Reuse Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credentials in FMC create repeatable auth signatures—same username/password from multiple sources or repeated failed attempts before success suggest automated exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed then successful FMC logins using identical credentials from different source IPs within short time windows. Hard-coded password exploitation often includes scanner or script retries before successful access.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Changes by Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated via hard-coded low-privileged account, attacker may modify firewall rules, disable logging, or create backdoor accounts—untypical for low-priv role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag config modifications (rules, access lists, authentication settings) performed by low-privileged FMC accounts, especially new account creation or privilege elevation attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' — implies FMC is reachable from internet. Pipeline missed asset-exposure detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances accessible from untrusted networks. Query for open TCP ports 443/8305/8307, TLS certificate issuer matching Cisco, or HTTP responses containing 'Firepower' or 'Secure Firewall' banner strings. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 patch status from vulnerability scanner.

suggestion.title: Authentication Attempts Using Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'hard-coded password' enables login without valid credentials. Pipeline failed to surface credential-use detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC login endpoints for authentication attempts using hardcoded or default account names (if disclosed). Flag successful logins from anonymous/untrusted networks or IP ranges outside known administrative CIDR blocks. Correlate with failed attempts to detect brute-force patterns.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Low-Privilege FMC Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data' — post-compromise data collection. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for queries, exports, or API calls from low-privilege accounts accessing firewall policies, threat feeds, device configurations, or VPN user lists. Baseline expected behavior per role and alert on bulk exports, geographic anomalies, or access to objects unrelated to the account's known function.

suggestion.title: Failed Login Attempts Against Cisco FMC Hardcoded Account
suggestion.rationale: Attackers will brute-force the hardcoded account. Article: 'unauthenticated' attackers attempting remote authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts against Cisco FMC targeting hardcoded or default service accounts (if name/pattern disclosed). Use sliding-window threshold (e.g. >10 failures in 5 min) and correlate with source IP geolocation, user-agent anomalies, and time-of-day deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Database Export
suggestion.rationale: Successful compromise of FMC enables exfiltration of policies, threat intelligence, and deployment topology. Article: 'access to sensitive data within impacted systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large outbound transfers from Cisco FMC (>50 MB/min) to non-whitelisted external IP addresses, especially database dumps, policy XML exports, or threat-feed snapshots. Monitor for successful database backup operations initiated by low-privilege accounts outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entry means active exploitation in wild; canonical hunt is scanner correlation. 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scan output (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) for CVE-2026-20316 across all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Flag any system marked as vulnerable, unpatched, or not scanned in past 30 days.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Access to Cisco FMC — Hard-Coded Password Login
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hard-coded password allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to affected device.' Requires detection of successful authentication using the known credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from external/untrusted IP ranges using the hard-coded low-privileged account. Baseline normal FMC access patterns by source IP, geography, and time-of-day to detect anomalies.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Access from Internet-Routable IPs
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password is remotely exploitable; article implies FMC exposure. 'Unauthenticated, remote attacker' requires network reachability check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC default management ports (TCP 8305, HTTPS 443) accessible from external IP addresses. Flag any FMC instance reachable from the internet without VPN/bastion host mediation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Configuration Changes via FMC Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated via hard-coded password, attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Expect firewall policy changes, rule modifications, or logging disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for policy modifications, rule creation, logging disablement, or backup/export operations initiated by low-privileged accounts during off-hours or from unusual IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Compromised FMC Pushing Rogue Firewall Rules
suggestion.rationale: Article describes access to 'impacted systems' (plural) via management appliance. Compromised FMC can weaponize firewall configurations to enable exfil or maintain persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate firewall configuration pushes from FMC with unexpected allow rules for rare destination ports/protocols, unusual DNS redirects, or outbound traffic to attacker-controlled IPs. Look for firewall rules that bypass normal security zones.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attempts Against Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password creates low-volume attack surface; article threat profile describes active exploitation. Attackers testing the known credential will generate failed auth attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed authentication attempts to FMC management interfaces (>5 failures in 10 min) from a single source IP, especially if followed by a successful login using the hard-coded credential.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Detection of successful authentication using known hard-coded credentials is the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC logins using hard-coded account names associated with CVE-2026-20316. Baseline typical administrative login patterns (time, source IP, frequency); trigger on access outside baseline, especially from untrusted ASNs or at off-hours.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies internet-facing FMC. Asset discovery hunt required to locate all exposed instances prior to 2026-08-01 federal deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and network discovery tools for Cisco FMC instances reachable on standard management ports (443, 8305) from internet-routable IP space. Cross-reference against patch inventory; flag all instances regardless of patch status (CISA KEV = active exploitation).

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Once authenticated via hard-coded credential, monitor for abnormal data exports, policy downloads, or configuration exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk exports or downloads of firewall rules, threat intelligence, user/asset databases, or device configurations from low-privileged FMC accounts. Alert on exports to unexpected destinations or during off-hours. Correlate with hard-coded credential authentication detections.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scan Match and Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation requires federal remediation by 2026-08-01. Automated scanner detection and compliance reporting is mandatory procedural control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute active scans for CVE-2026-20316 against all Cisco FMC instances. Maintain compliance dashboard tracking patch status per asset against 2026-08-01 deadline. Flag all vulnerable or unverified instances as critical priority regardless of perceived exploitability.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Access Pattern to FMC Management Plane
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential compromise typically manifests as access from atypical geography, ASN, or time-of-day. Article implies rapid attacker pivot once credentials are known.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for FMC management access (source IP/ASN, geolocation, time-of-access patterns). Alert on significant deviations—access from residential IP ranges, different continent, or outside business hours. Weight alerts higher if occurring within 72 hours of CISA KEV publication (2026-07-29).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20316' requires federal remediation. Pipeline should generate baseline asset-exposure use case per template logic but failed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-20316 on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center. Cross-correlate with network exposure data for FMC management ports (TCP/443, TCP/8305) accessible from untrusted networks to identify at-risk assets before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication Using Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' leveraging 'hard-coded password.' Pipeline should detect credential-based access patterns but generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful remote logins from non-administrative sources using default or low-privileged service account names. Detect rapid failed login attempts followed by successful authentication (brute force then successful access pattern).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could allow...access [to] sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for post-exploitation data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Cisco FMC audit/access logs for bulk queries, policy exports, intelligence data downloads, or sensitive configuration access immediately following remote authentication from anomalous sources. Alert on data retrieval operations from newly-compromised sessions.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' but pipeline generated zero hunts for exposed FMC instances despite federal agencies being required to remediate by federal due-date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management interfaces reachable from untrusted networks. Query firewall/NSM for inbound rules permitting external traffic to FMC administrative ports. Cross-reference DNS records, SSL certificates, and shodan/censys external scanning data for exposed FMC instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Exposure and Access (CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can 'log in to an affected device' via management interface. Canonical asset-exposure hunt should match CVE-2026-20316 across vulnerability scanner output and network telemetry for exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound network connections to Cisco FMC management ports (typically TCP 443) from untrusted sources. Correlate against CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner hits. Establish baseline of legitimate administrative source IPs and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'use of hard-coded password' enabling 'low-privileged account' access. Should hunt failed/successful authentication to FMC using known hard-coded service account names or brute-force patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded account identifiers. Flag repeated failed authentications from single source (credential-guessing), or successful logins from geographic/network anomalies inconsistent with administrative patterns.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FMC Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Should detect unusual query patterns, data exports, or API calls from low-privileged FMC accounts post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls, database queries, or bulk exports initiated by low-privileged FMC accounts targeting sensitive configuration, threat intelligence, or network policy data. Alert on unusual volume or scope of data access requests from automated or non-administrative contexts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states unauthenticated remote attacker can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — implies hard-coded or default credential abuse. Pipeline missed detection for authentication events with known weak/default credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC and related devices for failed and successful authentication attempts using documented default or hard-coded service account credentials. Flag any login from unexpected source IPs, outside business hours, or followed by lateral movement attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Public-Facing Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20316 requires network access to management interface. Article classifies as T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application), implying asset is discoverable on internet. Pipeline must emit asset exposure/inventory verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances across enterprise. Cross-reference with public IP space and shodan/censys lookups. Alert on any FMC bound to 0.0.0.0 or publicly routable IP without restrictive ACLs. Track patch versions against CVSS timeline.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Unauthorized Access to Sensitive Data
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns of 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-authentication. Pipeline omitted detection for data exfiltration or unusual data access patterns post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit and access logs for low-privileged account queries or exports of sensitive policy objects, rules, or configuration data immediately following authentication. Correlate with known CVE-2026-20316 exploitation indicators (failed auths, new sessions from untrusted sources).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal due date 2026-08-01 requires patch validation. Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline must generate compliance hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference against published patch version thresholds for CVE-2026-20316. Flag any instance running affected versions as critical/overdue remediation. Correlate scan dates with deployment timeline to identify patch lag.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Lateral Movement Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credentials grant access to a management appliance controlling firewall policies—natural pivot point for lateral movement. Pipeline missed detection for policy changes or reconnaissance from FMC context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, FMC provides centralized control plane access. Monitor for administrative actions (policy changes, rule modifications, rule disablement) originating from FMC after hard-coded credential authentication. Flag deployments of new policies or mass rule deletions.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-20316'. Pipeline should have generated this primary detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances in vulnerability management and asset inventory systems. Correlate with scanner data to find systems vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize internet-facing FMC instances and flag those unpatched past the federal due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'. This authentication mechanism needs detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded account names with default credentials. Detect low-privileged account authentications from external IP sources combined with subsequent access to system functions or data export features.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Post-authentication data access and exfiltration should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual data retrieval patterns from Cisco FMC by low-privileged or newly-authenticated accounts: policy exports, configuration downloads, or large data transfers to external IPs on non-standard ports. Establish baseline of normal FMC data access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public-Facing Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms 'observed exploited in the wild'. Article emphasizes this is currently active exploitation requiring immediate threat hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation patterns against Cisco FMC: rapid sequential authentication attempts from single source IP, requests to FMC default HTTPS ports (8305+) with specific payload patterns, and failed-to-successful login transitions. Cross-correlate with network telemetry for exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration or Policy Export by Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'access sensitive data'. FMC policy databases are high-value targets. Monitor for unauthorized configuration exports as collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privileged account access to policy viewing, rule export, or configuration backup functions within Cisco FMC. Flag sequences of: authentication → navigation to sensitive features → export/download attempts, especially within hours of initial access.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploiting public-facing FMC (T1190) and explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunt from template. Pipeline extracted no detection despite direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances accessible from internet-facing networks. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner results. Alert on exposure of unpatched versions post-disclosure (2026-07-29).

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Exploitation: Default Account Login
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hard-coded password' and 'log in using a low-privileged account'—direct credential access attack. Pipeline missed T1078.001 entirely despite straightforward attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management console for successful authentication using low-privileged or default accounts from non-internal source IPs. Alert on logins post-vulnerability disclosure or from internet-routable addresses.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Sensitive Data Access from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Pipeline generated no detection for data reconnaissance or exfiltration from management plane.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC authentication, monitor for data extraction: configuration/policy file access, network topology queries, security rule enumeration, or bulk export operations. Flag unusual access patterns inconsistent with baseline admin activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Remediation Tracking & Federal Compliance Timeline
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designates active exploitation; federal due-date is 2026-08-01. Pipeline should correlate patch status with exploit timeline and compliance deadlines but generated no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Cisco FMC instances and track CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Alert on unpatched instances detected after KEV publication (2026-07-29). Escalate against federal remediation deadline (2026-08-01) for compliance.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Failed authentication attempts from external networks
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploiting hard-coded password. Brute force or credential-spray attempts against the management interface are the obvious attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC management interface (TCP 443) from external IP ranges within a short time window. Baseline normal admin access by geography/time and flag anomalies. Combine with known hard-coded account names if available.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Successful authentication using default/hard-coded credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hard-coded password as the vulnerability. Any successful login using known default account names or weak credentials tied to this CVE is a direct compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful authentication events to FMC using known default usernames (e.g., admin, cisco) or credential pairs associated with CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with active CVSS/KEV feeds to maintain current credential lists.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive data access post-authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-auth data queries, exports, or API calls warrant alerting to detect post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a successful login (especially from unusual source), trigger on bulk data queries, configuration exports, user/credential dumps, or API calls exfiltrating policies, rules, or sensor configurations. Establish baseline for legitimate admin activity and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Lateral movement from compromised management center
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded access to FMC is a gateway to downstream sensor and firewall management. Article implies 'low-privileged' initial access, but FMC access enables broader network control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FMC-initiated connections to managed firewalls/sensors immediately after a suspicious authentication. Flag policy pushes, rule modifications, or sensor reconfigurations that deviate from change control logs or after-hours admin windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-20316 is primary tracking identifier and must be matched against vulnerability scanner. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20316 matches against Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Flag any vulnerable systems with network exposure to untrusted networks or internet.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco FMC Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1190 exploitation of public-facing application; FMC defaults to HTTPS 443 and administrative port 8305. Pipeline did not establish initial-access detection for asset exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound connections to Cisco FMC standard ports (443, 8305) from untrusted networks. Correlate with reverse DNS / service fingerprinting to confirm FMC service presence on exposed assets.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication to FMC Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions hard-coded password as attack vector and unauthenticated remote access. Pipeline did not map credential-access or brute-force attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC admin interface logs for repeated failed login attempts followed by successful authentication. Baseline known-good admin credentials and flag anomalous patterns; hard-coded credentials often show non-human timing or source-IP patterns.

suggestion.title: Successful FMC Login via Hard-Coded or Default Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'; hard-coded password implies credential stuffing or known weak account. Pipeline missed credential-based post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to FMC from unusual geographies, non-admin IP ranges, or IPs not in administrative baseline. Correlate with scanner detection of CVE-2026-20316 to confirm exploited asset.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states objective is to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline did not establish data-exfiltration or discovery indicators for post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC authentication, monitor for unusual data queries, policy exports, certificate extraction, or user-credential dumps. Hard-coded-password compromises often lead to lateral-movement reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Patch Lag on Cisco FMC Fleet
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due-date is 2026-08-01. Pipeline did not establish compliance or patch-status use case despite explicit advisory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all Cisco FMC instances in your environment against the CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Flag any systems still running vulnerable versions post–2026-08-01 due date; prioritize exposed instances for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — this is the direct exploitation vector and deserves frontline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for login attempts using default/hardcoded credential patterns. Alert on successful logins from public-routable IPs, especially during off-hours. Correlate with vulnerability scanner CVE-2026-20316 detections on the same host.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privileged Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — need detection for unauthorized data reads/exports by constrained privilege levels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when low-privileged accounts on Cisco FMC perform administrative-level data access, configuration exports, or sensitive file reads. Establish baseline for account privilege levels and flag anomalous access to config/credential storage paths.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Firewall Management Center Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'unauthenticated, remote' per article — requires internet-facing exposure. Asset exposure hunt is mandatory pre-requisite for this CVE risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center / Firepower Management Center instances with public IP addresses or internet-routable DNS records. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize instances with recent scan dates.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline template references CVE-substitution for asset-exposure hunt; federal remediation deadline is 2026-08-01 (one day from article publish) — scanner baseline is the critical compliance hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate all vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-20316 or product='Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center'. Flag any 'not vulnerable' results for manual re-verification; patch lag is high-risk. Cross-correlate with network access logs to confirm scan reachability.

suggestion.title: FMC Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access to exposed FMC instances. Requires detection of reachable FMC (typically TCP/8305) on untrusted networks as initial entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to TCP/8305 from external networks. Baseline legitimate administrative access; flag anomalous source IPs, unexpected geographies, or sustained connection attempts indicating attacker reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly prescribes 'match against your vulnerability scanner' as primary hunt method. Scanner-based detection is mandatory for CISA KEV assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner reports for FMC instances flagged with CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with network-exposed instances (externally routable TCP/8305) and patch dates; prioritize systems exceeding federal due-date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Account Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromise via 'low-privileged account' with 'hard-coded password.' Successful or repeated failed logins with default credentials indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful SSH/HTTPS authentication to FMC from external sources using default account names, or failed-login bursts preceding success (spray patterns). Alert on external-origin authentication spikes; baseline legitimate administrative access.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FMC Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise allows 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Indicates attacker enumeration of device configs, policies, or credentials post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk device-inventory queries, policy exports, or credential lookups shortly after successful external authentication. Alert on data-export volume anomalies or unusual queries from low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Malicious Policy Push from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC enables direct policy deployment to all managed firewalls, permitting attacker to disable logging, modify rules, or exfiltrate traffic—high-impact post-compromise action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate policy-push events from FMC to managed devices with timestamps of suspicious account access. Alert on policy changes that disable security logging, widen inbound access, or remove IDS/IPS rules—especially unscheduled changes post-compromise window.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Attackers Exploit Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator Command Injection Flaw'—indicates CVE-level exploitation with no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator endpoints for malformed HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), `) in query parameters or POST bodies targeting known vulnerable API paths. Baseline: VeloCloud APIs should not receive raw command constructs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from VeloCloud Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Command injection implies code execution; article mentions 'attackers exploit' but pipeline provided no detection for the execution phase triggered by injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by VeloCloud controller/orchestrator processes (e.g., velocloud_orch, orchestrator daemon). Establish baseline of legitimate child processes; flag bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe when spawned by non-shell parent processes.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Outbound Command-and-Control
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation activity typically involves C2 callbacks; article does not specify infrastructure but is critical for defenders to detect egress to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections originating from VeloCloud Orchestrator to non-Arista, non-enterprise-approved external IP ranges. Flag domains registered recently or with low reputation scores. Correlate with process execution events on orchestrator hosts.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Config or Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Command injection on orchestrator platform likely targets sensitive config files or stored credentials; no use case addresses data collection or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of VeloCloud configuration files (/etc/velocloud/*, registry paths, database files) or credential stores by unexpected processes. Flag file transfers of config blobs to external destinations (FTP, SMB, HTTP PUT).

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Persistence via Cron or Scheduled Task Injection
suggestion.rationale: Command injection enables persistence establishment; no detection rule for post-exploitation persistence mechanisms was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cron/crontab additions, systemd service file modifications, or Windows scheduled task creation triggered by VeloCloud processes. Alert if new tasks contain shell invocations or disable security software.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Successful Authentication with Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—detection must flag successful authentication using known hard-coded/default credentials against exposed FMC interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface (typically port 443 HTTPS) for successful authentication events. Alert when low-privileged account logins originate from external IPs or occur at suspicious times. Correlate with failed attempts to detect credential-stuffing or hard-coded password brute-force patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Configuration Access by Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via low-privileged account—detection must identify unauthorized configuration or credential store access following authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of which data/config objects low-privileged FMC users should access. Alert on queries or exports of administrative settings, device credentials, access control lists, or crypto keys by unexpected accounts. Flag rapid sequential access to sensitive objects post-login.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Vulnerability Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal remediation deadline (2026-08-01) and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—detection must identify unpatched FMC versions in your environment vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run Cisco vulnerability scanner (e.g., Cisco Security Advisory) or CVSS/NVD feeds targeting CVE-2026-20316. Match any Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instance to unpatched version ranges. Escalate findings for systems not remediated by federal due date or organization's own SLA.

suggestion.title: FMC Remote Management Interface Access from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' accessing FMC externally—detection must flag anomalous source IPs/geolocations attempting connection to management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate FMC management sources (admin jump hosts, SOC IPs). Alert on connection attempts from residential ISPs, VPNs, Tor exit nodes, or geographic regions inconsistent with your admin footprint. Combine with high-frequency failed-auth patterns to detect exploitation scanning.

suggestion.title: FMC Account Creation or Privilege Escalation Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Attack narrative enables low-privileged access; attackers often follow with lateral escalation—detection must catch account/privilege changes by newly-authenticated users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful low-privileged account authentication (especially from external sources) with subsequent user management events: new account creation, role/permission changes, or administrative group membership additions. Flag same-session or near-immediate privilege-escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Failed and Successful FMC Authentication Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential exploits often present as multiple failed attempts followed by success—detection must identify this pattern indicative of credential-guessing or known-secret exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous login-attempt patterns: >5 failed attempts to FMC within 5 minutes followed by successful authentication (same or different account) from the same source IP. Track per-source-IP to identify systematic exploitation attempts, and correlate with external scanning to confirm CVE-2026-20316 targeting.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Hard-coded Credential Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—core attack vector requires detection of successful authentication using the compromised low-privileged built-in account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using low-privileged default accounts from untrusted or internet sources. Alert on any successful auth to internet-exposed FMC from unexpected geographic origins. Baseline expected administrative access to filter noise.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Internet Asset Exposure for Active Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implying internet reachability. Article template explicitly mentions 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as required for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances and flag those with internet-routable IPs or exposed management ports (443 typical). Cross-reference against external scanning data. Alert on newly discovered FMC instances appearing in public-facing asset inventories.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Data Access by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-exploitation phase must detect unauthorized data collection via the low-privileged account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for unusual data access patterns by low-privileged accounts, especially to firewall policies, threat intelligence feeds, or system configs. Alert on deviation from baseline access for that account role. Correlate with initial access alerts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due-date 2026-08-01. Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'—scanner-based detection essential even for systems claiming patches are applied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20316 across Cisco FMC fleet. Cross-validate scanner results against patch records to catch false negatives. Flag all vulnerable instances; prioritize internet-exposed systems. Track remediation against federal due-date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Status Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal patch due 2026-08-01 and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Standard asset-exposure hunt per _TEMPLATES for CVE-2026-20316.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset DB for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances; cross-reference with patch management system. Flag any instance running unpatched version. Escalate to leadership for federal compliance tracking (due 2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication from Unexpected Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Any successful authentication to FMC is suspicious; baseline expected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC from IPs not in corporate whitelist, geographic anomalies, or known malicious sources. Hard-coded credential exploitation typically originates from public scanning infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article core issue: 'hard-coded password vulnerability.' Monitor for attempts to use known hard-coded or default Cisco FMC credentials extracted from CVE details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication attempts using Cisco FMC system or default accounts. If CVE details expose specific credential pairs, alert on login attempts with those usernames. Correlate repeated failed attempts with successful bypass.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Data Export from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' via low-privileged account. Monitor data queries and exports by non-administrative users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data export, API calls, or policy queries initiated by low-privileged FMC accounts. Baseline normal export volume and frequency; flag spikes or exports of security policies, firewall rules, threat intelligence, or configuration data.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Scan & Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies accessible management port (443 or 8305). Monitor for scanning and exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume connection attempts to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) from unexpected sources. Correlate scanning activity with subsequent authentication events. Flag any source IP that scans then successfully authenticates.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Account Persistence via FMC
suggestion.rationale: After hard-coded credential access, attacker may create new accounts or modify group membership for persistence and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for user account creation, group assignment changes, or privilege modifications performed by low-privileged accounts or shortly after suspicious authentication events. Flag any administrative action from a non-admin context.

suggestion.title: FMC Unauthenticated Remote Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit the management interface. This is explicit initial access; Cisco FMC access logs record source IP, timestamp, and success/failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface ports (443/tcp, 8305/tcp) for successful remote login from non-sanctioned source networks. Baseline and alert on successful access from unexpected geolocations, non-business-hours logins, or access from residential/datacenter IP ranges. Correlate source IP against network asset inventory to identify unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Default Account Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions hard-coded password vulnerability enabling access via 'low-privileged account.' This is credential-reuse at scale once attacker obtains the credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any login attempt using the hard-coded credential (once identified via vulnerability research) from source IPs outside corporate networks. Additionally, baseline legitimate low-privilege account usage patterns in FMC; detect anomalous logins (time-of-day, geolocation, volume) on these accounts, which may indicate credential compromise.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Configuration Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC contains security policies, threat intelligence, network topology. Exfiltration should be detected post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create baseline of policy/config access patterns by role and time-of-day. Alert on bulk exports or downloads of threat rules, network policies, or asset lists by low-privilege accounts, from unusual source IPs, or outside business hours. Monitor for unusually large data transfers from FMC to external or cloud endpoints.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Cisco FMC Instance Identification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires public-facing exposure ('public-facing application'). This is reconnaissance/pre-exploitation. Recommend immediate inventory of all FMC instances and network exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and firewall rule databases for Cisco FMC instances with inbound WAN/internet access to management ports. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Alert on any FMC instance identified as both exposed and unpatched, prioritize for emergency patching.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status mandates proactive hunt. Query all vulnerability scanners for Cisco FMC instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 via version identification or banner grab.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cisco FMC instances (via SSH, SNMP, or HTTP banner grabbing on ports 443/8305) for version numbers matching CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable range. Cross-reference with patch deployment records. Alert on instances vulnerable + exposed to untrusted networks + unpatched as of patch due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via 'hard-coded password vulnerability'—the exploit path is the hard-coded credential itself, not just network access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface logs (typically ports 443, 8305) for successful authentication using default/low-privilege account names (e.g., 'admin', 'readonly') from external IP ranges during unusual hours. Baseline normal FMC login patterns by region/admin and alert on anomalous access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—no detection logic provided for data collection phase, which is the impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk export/backup operations on FMC (configuration downloads, policy rule exports, device inventory dumps). Alert on unusual volume or destination IP for data transfers from FMC to external networks, especially outbound to non-corporate CIDR blocks.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of 'remote' access to 'affected device'—reconnaissance of FMC version/status is a prerequisite. Pipeline missed version enumeration technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to FMC management interface (e.g., /admin, /api/version, /.well-known endpoints) that probe for version info, product identification, or login pages from non-whitelisted IPs. Flag high-velocity probe patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management console; article does not state scope but compromise could enable attacker to push malicious policies or commands to connected firewalls. Missing entire post-compromise lateral movement vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC-to-managed-firewall communication for unusual policy pushes, configuration changes, or command execution originating from compromise window. Baseline normal policy update cadence and alert on deviations correlated with unauthorized FMC access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Privilege Escalation from Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' as entry point—implies attacker must escalate to admin or sensitive data roles. No detection for in-console privilege escalation attempts or lateral escalation within FMC role hierarchy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for privilege escalation attempts (role changes, group assignments, permission grants) initiated from low-privilege accounts, especially during the exploitation window (post-2026-07-29). Alert on successful role promotions to admin within minutes of initial login.

suggestion.title: FMC Default/Hard-Coded Account Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article imples existence of hard-coded credentials; no detection for attacker discovery of which account names are active or exploitable on target FMC instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on brute-force or dictionary attacks against FMC login endpoints (>5 failed logins in 60 sec, attempt patterns matching known default usernames). Correlate with vulnerability scanning or exploitation tool traffic signatures.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Manipulation on Widely-Depended Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the core attack vector enabling the compromise to 23,000 downstream repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories with 100+ external dependencies for tag creation/modification events where the tag moves to a commit not on the main branch or moves backwards in history. Trigger alert if tag modified by account with no recent commit history in that repository.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets Exposed in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states the attack 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs' and details how secrets 'appear in the build log' despite GitHub's encryption. This is the direct impact method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for regex patterns matching common secret formats (AWS_KEY patterns, JWT tokens, API keys, GitHub PATs, etc.). Cross-reference against declared GitHub secrets to identify unexpected plaintext leakage. Alert on matches in public repositories.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Egress Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' External C2 or payload fetch is a key IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions runner network egress for unexpected HTTPS/HTTP calls to non-GitHub domains. Flag calls to dynamic DNS, short-lived domains, or IP ranges known for C2. Baseline expected domains per organization and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commits in High-Value Git Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explains orphaned commits as a key obfuscation technique: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext' via 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches.' Orphaned commits are rare in normal development.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically run `git fsck --full` or query GitHub API for unreachable commits in repositories with high external dependence. Alert on new orphaned commits created by accounts that do not regularly work in main/develop branches. Cross-reference with tag manipulation events.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Access Granted to Supply-Chain Critical Projects
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on' as the prerequisite for the entire attack. Unusual write permission grant is the initial pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new write/admin access grants to repositories with 1000+ external dependencies or high GitHub Stars. Implement peer-review requirement for permission changes on critical projects. Flag grants to inactive or recently-created accounts.

suggestion.title: Release Tag Pointing to Non-Main-Branch Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates that tags can point to orphaned/arbitrary commits: 'GitHub tags are just convenient strings pointing to a particular commit.' Abnormal tag targets bypass branch protection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each release tag in a repository, verify the tagged commit exists on main or a tracked release branch. Alert if a tag moves to a commit with no branch ancestry or if the tag's target commit changes (tag repoint). Use `git log <tag> --not main` to detect off-branch tags.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication — Hard-coded Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' No detection UC for suspicious FMC login patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected sources or rapid authentication attempts. Correlation of failed+successful login pairs within short windows may indicate hard-coded credential exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposure — Asset Enumeration and Port Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed' FMC systems are targets; article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' No detection for identifying or monitoring FMC asset exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanners against network asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances running unpatched builds. Flag externally-routable FMC instances (port 443, admin GUI). Compare against baseline to detect new exposures post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access — Suspicious Collection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No detection for abnormal data access, export, or exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit/API logs for unusual data queries, policy exports, rule extractions, or sensor configuration downloads from low-privileged accounts. Flag rapid sequential reads of firewall rules, sensor configs, or threat intelligence.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement — FMC as Pivot Point
suggestion.rationale: Article implies FMC compromise grants 'access to sensitive data.' Compromised management console is often used for lateral movement into managed sensors/firewalls. No lateral-movement detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FMC-initiated connection attempts or commands to managed sensors/firewalls that deviate from administrative baseline. Flag unusual sensor queries, rule pushes, or policy changes originating from FMC after a compromise window.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Authentication Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device' — detection must monitor authentication to FMC, especially from unexpected origins or with known hard-coded account identifiers.
