suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center login events for successful authentications from untrusted IP ranges, multiple failed attempts preceding success (credential spray), or logins using known hard-coded account names. Baseline legitimate administrative source IPs.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — detection must capture FMC configuration exports, policy downloads, or database queries by compromised low-privileged accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk exports, configuration backups, or policy file downloads initiated by low-privileged accounts or system service accounts. Flag unusual API queries against FMC databases or config dumps to external destinations.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration or Policy Tampering
suggestion.rationale: A compromised management center (via hard-coded creds) becomes a pivot point to alter firewall rules — article does not restrict impact to read-only access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline authorized FMC configuration change actors and flag unauthorized policy deployments or rule modifications. Alert on disabling security controls, adding allow rules for restricted ports, or modifying access control lists from unexpected accounts.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploited only if FMC management interface is reachable remotely; article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker.' Asset discovery must identify exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center deployments. Cross-check for internet accessibility on TCP 443/8305 using external port scanners or VPN-less access logs. Flag FMC instances without network segmentation or IP whitelisting.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage in Authentication Logs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism explicitly 'use of hard-coded password' — detection should surface authentication attempts using known Cisco Secure Firewall hard-coded account names or patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication attempts for known Cisco Secure Firewall hard-coded account identifiers (e.g., default admin or service accounts documented in CVE details). Correlate with threat intelligence feeds for exploitation signatures and known attacker IP ranges.

suggestion.title: FMC REST API Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: FMC exposes management API; 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' scenario is consistent with credential-based or default-credential API abuse on management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API endpoints (e.g., /api/fmc_config/v1) for successful requests from unexpected source IPs, automated scanning patterns, or API tokens tied to low-privilege service accounts. Flag token reuse across multiple source IPs within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Login via Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can log in 'using a low-privileged account' remotely and unauthenticated. Pipeline missed the initial-access foothold: authentication attempts with or without the hardcoded credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC admin/management-interface logins from unexpected external networks. Baseline normal access IPs and flag logins from new sources, especially if preceded by multiple failed auth attempts or at off-hours.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline should surface credential-access detections: payload fingerprints, known-credential stuffing patterns, or authentication-bypass signatures specific to this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20316 exploit patterns (malformed auth headers, bypass payloads in parameters). Flag repeated auth failures immediately followed by success from same source IP. Alert on credential-reuse patterns or automated scanning tools targeting /admin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline missed post-exploitation collection phase: audit logs, config export, rule enumeration, or credential-store access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a successful FMC login, detect anomalous data-access patterns: export of firewall policies, access to stored credentials, bulk rule/config downloads, or database queries from accounts that don't routinely perform those actions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Affected Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)' as the vulnerable product. Pipeline must identify all FMC instances in the environment and cross-reference patch status against the published vulnerability range.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database and vuln scanner for Cisco FMC instances. Flag any unpatched, internet-routable, or externally-exposed FMC instances. Compare version numbers to CVE-2026-20316 advisory. Prioritize remediation by network exposure (external-facing > DMZ > internal).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Web Interface Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: CVE is mapped to T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application.' Pipeline should detect web-layer exploitation: malformed requests, path traversal, payload injection, or known Cisco FMC exploit signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC web server logs for exploitation signatures: unusually long URIs, SQL-injection patterns in parameters, repeated 40x responses followed by 200, or requests with known Cisco exploit payloads. Alert on probing activity targeting common FMC endpoints (/admin, /api, /login).

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can reach the service—network exposure is the attack surface. 'Public-facing application' per T1190 mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances responding on standard ports (443, 8305, 8307) from untrusted networks. Correlate with scanner fingerprinting (FMC version in HTTP headers, SSL certificates containing 'Cisco Secure Firewall'). Identify assets in DMZ or external-facing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Login Attempts to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'hard-coded password vulnerability' allows attacker to 'log in'. Article explicitly names this as the exploitation method, not code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login events with known hard-coded vendor defaults. Detect both failed brute-force patterns (T1110.004) and successful logins (T1078.001) from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with FMC access within 1 hour of first login attempt.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise 'could allow...access to sensitive data'—attacker goal is data extraction, not just system access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC login, hunt for bulk export of device configurations, policy documents, firewall rules, or threat intelligence datasets. Look for large outbound file transfers or API queries returning >1MB of policy/inventory data. Detect tools like curl/wget targeting FMC endpoints post-auth.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Policy Rule Modifications Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: With FMC access, attacker can disable defensive rules or create backdoors. 'Access to sensitive data' includes operational control per implied impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for firewall policy changes, rule additions/deletions, or device policy re-assignments immediately following suspicious FMC login events. Look for ruleset deletions that disable threat detection, or creation of new allow-rules for suspicious IPs. Correlate timestamp of config change with attacker login event.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Default Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account' via hardcoded password; this is the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management authentication logs for attempts using known default credentials or hardcoded account names (admin, cisco, etc.). Alert on successful login following repeated failed attempts, or login from untrusted network segments. Correlate authentication source IP with threat intelligence for known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' to reach management interface; implies FMC exposed on untrusted/internet-facing network segment rather than properly segmented management VLAN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management ports (typically 443/TCP for HTTPS, 8305/TCP) accessible from public internet or untrusted networks. Scan externally-facing IP ranges for FMC management interface banners. Alert on network flows from external ASNs or geographies outside expected administrative footprint to FMC management ports.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access and Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-authentication; monitor for data extraction patterns inconsistent with normal FMC administration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for unusual query patterns, bulk data exports, or configuration downloads. Flag sessions that extract policies, access control lists, threat data, or user databases. Correlate authentication logs with data-access events to identify suspicious sessions where low-privileged accounts query sensitive data repositories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Match and Exposure Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article template explicitly directs scanning for 'CVE: CVE-2026-20316' as the primary IOC; vulnerability scanner findings are foundational indicators of actively-exploitable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner output (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable, Rapid7, etc.) for CVE-2026-20316 findings on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Prioritize findings matching vulnerable product versions per Cisco advisories. Escalate to emergency remediation workflow given CISA KEV federal due date of 2026-08-01; assume active exploitation in-the-wild.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-facing Cisco FMC Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability in 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' context with exposed FMC as attack surface; template itself references _TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure but no asset-hunting use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Cisco FMC instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm patches deployed by federal due-date (2026-08-01). Monitor external IP ranges and public DNS records for Cisco FMC management ports (8305/TCP, 443/TCP) reachable from internet. Use network telemetry to detect inbound connection attempts to FMC from non-corporate IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Credential Access: Hard-coded Password Authentication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' to 'log in'; credential compromise is the attack primitive but no auth-focused detection use case was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins matching known hard-coded credential patterns (default usernames, vendor-documented weak passwords). Flag successful logins by low-privilege service accounts from unexpected geographic regions or at anomalous times. Correlate rapid-fire failed authentication attempts followed by successful low-privilege logon as indicator of hard-coded credential exploitation.

suggestion.title: Data Access: Sensitive Configuration and Audit Log Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow...access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'; post-exploitation data access patterns not captured in any use case despite being the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk export operations, API queries, or database reads targeting sensitive FMC data (firewall policies, device configurations, audit logs, security events) by low-privilege or newly-authenticated accounts. Monitor for automated or scripted data access patterns (high-volume downloads in short time windows). Flag administrative data pulls from accounts lacking historical access to those repositories.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Status Validation: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due-date of 2026-08-01 (3 days); scanner-based compliance and remediation-tracking use case necessary but absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query continuous vulnerability scans for CVE-2026-20316 status across all Cisco FMC deployments. Cross-reference scanner findings with patch-management records to confirm remediation completion. Alert on instances still marked vulnerable as of federal due-date (2026-08-01). Track time-to-patch and flag instances exceeding SLA for regulatory audit trail.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Low-privilege Account Access to Administrative Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'low-privileged account' access; lateral escalation or privilege escalation from low-priv to sensitive functions not mapped to MITRE or detection scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for privilege escalation attempts by accounts designated as low-privilege (readonly, viewer, analyst roles). Detect attempts to access administrative API endpoints, modify policy rules, or export full audit logs by accounts lacking authorization. Flag role-assignment changes or permission grants to compromised low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Script Modifications or Injection via Adform CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that 'hackers poison Adform script' — direct evidence of malicious script injection into a trusted ad-delivery supply chain. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for script-source anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network requests to Adform CDN and detect deviations in script hash, content-length, or response headers. Flag if legitimate advertisement domains begin loading unexpected JavaScript payloads from Adform URLs or if Adform URLs are modified in <script> tags on customer pages.

suggestion.title: Detect Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Replacement in Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites.' No use case exists to catch this form of DOM manipulation or content injection targeting payment addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of cryptocurrency wallet addresses on monitored e-commerce or payment sites. Alert when JavaScript executes document.replace(), innerHTML manipulation, or regex substitution patterns that target hexadecimal addresses matching common cryptocurrency formats (Bitcoin, Ethereum). Correlate wallet address changes with Adform script injection timeline.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply-Chain Script Sources Diverging from Legitimate Publisher Registrations
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploits trust in Adform as legitimate vendor. Pipeline provided no kill-chain entry for supply-chain compromise. Article phrase 'Adform script' implies origin-trust violation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish known-good Adform CDN IPs, ASNs, and certificate subjects. Flag script-serving endpoints that resolve to unexpected geographic regions, autonomous systems, or TLS certificates not issued to Adform or its parent company. Cross-reference with certificate transparency logs for domain registration anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Simultaneous Malicious Script Activity Across Multiple Customer Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'across customer sites' (plural, widespread impact). Pipeline omitted lateral/multi-site correlation detection. A single compromised script affects all downstream subscribers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate script-injection or wallet-replacement detections across all monitored Adform-subscriber domains within a 1-hour window. High-count aggregation (>5 unique customer domains with same malicious pattern in 60 minutes) suggests supply-chain compromise rather than isolated intrusion. Escalate as critical.

suggestion.title: Detect Attacker-Controlled Cryptocurrency Wallet Addresses in Ad-Tech Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is crypto theft via address replacement. Article establishes specific IOC class (malicious wallet addresses) that should be extracted and correlated with web-injection events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain blocklist of known attacker-controlled cryptocurrency wallet addresses from threat intelligence. Detect when any registered Adform customer site references these addresses in payment forms, checkout flows, or donation prompts. Trigger alert on first reference and escalate if address persists after 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Detect Script Execution Performing String Replacement on Page Content
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism is runtime string substitution of wallet addresses. Article implies regex or string-replace operations in malicious script payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hook JavaScript String.prototype.replace() and RegExp execution on pages known to handle cryptocurrency payments or addresses. Alert on patterns matching wallet-address regex (Bitcoin: ^[13][a-km-zA-HJ-NP-Z1-9]{25,34}$, Ethereum: ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$) being replaced with unrecognized values or loaded from unsigned scripts.

suggestion.title: Fake Update Prompt from Compromised Network
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'Hijacked Hotel Wi-Fi Pushes Fake Updates.' Pipeline must detect browser-injected or network-intercepted update dialogs prompting users to install malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual update installation attempts initiated from Wi-Fi network traffic patterns. Flag if update domain resolves to non-canonical WHOIS registrant or IP geolocation mismatches vendor headquarters. Correlate with lateral process creation (msiexec, installer spawning unexpected child processes).

suggestion.title: MITM Attack via Compromised Hotel Wi-Fi Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Wi-Fi hijacking as attack vector. Must detect ARP spoofing, DNS hijacking, or certificate interception patterns typical of MITM on public Wi-Fi.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on certificate authority mismatches or expired certs served by Wi-Fi gateway IP. Detect DNS responses from gateway IP (vs. ISP resolver) for known CDN or update domains. Flag simultaneous connections to multiple victims from same gateway MAC/IP within short time window.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Post-Installation Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is 'surveillance malware.' Must detect screen capture, audio recording, or credential theft post-execution (T1113, T1123, T1056 behaviors).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to screen/audio APIs (BitBlt, GetDC, waveIn*, AUDCLNT_*). Detect unexpected C2 beaconing from newly installed executable (correlation: installation time + network initiation within minutes). Flag data exfiltration patterns (high bytes out, off-hours, to non-US IP).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Executable Installation from Update Process
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain includes fake update delivery leading to malware install. Detect when update processes spawn or download executables outside vendor-signed paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when update-related process (msiexec, wuauclt, installer variants) creates unsigned executables or DLLs in temp/roaming directories. Flag if update binary's parent process is browser or networking service (svchost, lsass anomaly). Correlate download timestamp with installation timestamp for anomalous delays.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSL/TLS Certificate Usage on Public Wi-Fi
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked Wi-Fi implies MITM capability; must detect self-signed or mismatched certificates presented to common update/app domains on hotel networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for self-signed or third-party CA certificates served by non-authoritative IPs for software update domains (Microsoft, Apple, Adobe, etc.). Flag CN/SAN mismatches on HTTPS connections. Correlate certificate anomalies with DNS responses from gateway IP.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll Masquerade
suggestion.rationale: Article states NightLedger 'masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' Core defense-evasion mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SspiCli.dll loads from non-System32 directories or triggered by AppVShNotify.exe. Detect SspiCli.dll file writes to temporary, user-writable, or staging directories. Flag unexpected delay-load patterns from RPCRT4.dll that route through suspicious DLL sources.

suggestion.title: Recruitment and Videoconferencing Phishing Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.' Primary initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with HR/recruitment subject lines from external senders linking to or attaching archive files (RAR, ZIP). Alert on clicks redirecting from recruitment/job-portal domains to file-sharing services (archive.org, mediafire, etc.). Flag lookalike videoconferencing domains (zoom-xxx, teams-xxx variants) redirecting to non-corporate infrastructure.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Backdoor Reconnaissance Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies backdoor capabilities: 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture.' Behavioral sequence indicates active post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution chains: tasklist/Get-Process → dir/Get-ChildItem → screenshot APIs (BitBlt, GDI+). Alert on unexpected parent-child relationships where AppVShNotify.exe spawns cmd.exe or PowerShell with enumeration commands. Flag reconnaissance patterns in aerospace/aviation sectors targeted per article.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneling Tool Deployment (ArcBridge/BridgeHead)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers, ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling' deployed 'during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound WebSocket (WS/WSS) connections on non-standard ports from system binaries or DLLs. Detect persistent WebSocket tunneling patterns indicative of operator-controlled C2. Alert on WebSocket traffic from Egypt- or Pakistan-based aerospace/aviation infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Tunneling Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article documents BridgeHead deployment 'during post-exploitation activities' following spear-phishing compromise. Indicates transition from access to persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry Run key modifications or startup folder modifications associated with ArcBridge/BridgeHead components. Detect file system writes of tunneling binaries to directories like AppData or ProgramData post-intrusion. Monitor for scheduled task creation or service installation by compromised processes.

suggestion.title: Mirage Kitten Malware Signatures and Attribution Markers
suggestion.rationale: Article names three malware families (NightLedger, ArcBridge, BridgeHead) uniquely developed by Mirage Kitten with specific code and behavioral signatures. Requires signature-based and heuristic detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create file-hash and behavioral signatures for NightLedger DLL (masquerade pattern, DLL search-order hijacking). Detect ArcBridge/BridgeHead process execution or module loading. Alert on known code patterns, mutex names, registry markers unique to Mirage Kitten malware in aerospace, defense, telecom, and aviation organizations.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication with Known Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded password is an exploitable backdoor account — need detection for login attempts using known weak/backdoor credentials or abnormal authentication success rates on low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins to known low-privilege backdoor accounts or patterns of rapid authentication attempts from external networks. Baseline legitimate FMC admin access and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unusual FMC Management Interface Access from External/Non-Approved Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote attacker...access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC is a management interface; detect access from unexpected IP ranges, geolocations, or non-management VLANs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FMC web/management interface access (port 443, SSH 22) from IP ranges outside known trusted admin networks or with ASN/geolocation mismatches. Correlate with baseline admin access times.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Extraction / Unusual Queries from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Once attacker gains access via hard-coded credential, they will enumerate and exfiltrate configuration, policy, and audit data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit/query logs for bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or unusual API calls to sensitive endpoints (users, device configs, threat intelligence) from low-privilege or newly-seen accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Asset inventory and scanner must confirm patch status; unpatched FMC instances are high-priority breach risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for instances of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center with version < patched baseline for CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with firewall rule allows (port 443, SSH) and external reachability tests.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Credential Exposure in Logs or Configurations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline/SIEM may ingest FMC debug logs, error messages, or configuration dumps where the hard-coded credential leaks; need detection for secrets in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan FMC debug/error output and exported configurations for common hard-coded credential patterns (password=, secret=, key=, admin credentials in plaintext). Flag any exposure in logs or unencrypted backups.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Cisco FMC on Internet-Facing Network
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' establishes prerequisite network exposure of management plane. Vulnerability requires internet reachability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances with TCP 443, 8305, or 22 exposed on external-facing interfaces. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20316 patch status. High-risk if exposed and unpatched.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Abuse — Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core exploit: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability...allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Detection must capture successful auth via known default/hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using default/hard-coded account names (admin, root, default service accounts). Flag successful auth from unexpected external IPs, especially if preceded by failed login probes in prior 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Data Access from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article objective post-exploitation: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detect database queries, policy exports, or config retrieval after successful unauthorized auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful low-privileged FMC account authentication with unusual bulk data operations: firewall policy exports, network topology queries, session log retrieval, or configuration backups inconsistent with that account's baseline activity.

suggestion.title: Failed Auth Spike Followed by Successful Low-Privilege Login — Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Typical exploitation workflow: attacker probes for vulnerability before exploiting. Signature: 3+ failed auths in short window → successful low-priv account login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 3+ failed authentication attempts from single source IP within 5-minute window followed by successful login to low-privileged service account within 10 minutes. Alert especially if source IP is external or not in approved admin whitelist.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version Fingerprinting via Banner Grab
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must enumerate vulnerable FMC versions before exploitation. Article references product by name; HTTP/SSH banners leak version identifying exploitable builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connection attempts to FMC interfaces (TCP 443, 22, 8305) for banner-grab patterns: HEAD requests, OPTIONS requests, incomplete SSL handshakes, or SSH version queries. Correlate banner-grabs with subsequent failed auth attempts or exploitation signatures within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-20316 as the vulnerability. Pipeline should generate baseline detection rule matching scanner findings against this CVE ID.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset running Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 in vulnerability scanner output. Cross-correlate with patch status to distinguish known-unpatched from remediated assets.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implying network accessibility. Article template recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Pipeline must generate asset discovery rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco FMC instances accessible from untrusted networks (external, DMZ, guest). Flag any FMC management console listening on standard ports (443, 8305) reachable from non-administrative subnets.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'hard-coded password vulnerability'—attacker uses known static credentials. Pipeline should generate rule for authentication probe/success patterns matching this exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected source IPs using default or low-privileged accounts within 24 hours of CVE disclosure or suspected exploit campaigns. Correlate with vulnerability scanner confirmation of unpatched FMC.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via unauthenticated, low-privileged account. Pipeline should detect data-access patterns post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within FMC audit logs, identify unusual data queries, report generation, or policy export activity occurring immediately after successful authentication from external sources or unexpected geographies. Flag bulk access to sensitive security policies or network configuration data.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version and Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal patch due date 2026-08-01 (now overdue as of 2026-08-03). Pipeline should generate compliance-driven hunt to verify patched state across inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management system for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Extract software version and cross-reference against CISA KEV published patch cutoff date (2026-08-01). Alert on any version older than patched release with a compliance SLA based on CISA directive.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access to FMC — requires asset-inventory hunt for internet-exposed instances. Pipeline identified T1190 but generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances (port 8305, SSL subject CN patterns, Cisco FMC banner probing) accessible from public internet or DMZ. Correlate with organizational asset inventory to flag unmanaged or rogue instances.

suggestion.title: FMC CVE-2026-20316 Credential Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hardcoded password vulnerability...log in to affected device using a low-privileged account.' Detect anomalous low-priv FMC logins from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for low-privileged account logins from non-approved IP ranges, off-hours, or from IPs not in baseline admin-access whitelist. Correlate with failed login attempts preceding successful logins (exploitation pattern).

suggestion.title: FMC Post-Compromise Data Access Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detect unauthorized config/backup export or data queries post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for bulk configuration exports, backup file creation/download, policy export commands, or large network transfers initiated from low-privileged authenticated sessions. Baseline normal admin data-export patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Evasion & False-Negative Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article context: CISA KEV entries exploit patch-lag and scanner false-negatives. Verify vulnerability scanner reports match actual FMC patch status on systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-validate CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner results against Cisco FMC version inventory and patch-management logs. Flag systems where scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but version is known-affected (common with hardcoded-credential vulns due to scanner limitations).

suggestion.title: Anomalous FMC Management Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated remote exploitation requires detection of login attempts deviating from baseline—external source IPs, off-hours, failed auth storms preceding successful logins with hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts to Cisco FMC from public IP space, ASNs owned by VPS/hosting providers, or geographies outside organizational footprint, especially clustering of failed attempts followed by successful authentication or anomalous privileged operations.

suggestion.title: FMC-to-Managed-Device Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC account grants implicit access to deploy configurations or commands across all managed security appliances, enabling lateral movement into protected network perimeter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect configuration pushes, rule modifications, firmware updates, or command execution on managed firewalls/threat defense devices originating from or correlated with a compromised FMC account, especially commands not matching change control ticketing.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' via 'hard-coded password vulnerability'—direct attack vector requiring baseline of compromised credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for successful remote authentications from external sources using low-privileged accounts. Establish allowlist of legitimate administrative access sources and flag deviations; correlate with failed-attempt clusters to catch credential-stuffing patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unexpected Remote Management Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote attacker' accessing management console—baseline of normal access is prerequisite for anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag remote connections to FMC administrative interfaces from non-whitelisted source IPs, especially internet-routable addresses. Alert on country/geolocation anomalies for internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Configuration or Policy Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-compromise data collection from central management platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC logs for bulk policy exports, configuration downloads, or sensitive-file reads (especially credentials, CA certificates, keys). Correlate timing with suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Status—CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-01—patch inventory is mandatory for compliance and risk assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances and cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Flag unpatched instances as critical risk; prioritize remediation for internet-exposed or DMZ-deployed appliances.

suggestion.title: FMC-Managed Firewall Policy Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC enables lateral movement to managed firewall devices—central console is high-value pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous policy deployments to managed firewalls following FMC compromise indicators. Flag out-of-band configuration changes, creation of new allow-rules, or disabling of security controls.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Account Brute Force or Credential Testing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers will test hard-coded credentials across FMC instances; failed attempts precede successful exploits.
log_sources: WAF logs if FMC web interface is exposed
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed authentication attempts to FMC within short time windows from single source IP. Establish threshold triggers (e.g., 5+ failures in 10 minutes) to catch credential-spray patterns before successful breach.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation via Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—the core attack vector is authentication bypass via hard-coded password on Cisco FMC management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interfaces (HTTPS port 443, 8305) for authentication attempts from external IPs. Alert on successful login attempts using low-privileged accounts or credential patterns consistent with hard-coded defaults, especially when followed by data access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact is 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—detection must capture what data is accessed after successful hard-coded credential exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected data access patterns by account privilege level in FMC. Alert on low-privileged or newly-authenticated accounts accessing security policies, firewall rules, threat intelligence feeds, or other classified configuration data. Flag bulk data exports.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Connection Attempts to FMC Management Center
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—detection should identify direct connection attempts to FMC without prior authentication handshake or with truncated credential submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound HTTPS connections to Cisco FMC management ports from external IPs that transition directly to authenticated state or bypass standard login prompts. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to other perimeter systems.

suggestion.title: Low-Privileged Account Privilege Escalation in FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker gains 'low-privileged account' access—this suggests escalation attempts or lateral access to higher-privilege functions post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track function access and permission changes requested by low-privileged FMC accounts after initial login. Alert on attempts to view administrative dashboards, modify policies, or create new administrative accounts using existing low-privilege session.

suggestion.title: Git Release Tag Redirection to Malicious Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is a direct evasion technique that allows an attacker to silently redirect downstream consumers to compromised code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for changes to release tags, especially tags that move backward in commit history or point to commits not on main/default branches. Alert when tags are reassigned to commits authored by unusual accounts or created in isolation. Correlate with push events from accounts with repo write access.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Public GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' as a key obfuscation technique. Orphaned commits are inherently suspicious in public repos and indicate deliberate hiding of code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits that exist in a repository but are not reachable from any branch or tag. In high-security repos, alert on any orphaned commits. Correlate with unusual push activity, tag changes, or commits that contain suspicious code patterns (network exfiltration, secret exposure).

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secret Exposure in CI/CD Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is the impact vector—secrets are logged where CI/CD logs are often public.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for patterns indicating unencrypted secrets (AWS keys, API tokens, private keys). Flag any Action step output that contains Base64-encoded or plaintext credentials. Correlate with recent pushes to the Action's main repository and alert on modified logging/echo statements.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Network Calls from GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This was the detection vector for the actual compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted endpoints. Establish a baseline of expected external calls per Action and alert on deviations. Flag downloads of arbitrary code from external hosts, especially when correlated with recent commits to the Action repository.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Repository Write Access by Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' The root cause is unauthorized or compromised write privileges on a critical shared asset.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new or unexpected write access grants to high-impact repositories (especially those with 1000+ dependents). Flag PAT creation or API token usage from unusual locations/times. Monitor for access grant changes by privileged accounts. Correlate with commits that modify CI/CD behavior or external network calls.

suggestion.title: Mass Pinning to Compromised GitHub Action Version
suggestion.rationale: The article describes 23,000 downstream repos pinning to the malicious tag. Detection should include identifying repos that auto-update or pin to recently-modified release tags without verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In your own environment, scan workflow YAML files for pins to external GitHub Actions, especially to tags that were recently modified or point to non-standard commits. Correlate with increased activity on dependent projects after a tag change. Implement software composition analysis to detect when widely-used Actions introduce malicious dependencies.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded credentials are the attack vector; monitor for successful/failed logins from unexpected sources to FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful logins to Cisco FMC with low-privileged default accounts from external/unapproved IP ranges. Correlate with failed brute-force patterns. High signal on unpatched FMC versions per patch due date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies management interface is network-reachable. Asset exposure hunt for TCP 443 (typical FMC HTTPS) or fingerprint banners matching Cisco FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances responding to remote probes (IPv4/IPv6). Correlate with unpatched inventory. Flag any FMC management port reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Cisco FMC Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After hard-coded credential compromise, detect exfiltration of FMC-stored configuration, firewall rules, or policy data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk export/download of policies, rule sets, or configuration snapshots by low-privileged accounts. Detect unusual data staging or archive creation patterns post-login.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance - CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-08-01. Asset owner hunt: which Cisco FMC instances are patched vs. vulnerable?
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory with Cisco FMC version/build against CVE-2026-20316 patch timeline. Escalate any unpatched instances post-2026-08-01 for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Remote Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — requires immediate detection of external network access bypassing authentication controls
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management ports (8305, 8307) for successful authentication from external/untrusted networks. Alert on successful logins preceded by connection attempts from non-whitelisted IPs, particularly any external sources for a management interface.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Exploitation on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'use of hard-coded password' — must detect both exploitation attempts and successful low-privileged account logins
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for repeated use of known low-privileged account names (e.g., default service accounts). Flag successful authentications with these accounts from unexpected source IPs or timestamps inconsistent with normal operations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes remote unauthenticated exploitation — FMC must be internet-accessible. Standard exposure hunt required for CISA KEV prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query external scanning data and internal asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances exposed on public internet. Cross-reference with firewall rules and segmentation policies; escalate any instances without proper network isolation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Collection Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — requires detection of data collection/exfiltration following successful access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data export patterns, large query results, or configuration data access from FMC after successful authentication. Establish baseline for normal admin activity; alert on deviations such as bulk exports, new scheduled reports, or access to credential stores.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal due date 2026-08-01 — vulnerability scanner output must confirm remediation status to ensure compliance and identify active risk window
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute vulnerability scans targeting Cisco FMC infrastructure for CVE-2026-20316 detection. Confirm patched status across all FMC instances. Flag any systems running vulnerable versions and correlate with remediation tickets; escalate non-compliance before federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password — requires detection for successful authentication using default/hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful remote login attempts using default or hard-coded account patterns. Flag successful authentication to FMC management interface from external IP ranges, especially when preceded by failed authentication spikes.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — requires detection for unauthorized data extraction or policy/configuration exports from compromised FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual backup exports, policy extractions, or configuration dumps initiated from FMC, especially by low-privileged accounts or newly-authenticated session IDs. Correlate export activity timing with successful hard-coded credential authentication.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' capability — requires exposure hunt to identify externally-reachable FMC instances and verify patch status against CVE-2026-20316.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan perimeter for exposed FMC management ports (443, 8305). Cross-reference discovered instances against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable versions. Flag any FMC deployments reaching federal patch due-date of 2026-08-01 still running vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Spike to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential exploitation implies attacker may attempt multiple login vectors — detect authentication failure anomalies that precede successful compromise indicating credential-guessing activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for sustained or distributed failed login attempts targeting default/low-privilege accounts. Alert when failed authentication pattern is followed by successful login from the same source within short time window.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Privilege Escalation on FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies compromise begins with 'low-privileged account' — requires detection for subsequent privilege escalation or lateral movement from that constrained context to access sensitive data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration changes, policy modifications, or access to management-level objects initiated from low-privilege FMC accounts. Flag escalation attempts or assumption of higher-privilege contexts by accounts authenticated via hard-coded credentials.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal due-date 2026-08-01 — requires continuous compliance hunt to track vulnerable vs. patched FMC instances across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute recurring vulnerability scans targeting all Cisco FMC deployments. Maintain real-time inventory of installed FMC versions and correlate against CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability matrix. Escalate unpatched instances post-due-date for emergency remediation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' No use case for detecting hardcoded credential exploitation or brute-force attempts against Cisco FMC management interface (port 443).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC port 443 for login attempts from external networks or rapid successive failures followed by successful auth from same source. Baseline legitimate admin source IPs; alert on deviations. Search for known hardcoded account names in auth logs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC External Accessibility Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' presupposes FMC is internet-exposed. Inventory internal Cisco FMC instances and hunt for those accessible from untrusted networks; correlate with vuln scanner fingerprints for CVE-2026-20316.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query netflow/firewall logs for inbound port 443 connections to Cisco FMC IP ranges from external/non-admin sources. Cross-reference with active vuln scans for CVE-2026-20316 or Shodan/Censys reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Low-Privilege Account Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: gained access grants 'low-privileged account' to reach 'sensitive data within impacted systems.' Pipeline missed detection for post-compromise data collection—policy exports, credential queries, or sensor configs via that account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-authentication, alert on low-privilege FMC accounts performing bulk policy/rule exports, querying firewall device credentials, enumerating sensor/appliance inventory, or invoking backup/export APIs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal due date 2026-08-01; template recommends asset-exposure hunt but pipeline did not generate version/patch-level queries. Enumerate Cisco FMC fleet and flag unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances; extract version/patch level. Cross-reference against Cisco security advisories for CVE-2026-20316 patched versions. Flag all vulnerable versions, especially those internet-facing.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Remote Login Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—pipeline failed to generate any detection for unauthorized access to FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management endpoints (typically ports 443, 8305) for login attempts from external/untrusted networks. Alert on successful logins preceded by no pre-authentication activity. Correlate asset inventory with network flow data to identify publicly accessible FMC instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hard-coded password vulnerability'—no detection rule for weak or default credential exploitation was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC login logs for repeated authentication attempts using low-privileged default usernames (admin, root, etc.). Flag failed attempts followed by success from the same source within brief time window, suggesting credential enumeration or hardcoded-password exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Network Exposure Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'public-facing application' exposure; pipeline should generate standard asset-hunting query to identify reachable FMC instances in the environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results against inbound network flows to Cisco FMC ports from untrusted sources. Identify all FMC instances and validate network segmentation; flag any instances accepting inbound management connections from the internet.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise allows 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—no detection for data exfiltration or bulk access by low-privileged accounts was modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC configuration exports, database dumps, and policy downloads by low-privileged accounts. Track outbound HTTPS/SSH transfers of FMC data to external destinations. Alert on unusual API queries or bulk data requests post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Privilege Escalation After Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' access—pipeline omitted detection for privilege escalation that would follow initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit and debug logs for role or permission elevation requests from low-privileged user sessions. Alert on administrative function calls (policy modification, user management, credential changes) by accounts that previously only held read access.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Cisco FMC Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access — implies management interface exposed to internet. Need baseline of which FMC instances are reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC default management ports (443, 8305, 8307) reachable from external IP ranges. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unpatched instances. Look for new external IPs initiating TLS handshakes to FMC ports.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Need to detect login attempts using known Cisco FMC default/hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication attempts against FMC using known hard-coded account names (e.g., admin, cisco, root with default passwords). Alert on successful logins with these credentials, especially from external IPs. Cross-reference failed attempts spike before successful login.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After initial compromise via hard-coded password, attacker will query/exfiltrate firewall rules, logs, policies, or threat intelligence configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API calls and database queries for large data exports post-authentication. Detect policy/rules downloads, threat intelligence database pulls, or configuration backups initiated by low-privileged accounts. Flag unusual access patterns to sensitive tables (user configs, encryption keys).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or Low-Privilege Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Need baseline of normal admin vs. low-privilege access patterns and alert on deviations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of which accounts typically access FMC and from which IPs/times. Alert when low-privileged credentials are used to access admin functions, perform config changes, or export sensitive data. Cross-correlate with network indicators to catch lateral movement attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means active exploitation in the wild. Need detection for the specific CVE exploitation signature or access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to FMC that attempt to bypass authentication or exploit the hard-coded password flaw (e.g., specific request patterns, API endpoints used by public PoC tools, or known malicious payloads). Correlate with patch status from vulnerability scanner.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Script Integrity Violation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Hackers Poison Adform Script' — core attack vector is modification of trusted ad-serving JS. Pipeline failed to flag script authenticity failures despite this being the enabling mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Subresource Integrity (SRI) checks fail for Adform or major ad-network script tags. Monitor for Content-Security-Policy violations on ad-tech domains. Detect script hash mismatches between signed baseline and runtime execution.

suggestion.title: Crypto Wallet Address Anomaly in Page Response
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites.' Pipeline should detect cryptocurrency addresses (Bitcoin, Ethereum) appearing in HTTP responses from non-crypto domains, especially ad-serving responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Regex-flag responses containing valid crypto wallet formats (^[13][a-km-zA-HJ-NP-Z1-9]{25,34}$|^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$) from Adform CDN or customer ad-injection endpoints. Correlate with reports of redirected transactions.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise — Adform CDN Origin Unauthorized Write
suggestion.rationale: For script poisoning at scale, attacker achieved write access to Adform CDN origin or cache layer. Pipeline should detect unauthorized object modifications on ad-network infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PUT/POST requests to Adform origin servers from anomalous IPs or service accounts. Detect cache invalidation commands outside maintenance windows. Monitor for unauthorized file writes to ad-script directories.

suggestion.title: Script Load from Non-Canonical Adform CDN Host
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may have hosted poisoned script on attacker domain or redirected Adform requests via DNS/MITM. Pipeline should detect script loads from unexpected origins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests for 'adform' domain resolving to non-canonical CDN IPs or attacker ASNs. Alert on script downloads over HTTP vs HTTPS. Monitor for DNS CNAME poisoning or IP geolocation anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Crypto Transactions Tied to Compromised Web Session
suggestion.rationale: End-state impact is users' crypto wallets sending funds to attacker addresses. Pipeline should correlate unexpected blockchain transactions with sessions where script integrity failed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cryptocurrency outbound transactions from company/customer wallets to novel recipient addresses within 1 hour of web sessions where Adform SRI checks failed or malicious wallet regex matched.

suggestion.title: Adform Script Modification Without Deployment Event
suggestion.rationale: Injected crypto-swapping logic must persist in production script outside of CI/CD. Pipeline should detect script changes with no corresponding deploy ticket or code review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits or file edits to Adform script paths where committer is not a known release engineer, or edits occur outside deployment windows, or deploy audit log has no corresponding entry.

suggestion.title: Detect Wi-Fi Network Hijacking and Man-in-the-Middle Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Hijacked Hotel Wi-Fi' as the attack vector. Pipeline missed initial-access phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ARP spoofing, DNS redirection, or SSL certificate injection patterns in hotel/shared network environments. Detect asymmetric traffic flows, MITM-indicative certificate mismatches, or anomalous gateway-to-client traffic during suspicious connection periods.

suggestion.title: Detect Delivery of Unsigned or Masqueraded Update Packages
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'Fake Updates to Deliver Surveillance Malware.' Pipeline failed to generate delivery-phase detection despite this being central to the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable files with update-like names (e.g., 'SystemUpdate.exe', 'UpdateService.msi') lacking valid digital signatures or originating from non-standard update sources. Alert on downloads over HTTP from non-vendor servers during hotel Wi-Fi sessions.

suggestion.title: Detect User Execution of Malicious Update Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Attack relies on tricking users into executing fake updates. Pipeline missed the execution trigger that converts delivery into compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious update file download with immediate process execution, especially from non-administrative contexts or unusual parent processes (explorer.exe, browser, downloaded-file context).

suggestion.title: Detect Surveillance Malware Collection and Exfiltration Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware with 'surveillance' capabilities implying data collection and C2 communication. Pipeline generated zero detection coverage for post-compromise persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to suspicious or newly-registered domains post-infection. Detect exfiltration of keystroke logs, screenshots, credential databases, or browser history via encrypted channels following malware execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Malware Masquerading as Legitimate System Software
suggestion.rationale: Fake updates impersonate genuine software—a masquerading defense-evasion layer central to delivery success. Pipeline overlooked this obfuscation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables bearing legitimate update names but lacking authentic signatures, located in user directories, or executed from unusual parent processes. Cross-reference file hashes against legitimate vendor update catalogs.

suggestion.title: Detect Hotel/Shared Network C2 Traffic Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware delivered over hotel Wi-Fi will beacon outbound to C2 infrastructure from the same compromised network. Pipeline missed network-based detection of post-compromise communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate update traffic from hotel Wi-Fi. Alert on outbound encrypted or obfuscated traffic to non-whitelisted destinations post-update installation, especially to newly-registered or bulletproof-hoster domains.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes NightLedger masquerading as SspiCli.dll and targeting AppVShNotify.exe via DLL search-order hijacking: 'The implant masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for instances where RPCRT4.dll or AppVShNotify.exe load SspiCli.dll from unusual locations (not System32), particularly from current directory or temp folders. Correlate with presence of unsigned SspiCli.dll in non-standard paths. Alert on process load events showing delay-load behavior for authentication-related RPC calls.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing with Recruitment-Themed Lures and Fake Hiring Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial compromise vector: 'highly targeted spear-phishing campaigns, fake recruitment portals' and 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms'—a high-confidence attack pattern for this actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment-themed subjects claiming to be from major hiring platforms or aerospace/defense firms, containing file-sharing service links to archives. Monitor for Okta/LinkedIn/Indeed domain homoglyphs in sender addresses or URLs. Correlate recipients with target industries (aerospace, aviation, defense, telecom) in MEA region.

suggestion.title: Lookalike Videoconferencing Portal Redirects to Malicious Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers deployed 'lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services'—a specific social engineering vector not typically pre-mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clicks to homoglyph/typosquat domains resembling Zoom, Teams, or WebEx that 302-redirect to file-sharing services (mega.nz, mediafire, OneDrive) in referrer chain. Correlate with phishing email reports. Monitor for archive downloads to user temp directories following such redirects.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneler Traffic Detection (BridgeHead/ArcBridge)
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces two custom WebSocket tunnelers deployed in post-exploitation: 'two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers, ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling.' No protocol-level detection provided in article, but behavior is described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for persistent WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) from compromised hosts to unexpected destinations, particularly sustained bi-directional traffic on non-standard ports. Monitor for WebSocket upgrade handshakes followed by high-entropy binary payloads. Correlate with post-exploitation indicators (e.g., RPC enumeration, process snapshots) on the same host.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Reconnaissance and Screenshot Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies NightLedger capabilities: 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture'—distinctive behaviors that should trigger detection when combined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious processes spawned by rundll32.exe or svchost.exe loading SspiCli.dll, followed by screenshot APIs (GetDC, BitBlt) or use of GDI+ screenshot capture. Correlate with Process32 enumeration, file enumeration of Documents/Desktop, and WMI queries for installed software. Look for screenshot files in Temp or AppData directories shortly after process discovery activity.

suggestion.title: Aerospace and Defense Sector Targeting with Post-Exploitation Tunneler Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article reports specific victim profile: 'BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization'—signals sector-specific targeting that warrants organization-level alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For organizations in aerospace, aviation, defense, and telecom sectors in MEA region, implement enhanced monitoring for post-exploitation patterns: process enumeration, file share discovery, and unexpected outbound WebSocket or tunneling tool execution. Flag any combination of network reconnaissance + WebSocket listener spawning within 1 hour of phishing email engagement.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Anomaly Hunt — Hardcoded Credential Reuse

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal remediation due-date (2026-08-01). Pipeline ignored vulnerability lifecycle and compliance context required by SOC operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco FMC instances against vulnerability scan results (Tenable, Qualys). Identify versions pre-9.1.5 and pre-9.2.3 (per Cisco advisory). Post-due-date non-compliance triggers incident escalation per regulatory timeline.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Control Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attacker with hard-coded access may persist by disabling MFA or injecting credentials. No defense-evasion detection. Related directly to vulnerability exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on disabled TACACS+/RADIUS integration, deactivated MFA policies, or creation of local admin accounts in FMC. Monitor for SSH key injections or removal of authentication enforcement. Correlate temporal clusters with failed auth spikes.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Payload Detection in VeloCloud Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'exploits…command injection flaw' establishes execution vector but pipeline surfaced zero detection logic. Should monitor HTTP requests to Orchestrator endpoints for shell metacharacters and command substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to VeloCloud Orchestrator endpoints containing pipe (|), semicolon (;), backticks, or $() patterns in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with 500-level errors or abnormal response times indicating attempted injection.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from VeloCloud
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection results in arbitrary OS command execution within application privilege context. Pipeline failed to propose monitoring for this artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from VeloCloud Orchestrator parent (java.exe, orchestrator binary) executing interpreters (cmd.exe, bash, sh) or network utilities (curl, wget, netcat) with suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to VeloCloud Configuration APIs
suggestion.rationale: Command injection in public-facing Orchestrator typically exploits unauthenticated or low-privilege endpoints. Pipeline produced no detection for this initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected authentication patterns for Orchestrator endpoints. Alert on requests to /api/* or /config/* paths lacking authorization headers or with error responses indicating bypassable auth, especially from external IP space.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Remote Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — must monitor for inbound access attempts to FMC management interface (ports 8305, 443) from external or non-approved source IPs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful or repeated failed login attempts to Cisco FMC from external IP ranges or geographies outside trusted management networks. Correlate with T1190 exploitation attempts (HTTP/HTTPS requests to FMC API endpoints, HTTP 40x/50x status codes indicating exploitation probes).

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Abuse Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'use of hard-coded password' and 'low-privileged account' — must detect authentication events using known hard-coded service account identifiers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FMC authentication attempts or successful logins using documented hard-coded service account names. Flag if usage occurs outside expected automated service windows, from non-standard source IPs, or in conjunction with data-export activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Exports from Cisco FMC Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exploitation 'allows access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — must detect bulk downloads of configurations, policies, device credentials, or audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for large or anomalous data exports: policy configuration downloads, device inventory dumps, credential backups, or audit log extractions. Trigger alert if initiated shortly after new authentication events, from non-admin accounts, or with file sizes exceeding baseline.

suggestion.title: FMC-to-Managed-Device Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Cisco FMC compromise grants attacker access to managed firewall devices and their configurations — compromised FMC can be used to pivot to and compromise managed security appliances
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FMC-initiated configuration pushes, rule modifications, or credential dumps to managed firewall devices occurring after suspicious authentication or data-export activity. Flag rule changes that disable logging, modify access-control policies, or extract device credentials.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Tampering & Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Attackers with FMC access may disable audit logging, modify administrative accounts, or alter firewall rules to establish persistence or evade detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC audit logging disablement, admin account creation/modification, SSL certificate replacement, backup deletion, or large-scale rule modifications occurring post-exploitation. Correlate with authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scan Correlation & Follow-up Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch-due date (2026-08-01) requires immediate discovery and remediation — vulnerability scanner results must be cross-referenced against behavioral indicators of exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco FMC instances flagged by vulnerability scanners as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Correlate scanner results with network behavior: inbound connections to FMC ports from new sources, authentication failures/successes post-scan, or unusual API activity from flagged asset IPs within 24–48 hours.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Asset Exposure — Cisco FMC Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]' and directly instructs: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-20316'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this unambiguous directive.
