suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Firewall Management Center for unusual access to sensitive repositories (firewall rules, device credentials, policy configurations) by low-privileged accounts. Alert on bulk exports, API queries for credential objects, or data staging after initial compromise.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' exploitation (T1190)—need asset discovery detection for internet-routable FMC administrative interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances with administrative management ports (443, 8305, 22) exposed to untrusted or public networks. Correlate with patch-status and known CVE-2026-20316 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Firewall Management Center Public Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article states FMC is exposed and unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit. 'Public-facing' in T1190 mapping and federal agencies must remediate by 2026-08-01 imply active scanning. Pipeline failed to generate canonical asset-exposure hunt mentioned in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound probes to Cisco FMC typical ports (443, 8305, 8307) from external or unusual internal sources. Correlate with vulnerability scanner activity or port scans. Baseline known management subnets and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Login via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'hard-coded password vulnerability...allow unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Pipeline missed credential-access detection entirely despite explicit authentication vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts and successful sessions from external IPs or anomalous geographies. Alert on successful logins followed by low-privileged account enumeration or configuration access. Baseline legitimate management access.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after login. Post-compromise collection phase completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for bulk data exports, policy retrievals, or sensitive object queries (managed device configs, threat intelligence, user credentials) from FMC after new or anomalous authentication sessions. Alert on configurations or intelligence data leaving FMC to unexpected destinations.

suggestion.title: FMC Lateral Movement to Managed Devices
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of management center historically precedes compromise of managed devices. Article implies access to 'impacted systems' (plural) but pipeline missed lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FMC compromise indicators with anomalous commands or policy pushes to managed Firewall/IDS devices. Monitor for unauthorized device firmware updates, config changes, or credential resets issued from the management center.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Public Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker' which requires FMC to be network-accessible from untrusted sources. This is the necessary entry condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful TCP connections to Cisco FMC ports (443 HTTPS, 8305 admin interface) from external/untrusted IP ranges. Alert on FMC login pages accessible from internet-routable sources. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scan results to identify exploitable instances.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly involves 'hard-coded password'—attacker must either know the credential or brute-force it. Authentication logs must be monitored for default/weak credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC login attempts for known hard-coded or default usernames (admin, fmcadmin, etc.). Alert on repeated failed authentication attempts followed by successful login from external source IPs, or on successful logins using weak/default credentials from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Admin Access from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful access by 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—external login to FMC admin interface is inherently anomalous and exploitative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC login from IP addresses outside your organization's trusted administrative IP ranges. Correlate with geographic impossibilities, non-business-hours access, or deviations from baseline administrator login patterns.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Extraction from Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Attacker goal is 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—FMC repositories contain firewall policies, security configurations, credentials, and network topology. Post-authentication data queries indicate adversary moving to collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk API queries or database reads targeting FMC policy repositories, device configurations, and security group definitions. Flag large sequential API calls to sensitive endpoints within compressed time windows, especially within minutes of newly-authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Policy Deployment via Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management platform that controls downstream firewalls. Exploitation enables lateral movement and defense evasion by pushing policies to disable security controls across the managed infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for policy pushes originating from non-standard admin accounts or following external authentication. Flag policy changes that disable security modules, modify firewall rules to whitelist unusual traffic, or add new administrative accounts to managed firewalls.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation in the wild. Federal patch due date is 2026-08-01. Presence in vulnerability scans is critical indicator of exploitable exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated daily/weekly scans of all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances must test for CVE-2026-20316. Alert on any positive result. Cross-reference with patch records and inventory to confirm true positives and identify unpatched/unknown instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt'; FMC is internet-facing management appliance—primary detection vector is discovering vulnerable instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management systems for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Prioritize internet-exposed instances with patch lag relative to 2026-08-01 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Anomaly - Hard-Coded Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker using 'hard-coded password' via 'unauthenticated, remote' access to 'log in to an affected device'—detect authentication attempts with known hard-coded low-privilege account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts with hard-coded low-privilege account. Flag any successful login from public/unexpected IP ranges. Correlate with vulnerability scanner alerts for same host to confirm exploitation window.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—detect bulk data export or unusual configuration retrieval patterns following successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within FMC audit logs, flag bulk policy downloads, device configuration exports, credential lookups, or inventory queries executed shortly after successful authentication. Correlate timing with known exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FMC Instances Post-Deadline Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date '2026-08-01'; any unpatched FMC post-deadline represents non-compliance and active exploitation risk given CISA KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated alert for any Cisco FMC instance without CVE-2026-20316 patch applied after 2026-08-01. Include remediation owner, current exposure duration, and CISA KEV exploitation-in-wild evidence in escalation.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Nimbus Manticore Deploys NightLedger'—malware execution is the primary attack vector. Pipeline produced zero detection use case despite this being the core IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NightLedger process instantiation, module loading, and file-system artifacts. Monitor parent-process chains typical of malware distribution (Office macros, script execution, MSI install). Establish YARA signatures and file-hash IOCs. Flag registry/scheduled-task creation during malware execution.

suggestion.title: Covert Relay Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article states systems are turned into 'covert relays'—this functionality must persist across reboots. Pipeline missed persistence detection despite this being definitive to the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unauthorized registry autostart modifications (HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce), new service creation, and scheduled-task installation. Flag unsigned executables in startup directories. Detect DLL search-order hijacking and service-binary replacement.

suggestion.title: Covert Relay Outbound Traffic Forwarding
suggestion.rationale: Systems functioning as 'covert relays' exhibit distinctive network patterns. Article describes relay infrastructure for attacker C2 without specifying domains/IPs, but relay forwarding is detectable via network behavior analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound connections on non-standard ports from previously dormant systems. Detect reverse-proxy patterns (inbound-then-outbound traffic pairs). Alert on traffic-volume spikes and anomalies inconsistent with baseline user behavior.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Relay Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Covert relay systems imply multi-stage attacks where compromised hosts stage further compromises. Article mentions 'victim systems' (plural), indicating networked compromise. Pipeline ignored lateral-movement detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network-access patterns: relay-compromised systems initiating connections to new targets. Monitor C$ admin-share access, WMI/RPC execution, and lateral-movement tooling staged through relay systems. Flag process-creation chains converging on relay infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Nimbus Manticore Attribution Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names threat actor 'Nimbus Manticore'. Pipeline produced zero actor-attribution detections or behavioral baseline despite actor name being the first signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish Nimbus Manticore TTP baseline: known C2 infrastructure, malware delivery methods, and exploitation patterns. Alert on re-use of actor-specific techniques even with new malware variants. Cross-reference actor IOCs against email, DNS, and endpoint logs.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires initial compromise to deploy NightLedger. Pipeline should detect delivery vectors (phishing, watering-hole, supply-chain) that precede malware execution and relay installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious email attachments or links, unauthorized software installation, and exploitation of known vulnerabilities. Flag if malware delivery correlates with software patching windows or trusted software updaters. Detect post-delivery persistence installation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance / Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center and federal patch due-date (2026-08-01). Pipeline must surface asset inventory hunts for affected product versions to catch unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and asset databases for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances matching the CVE-2026-20316 affected version range. Alert on hosts with FMC deployed but no recent patch activity or version mismatch against published fixes.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hard-coded password vulnerability' allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account.' This is a valid-account exploitation pathway not yet modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface logs and proxy/WAF logs for repeated failed or successful login attempts using known default/low-privileged account names (e.g., 'admin', 'fmc'). Correlate with network-originating IPs outside normal management ranges.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Exploitation success metrics must include data enumeration/exfiltration after authentication, not just login detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all data queries and exports from Cisco FMC API or GUI post-authentication. Alert on anomalous volume of policy rules, firewall configurations, or forensic data exported in short time window, especially from atypical user accounts or IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure of Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies the FMC management port is internet-reachable or VPN-accessible. Exposure hunts are canonical CISA KEV response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network telemetry for inbound traffic on standard Cisco FMC ports (e.g., 443, 8305) from untrusted networks. Cross-check against firewall rules and asset inventory to identify FMC instances with non-standard or overly permissive ingress ACLs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Brute-Force or Credential Stuffing
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password attacks often manifest as horizontal brute-force attempts across multiple accounts. Article describes 'low-privileged account' as entry point; repeated login attempts under stress should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 failed login attempts to Cisco FMC within 5 minutes, or ≥3 successful logins using the same low-privileged account from different source IPs in <1 hour. Baseline normal admin activity first to tune FP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Signature (IDS/IPS)
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation (CISA KEV) justifies development of network-level signatures. Payload or request patterns specific to this vulnerability's exploitation chain should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy/update IDS/IPS/WAF rules to match CVE-2026-20316 exploitation signatures (e.g., requests to FMC APIs with hard-coded credential payloads, or management endpoint probes). Cross-reference with Snort/Suricata communities for SID mapping.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-20316 Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker is 'unauthenticated, remote' and requires 'affected device' accessible from network. Exploitation requires exposed management interface. Federal due date 2026-08-01 demands immediate asset discovery and patch prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 affected versions. Prioritize instances with accessible management interfaces (ports 443/8305) by federal patch due date. Use CVSS context + CISA KEV 'actively exploited' to justify emergency patching.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Authentication Attempts via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' This is direct articulation of attack method—hard-coded credential exploitation. Pipeline generated zero detection for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC REST API or CLI from external IPs using service/low-privileged accounts. Monitor for repeated failed login attempts from single source followed by success (credential-spraying pattern). Correlate against known Cisco FMC default/hard-coded credential identifiers published in vendor advisories.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Data Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-exploitation includes bulk export of firewall policies, credentials, user data, and network topology. Pipeline did not generate detection for data-access/collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for bulk data exports (firewall policies, ACLs, VPN credentials, user configurations) initiated by low-privileged accounts or unexpected contexts. Alert on API calls to enumeration endpoints (GET /api/config/firewall_policies, /api/fwm/managed_devices) with large result sets. Correlate with external data exfiltration (large file transfer, DNS/HTTP tunneling, HTTPS POST with anomalous payload).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Post-Compromise Firewall Policy Modification
suggestion.rationale: Upon unauthorized access via hard-coded credentials, attacker typically modifies firewall rules to enable persistence or network egress for C2. Article describes 'low-privileged account'—suggests privilege escalation or direct rule-modification capability within FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall policy creations/modifications (rules added, updated, or deleted) from low-privileged service accounts, unexpected admin accounts, or IPs linked to initial compromise. Detect rules permitting outbound traffic to known C2 domains, disabling logging/monitoring, or allowing lateral movement. Correlate with suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance (Policy/Network Discovery)
suggestion.rationale: Attacker gains 'access sensitive data'—includes network topology, firewall policies, and user details stored in FMC. Post-compromise reconnaissance patterns include enumeration of policies and network objects to plan bypass/persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC API for repeated or bulk queries to network-object endpoints (/api/config/networkobjects, /api/config/firewall_policies, /api/identity/users). Alert on unusual enumeration patterns from low-privileged accounts, particularly rapid sequential API calls that suggest automated reconnaissance. Compare against baseline administrative query patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Hard-coded Credential Scanning and Brute Force
suggestion.rationale: CVE centers on hard-coded password vulnerability. Attackers will actively scan and exploit this using known credential sets. Standard brute-force detection may miss credential-spraying attacks using published hard-coded values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts using known hard-coded account/password combinations documented in Cisco CVE-2026-20316 advisory. Alert on distributed authentication attempts (multiple source IPs within short window targeting same FMC instance). Flag any successful authentication using non-standard service accounts or credentials that should remain unexposed externally.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Asset Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags CISA KEV status (active exploitation). Pipeline extracted no IOC. Vulnerability scanner results are the canonical first-line detection for known-vulnerable Cisco FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a vulnerability scanner identifies Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize hits on systems exposed to untrusted networks or internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Success
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline missed T1078 (Valid Accounts) and T1110 (Brute Force) entirely. Hard-coded passwords are credentials reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful login to Cisco FMC low-privilege default or service accounts (e.g., admin, pnadmin) from external/untrusted sources, especially when MFA logs show 2FA was bypassed or not enforced.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies post-auth impact: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' This is the collection phase—policy exports, credential access, config dumps from low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy configuration exports, security group exports, credential manager access, or diagnostic bundle generation initiated by low-privilege FMC accounts or from newly authenticated sessions without prior administrative behavior.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Cisco FMC Management Interface Discovery
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1190 presumes public-facing application. Pipeline did not propose network reconnaissance hunts for exposed FMC instances (port 443, 8305 banner grabs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management interfaces exposed to internet: query network data for IPs responding on port 443 or 8305 with Cisco FMC SSL certificate/banner; cross-check Shodan/Censys for FMC instances; validate asset inventory alignment.

suggestion.title: FMC Vulnerability Status Inventory Audit
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date is 2026-08-01 (2 days past). Pipeline provided no inventory-based IOC or version-check guidance. Asset inventory is the operational prerequisite for CISA KEV remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management system for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Extract version numbers and cross-reference Cisco advisory for CVE-2026-20316 affected versions. Flag unpatched instances, especially those with external/untrusted network access.

suggestion.title: Failed-to-Successful FMC Login Sequence (Hard-coded Credential Brute-Force Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password attacks often show multiple failed attempts before success, distinct from typical dictionary brute-force. Article's 'unauthenticated...remote attacker' implies reconnaissance or credential enumeration preceding auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 2–5 failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC default/low-privilege accounts from a single external IP, followed by a successful login within 5 minutes, with no intervening password reset or MFA challenge in logs.

suggestion.title: Detect release tag reassignment in GitHub repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes persistence mechanism: 'attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'attacker could point people to the malicious commit simply by updating the changed-files GitHub Action code's repo.' Tag manipulation is the direct propagation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor high-dependency GitHub repositories for release tag modifications, especially tags moving to different commits or newly-orphaned commits. Alert on bulk tag operations or tags reassigned without corresponding source-code audit trail.

suggestion.title: Detect plaintext secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies core impact: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Attack succeeds because malicious workflow code bypasses GitHub's encryption scheme: 'without the secret ever appearing in the build log' is the normal state that was violated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline GitHub Actions logs to expect zero secret leakage per GitHub's encryption design. Scan logs for AWS key patterns, GitHub tokens, API credentials, and private key headers. Flag any plaintext occurrences and correlate with recent workflow changes.

suggestion.title: Detect orphaned commits in high-value GitHub repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article names orphaned commits as 'key enabling factor' and provides detailed mechanics: commits remain navigable on GitHub even after branch deletion. Combined with tag manipulation: 'attack commit orphaned from any branches' was intentional obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query repositories with high external dependencies for commits without branch references but assigned release tags. Orphaned commit creation correlating with tag updates is high-risk. Monitor commit graph for floating commits in sensitive repos.

suggestion.title: Detect external network calls initiated from GitHub Actions workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals detection method: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' External calls are the observable signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network activity from GitHub Actions runners for undocumented external destinations. Baseline legitimate dependency pulls and flag novel external hosts. Correlate with recent workflow or action version changes.

suggestion.title: Detect write-access escalation on supply-chain GitHub repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article names write access as root cause: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo' and 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Write access is the prerequisite that enabled all subsequent steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new contributor access or permission elevation to repositories with high external dependents (1000+ stars or used by 1000+ downstream repos). Flag unexpected write-access grants and lack of corresponding change control tickets.

suggestion.title: Detect tag-pinned dependency resolution to unexpected commits
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector: workflows using 'tj-actions/changed-files@v35' suddenly pull malicious code because v35 tag was moved. Article shows: 'uses: tj-actions/changed-files@v35' — tag reassignment affected all 23,000 dependent repos silently.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For consumers of GitHub Actions, monitor source-pinned dependencies and detect when resolved commits diverge from historical baselines. Flag when a semantic-version tag now resolves to a commit newer than the previous resolution or to an orphaned commit.

suggestion.title: QR Code Embedded in PDF Phishing Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'QR code-embedded PDFs to bypass traditional email gateways' and 'auto-generated, victim-tailored PDF documents containing QR codes that direct to adversary-controlled M365 credential harvesting pages'. Explicit initial-access vector in >50% of engagements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PDF attachments with embedded or encoded QR codes, especially in messages from external or newly compromised domains. Correlate QR resolution to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Monitor for M365 credential harvesting pages referenced in PDF metadata or decoded QR output.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing M365 Defense Evasion: Suspicious Inbox Rules and SharePoint Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article directly describes: 'creating email inbox rules for defense evasion, leveraging SharePoint to host malicious documents, and sending additional internal and external phishing emails'. These are observed post-compromise behaviors from UAT-11764.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation by newly compromised accounts within hours of phishing success, especially rules deleting, hiding, or forwarding emails. Monitor for unusual SharePoint file uploads from low-risk-score accounts. Correlate phishing detection to subsequent mail-rule or SharePoint events.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Flow Phishing (ARToken PhaaS Platform)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ARToken exposing '80+ API endpoints for device code phishing' and 'bypassing MFA through the OAuth device authorization flow'. Direct bypass of MFA without stealing passwords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code authorization flows from unusual geos or IPs, especially multiple rapid-fire flows from same account. Monitor for device confirmation fatigue (repeated approvals over short interval). Flag device code flows immediately preceding token-based lateral movement or suspicious cloud activity.

suggestion.title: Trojanized MeshAgent Backdoor Installed as SYSTEM Auto-Start Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Sinobi operators 'use a trojanized MeshAgent binary as their primary C2 mechanism' installed as 'SYSTEM-level auto-start service, communicating over encrypted WebSocket (WSS) to an attacker-controlled server' enabling 'undetected access for approximately three days'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MeshAgent binary installation with SYSTEM privileges or registry auto-start entries where not pre-authorized. Monitor for WSS outbound connections from MeshAgent to unapproved C2 infrastructure. Hunt for MeshAgent running under SYSTEM context without corresponding legitimate MeshCentral deployment records.

suggestion.title: Zoho Assist Unattended Remote Access Deployment (Warlock/Storm-2603)
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'Warlock ransomware operators deploying an installer for the RMM tool Zoho Assist Unattended Agent, which is designed to allow administrative remote control of an endpoint without a user logged in'. Enables covert persistent access without user session requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Zoho Assist Unattended Agent installation outside approved MDM deployment channels. Monitor registry for Zoho Assist persistence mechanisms. Alert on unattended remote connections when no user is logged in or during high-risk hours.

suggestion.title: Service Account Credential Theft from NTDS.dit, Lateral Movement via RDP/WinRM to Ransomware Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes chain: 'obtained from the domain credential store, ntds.dit. The actor moved laterally through the network using RDP and WinRM, leveraging a service account with a weak, easily cracked password' followed by 'deployed the ransomware across the entire domain using a malicious Group Policy Object (GPO) logon script'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on NTDS.dit access outside domain controller operations or admin tools. Monitor RDP/WinRM connections from service accounts to multiple endpoints. Detect GPO modification adding malicious logon scripts. Correlate service account elevation to subsequent rapid encryption across domain.

suggestion.title: FMC Vulnerability Scanner Detection (CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites CVE-2026-20316 and directs to 'asset-exposure hunt' using vulnerability scanners as the primary detection method. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for any unpatched or end-of-life Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances flagged for CVE-2026-20316. High-risk finding if detected post-2026-08-01 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication via Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded credential exploitation is the core attack vector—baseline authentication logs must detect anomalous logins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful remote authentication to FMC management interface (port 443 typical) from external IPs or IPs outside normal administrative ranges, especially if followed by privilege escalation or sensitive data queries.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via low-privileged account post-login. Detection must cover lateral data movement after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC activity logs for queries or exports of configuration data, firewall rules, or policy objects initiated from low-privileged admin accounts; correlate with recent failed/successful logins to detect post-compromise data collection.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FMC Fleet Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and establishes federal due date 2026-08-01. Inventory of unpatched instances must be a standing hunt, not reactive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline query of all FMC instances in fleet; extract version/patch level and flag any instance running a version known to be vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316; compare against published patch guidance.

suggestion.title: FMC Network Access from Non-Administrative IPs
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential attacks are typically remote and come from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Network segmentation violations to FMC should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of administrative networks that should access FMC management interface. Alert on connection attempts from external IP space, residential ISPs, cloud providers, or VPN endpoints outside approved remote-access ranges.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'currently being exploited in the wild' by 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implies external accessibility. Recommended template asset-exposure hunt (referenced in article) was not generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances on public internet by certificate issuer fingerprint (Cisco/FMC), port 443/8305 banner, HTTP response headers. Alert on Shodan/Censys hits for FMC outside authorized public ranges.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Brute Force Against FMC Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' using 'hard-coded password'—attack vector is known-credential guessing, not zero-day exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication attempts to FMC from external IPs followed by successful login. Flag logins to default/documented hard-coded usernames (e.g., 'admin', Cisco default creds) from non-corporate IP ranges. Baseline normal login patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege FMC Account Access to Sensitive Policy/Rule Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via 'low-privileged account'—implies lateral movement within FMC to exfiltrate rules, policies, threat intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls/exports of security policies, firewall rules, threat feeds, or account directories by low-privilege accounts. Alert on bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or account enumeration queries initiated by compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerability Assessment and Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article references CVE-2026-20316 by identifier only; no version ranges specified. Fingerprinting to identify affected FMC versions is required for triage and scope assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for HTTP requests probing FMC version endpoints (/api/fmc_platform/v1/info, admin/version). Extract version from response headers, HTTP body, or TLS certificate metadata. Cross-reference against Cisco advisory for affected versions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Scheduled Backup or Database Export by Suspicious Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers access 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—FMC database exports and backups are high-value collection targets for threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC backup/export initiation by low-privilege accounts or from unusual times/locations. Correlate with recent authentication events to low-privilege accounts. Flag exports to non-standard destinations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Federal Compliance Remediation SLA Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'—CISA KEV compliance is a mandatory SLA. Lack of patching is auditable and carries regulatory risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Cisco FMC instances scanned after 2026-08-01 federal due-date showing CVE-2026-20316 as unpatched. Flag unpatched instances 14+ days past due-date for escalation to compliance/incident response.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential: Cisco FMC Default Account Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' + 'hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline zero UCs on default credential detection against FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful logins to Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 8305, 443) using default/low-privileged account names from non-corporate source IPs. Correlate with scripted authentication patterns (rapid successive requests, static credentials) and CVE-2026-20316 inventory flagged devices.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Public Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploiting exposed appliance. Zero UC for detecting routable Cisco FMC instances on internet-facing interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC appliances reachable from untrusted networks via network segmentation logs or public IP scans. Alert on inbound connection attempts to FMC management ports from non-whitelisted external IP ranges. Cross-reference with unpatched asset inventory for CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Exfiltration: Cisco FMC Sensitive Config Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline zero UCs for detecting policy/config export, data queries, or API abuse post-credential-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for bulk policy rule exports, configuration downloads, threat-feed retrievals, or backup-file generation within 30min of successful authentication via low-privileged account. Flag lateral querying of managed Firewall device configs. Correlate with external data transfer events.

suggestion.title: Authentication Enumeration: Cisco FMC Brute-Force / Account Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential exploitation vector implies scanning/enumeration of valid accounts on FMC before exploitation. Zero UCs for detecting authentication reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >10 failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC management interface from single IP within 10min window. Flag dictionary/credential-spray patterns (rotating usernames, static password). Alert on scanning for common FMC default accounts (admin, root, etc.).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise: FMC Role/Permission Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' used to breach system. Pipeline zero UCs for detecting subsequent escalation from low-priv session to admin roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for administrative privilege grants, role changes, or permission expansions applied to FMC user accounts immediately following successful authentication with low-privileged credentials. Alert on admin account creation, policy-modification grants, or audit-log access elevation from suspicious sessions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Cisco FMC → Managed Firewall Devices
suggestion.rationale: FMC is management plane for Cisco Secure Firewall estate. Article implies sensitive data access. Pipeline zero UCs for detecting pivot from compromised FMC to managed perimeter devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/HTTPS connections from compromised FMC toward managed Secure Firewall devices using FMC service accounts. Monitor for policy deployment, firmware upgrade pushes, or configuration synchronization commands to multiple firewall devices in rapid sequence post-breach.

suggestion.title: LockBit Ransomware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Case 01 – Leaked LockBit builder' and tags include 'Ransomware' as primary threat. Pipeline failed to generate detection for known ransomware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known LockBit signatures, file extension mass-renaming patterns, ransom note creation, and registry modifications associated with encryption activity. Correlate with network exfiltration to identify double-extortion scenarios targeting educational data.

suggestion.title: AnyDesk Deployment via Malicious Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Case 02 – DragonForce deployed via AnyDesk'—explicit use of remote access tool for malware distribution. Pipeline missed detection opportunity for remote-access-mediated execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AnyDesk installation and execution, particularly when initiated from unusual processes (e.g., software deployment tools, email clients). Alert on DragonForce or associated process names executing post-AnyDesk startup. Monitor for network connections to AnyDesk relay servers followed by suspicious child processes.

suggestion.title: Python Keylogger Execution by Insider
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Case 03 – Python keylogger used by an insider'. Pipeline did not surface insider threat detection combining legitimate user context with malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter execution with keylogger imports (pynput, keyboard, pyautogui) or execution of known keylogger scripts. Escalate alerts when executed by accounts with no historical development/IT activity. Correlate with clipboard access, input system APIs, and data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Software Deployment in Educational Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article states machines are 'used by multiple people without accountability', exposing institutions to unauthorized software install. Pipeline missed detection for post-compromise software staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor shared educational workstations for unsigned or suspicious executable creation, particularly in temp directories or system paths. Flag software installation events on machines with elevated user turnover. Correlate with subsequent malware execution or remote access activity.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Credential Abuse via Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'attackers can attempt phishing attacks and impersonate the victims in SIM swapping attacks'—threats enabled by PII data exposure. Pipeline failed to model post-exfiltration attack chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of phishing traffic targeting student/staff PII domains post-incident. Correlate external phishing campaigns with known exfiltrated PII sets (CPF numbers, phone, addresses). Flag SIM-swap attempts linked to compromised identity data from educational breaches.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance by Insider Threat Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights insider threat risk due to diverse user groups and minimal accountability; pipeline must detect reconnaissance by legitimate accounts before lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration commands (net group, whoami, ipconfig) or directory queries executed by educational staff with no IT role. Monitor for unusual network scanning (ping sweeps, port scans) from workstations, particularly those shared across users. Escalate when paired with credential harvesting tools.

suggestion.title: iOS App Installation from Untrusted Source / Sideloading Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates GHOSTBLADE deployment on iOS; no iOS-specific initial-access detection was generated. Typical iOS malware distribution bypasses App Store vetting via phishing, MDM profiles, or sideloading—none captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for iOS app installation outside official App Store channels, MDM profile delivery to managed devices, suspicious Xcode installation flows (DarkSword typically used by actors to repurpose legitimate dev tools for malware). Alert on apps requesting excessive permissions (location, contacts, photos).

suggestion.title: DarkSword Toolkit Execution Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'leaked DarkSword kit' but pipeline generated no toolkit-specific detections. DarkSword is a known iOS exploitation framework; its usage should trigger C2 communication and process-spawning signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: DarkSword typically invokes specific system binaries and establishes non-standard network channels. Look for spawning of `xcode-select`, `swift`, unusual use of `curl` or network APIs with hardcoded C2 domains, and execution of dynamically-loaded iOS frameworks post-installation.

suggestion.title: GHOSTBLADE Malware Indicators of Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Named malware family in article title but zero hash, certificate, or behavioral indicators extracted. Minimum expectation: file hashes, code signing certificates, bundle identifiers, or known C2 sinkhole domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution or installation of apps with bundle IDs or code-signing certs associated with GHOSTBLADE variants. Flag processes spawned by recently-installed third-party apps that attempt to hook system APIs or disable security features.

suggestion.title: Chinese APT Mobile Campaign Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies threat actor as Chinese but no actor name, infrastructure (IPs, domains, ASNs), or historical campaign patterns are captured. Pipeline should surface known APT infrastructure reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network traffic from compromised iOS devices to known Chinese APT C2 infrastructure (previous campaigns, OSINT data, VirusTotal passive DNS). Flag connections to bulletproof-hosting providers, Chinese ISPs flagged for APT activity, or domains registered via known compromised registrar accounts.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via iOS Backgrounding / Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes persistent malware on iOS; no detection for data collection (contacts, credentials, messages, location) or exfiltration patterns were suggested. This is typical for iOS spyware campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for iOS processes requesting repeated access to sensitive APIs (Contacts, Photos, Keychain, Location) especially when backgrounded. Flag unusual DNS queries to exfiltration infrastructure immediately after permission grants or during off-hours. Baseline expected data volumes per app.

suggestion.title: Persistence via iOS Launch Daemons or App Whitelisting Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Malware on iOS requires persistence mechanism but none identified. Article implies sustained compromise; should detect iOS-specific persistence (LaunchDaemons, iCloud Keychain abuse, or app-update hijacking).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: iOS malware often persists via MDM profiles, app-update interception, or Siri shortcuts abuse. Monitor for unusual modifications to system plists in `/Library/Preferences/`, installation of unsigned daemons, or Siri shortcut automation that re-launches suspicious apps after reboot.

suggestion.title: Passkey Authentication Without User Verified Flag
suggestion.rationale: Article description states: 'relying parties fail to validate the User Verified flag, reducing MFA to a single factor.' This is the core attack surface. Detection must flag passkey assertions where UV flag is absent or false during MFA-required flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebAuthn/passkey authentication events for missing or false User Verified flags on accounts configured for MFA. Correlate with successful access to sensitive resources. Establish baseline of per-user passkey assertion patterns to detect anomalous unverified submissions.

suggestion.title: MFA Policy Bypass: Single Factor Accepted as Multi-Factor
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'reducing MFA to a single factor' indicates the attack downgrades authentication strength. Should alert when MFA policy exists but authentication completes with only passkey (one factor).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication events where MFA policy is enforced but only one factor (passkey) is recorded. Compare configured MFA requirements against actual factors used. Flag accounts where passkey alone satisfies MFA policy when second factor should be mandatory.

suggestion.title: Passkey Reuse Across Devices from Anomalous Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article context 'attack surface in passwordless authentication' combined with unvalidated passkey acceptance creates risk of extracted/cloned passkey replay. Multiple uses of same passkey from different geolocations signals compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on same passkey used for authentication from multiple distinct geolocations or unrelated devices within 24 hours. Correlate with unverified passkey assertions to identify exploitation of validation gaps. High-risk if access precedes sensitive operations (data export, privilege elevation).

suggestion.title: Suspicious RCE Against N-central Management Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Attackers Take Over N-central Servers' + 'Initial Fix Proves Incomplete' — indicates successful exploitation and code execution on management infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central service processes for unexpected child spawning, PowerShell invocation, or system utility execution (cmd.exe, whoami, net.exe). Correlate inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to N-central endpoints from untrusted sources with process execution timing.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise on Management Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'take over N-central servers' implies lateral privilege escalation from initial RCE foothold to administrative access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track token impersonation events, UAC bypass attempts, and kernel-mode execution on N-central servers. Monitor for SeDebugPrivilege escalation, suspicious use of icacls/cacls, or indirect process calls from system services.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation on Compromised Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers take over...after initial fix proves incomplete' — re-compromise capability signals persistent backdoor or account-based persistence planted during initial compromise

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Management Plane to Managed Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article implies broad N-central deployment; compromise of central management server creates pivot point to customer-managed systems and agent networks
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP/SSH connections originating from N-central infrastructure to managed customer endpoints outside maintenance windows. Monitor for unexpected agent deployment, script execution, or configuration push to managed systems.

suggestion.title: Discovery of Account and System Inventory Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers take over' — post-exploitation reconnaissance on N-central's account structures and managed customer inventory is standard attacker behavior on management platforms
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for enumeration commands (net accounts, Get-AdUser, ldapsearch, arp, ipconfig) run from N-central service contexts. Monitor LDAP/Active Directory queries over non-standard ports and unusual DNS discovery of customer domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious C2 Beaconing from Management Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers take over' implies persistent attacker access mechanism; management plane compromise likely includes C2 callback or ongoing remote access for re-exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for encrypted outbound connections from N-central servers to rare/new external IPs or domains on non-standard ports. Correlate SSL certificate usage, detect periodic beaconing via network flow analysis, and identify anomalous DNS resolution patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Hard-coded Credential Login Attempts

Flag bulk exports of firewall rules, access-control policies, or threat intelligence feeds by low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Initial Session Establishment via Hard-coded Account

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new FMC management sessions using low-privileged default accounts originating from non-corporate IPs, especially those geolocated to known adversary regions or Tor exit nodes. Alert on simultaneous sessions from the same low-privileged account across multiple source IPs.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post Hard-coded Account Compromise

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Policy Export and Rule Enumeration

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After FMC authentication compromise, flag bulk policy rule exports, configuration backups, or queries to sensitive network zones (DMZ, data-center subnets). Monitor for unauthorized rule export or policy sharing to external IP ranges.
