suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline failed to generate collection-phase detection despite explicit data-access statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting suspicious FMC authentication, baseline file access patterns and alert on bulk data reads, configuration exports, policy downloads, or archive creation. Flag off-hours or high-volume access from compromised low-privilege session.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Firewall Policy Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC grants attacker access to all managed firewall policies and infrastructure. Configuration drift from compromised session is high-impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC change logs for policy modifications (rules, access controls, logging settings) initiated by low-privilege accounts or external IPs. Alert on disabling MFA, modifying admin accounts, or disabling audit logging during suspicious session windows.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — CVE-2026-20316 (Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE: `CVE-2026-20316`'. Pipeline generated no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed Cisco FMC instances on standard ports (8305, 443). Match vulnerability scanner hits against CVE-2026-20316. Alert on unpatched FMC versions visible on internet-facing infrastructure with due date passed (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Logon — Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — this is T1078 exploitation via embedded credentials, not covered by T1190 alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful interactive logon to FMC using default/hardcoded account names (admin, fmcadmin, etc.) from untrusted IP ranges. Baseline legitimate admin logons, alert on deviations. Correlate external IPs + FMC access + sensitive data read in same session.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via FMC Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — FMC is a management plane with visibility into firewall configs, threat intelligence, and network topology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk queries or exports from FMC database after hardcoded-credential logon. Alert on reads of firewall policies, threat feeds, or network topology from low-privileged accounts. Monitor for unusual query patterns (e.g., listing all managed devices, exporting rulesets).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC manages firewalls across infrastructure; compromised FMC is a pivot point to internal assets. Article implies 'systems' (plural) accessible post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH, HTTPS, or API calls from FMC to managed firewalls or internal infrastructure immediately after hardcoded-credential logon. Alert on policy pushes, config reads, or management commands from FMC outside scheduled maintenance windows. Monitor for connections to high-value targets (domain controllers, databases).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Remote Login Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Pipeline generated zero detections for initial exploitation via hard-coded credentials against exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) authentication logs for login attempts from non-administrative IP ranges or external sources. Correlate rapid sequential failed authentication attempts against FMC service accounts, indicative of hard-coded credential brute-force or password-spray attacks.

suggestion.title: Successful Cisco FMC Login with Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes successful exploitation via hard-coded password enabling 'remote attacker to log in.' No use case captures post-exploitation successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC from anomalous IP ranges, geolocation, or outside change-control windows. Baseline known-good admin access patterns; flag logins from cloud/relay IPs or non-corporate ranges. Cross-reference via vulnerability scanner: flag systems running unpatched CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No detection suggested for data collection phase or unauthorized information access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for policy exports, configuration backups, or credential/data extracts initiated by low-privileged accounts or outside normal administrative windows. Flag any bulk data queries or sensitive report downloads by accounts lacking data-access justification.

suggestion.title: Cisco Firewall Management Center Public-Facing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Exploit Public-Facing Application'; implies FMC is internet-exposed. No asset-exposure detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Proactive hunt: scan public IP ranges for exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (typical port 443, SSL certificate fingerprints, banner-grab signatures). Cross-reference against internal CMDB; flag unmanaged, shadow, or unexpectedly-exposed FMC instances requiring emergency remediation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry mandating patch by 2026-08-01; vulnerability scanning is the primary detection vector for passive inventory of affected hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-20316 in Cisco FMC. Correlate with patch management systems and enforce escalation to leadership on same day scanner hits reach NOC.

suggestion.title: FMC External Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—FMC admin interfaces must not be routable from untrusted networks. Standard network segmentation violation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound traffic to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) originating from non-RFC1918 or non-whitelist IPs. Cross-reference with vulnerability scan results. Flag any match for immediate network isolation.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Login to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability'—authentication logs are the primary signal once default credentials become known.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Cisco publishes known hard-coded credentials, create detection rules on FMC auth logs for successful logins matching those patterns. Supplement with velocity analysis: multiple failed logins from one IP followed by success.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Exfiltration from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—must detect abnormal data queries or exports post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for policy export operations, threat intelligence database queries, or configuration backups initiated by low-privileged accounts or from flagged IPs. Baseline normal admin data access patterns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous FMC Admin Access—Geographic & Temporal Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated remote attacker implies geographic anomaly; admin console access should be regionally and temporally stable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enrich FMC admin authentication logs with GeoIP and ASN. Alert on logins from countries outside organizational footprint, TOR exits, or known proxies. Combine with out-of-hours access alerts.

suggestion.title: FMC Network Segmentation Validation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires external reachability; proactive network segmentation audits must confirm FMC isolation from untrusted zones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run network reachability tests from external test hosts to FMC admin interfaces. Alert if any management port responds. Correlate firewall rule audit logs to identify misconfigured ACLs that expose FMC to internet routing.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC on Internet-Routable Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and FMC is described as accessible to 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'. Pipeline generated no UC for the canonical exposure pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC instances (ports 443, 22, or product-specific listeners) visible from untrusted networks via port-scan data, passive DNS, or shodan-style asset inventory. Focus on any FMC with public-routable IPs or accessible from non-datacenter ranges.

suggestion.title: Authentication to Cisco FMC with Hardcoded / Default Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account' via hardcoded password. Pipeline missed T1078 / T1078.001 (Default Accounts / Valid Accounts) entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for successful login attempts from external/unexpected source IPs using known default account names (e.g., 'admin'). Flag successful authentications preceded by failed attempts (brute-force baseline). Correlate with network exposure (UC 1) to prioritize external logins.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Low-Privileged Cisco FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows attacker to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' once authenticated. Pipeline omitted post-authentication data-access phase and corresponding T1005 (Data from Local System) detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a successful login from an external IP with low-privilege account credentials (UC 2), monitor for queries or exports of sensitive data assets (firewall rules, network topology, device configs, threat intelligence). Low-privilege accounts should rarely access such data; any activity is anomalous.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Brute-Force Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded password vulnerability is low-hanging fruit for brute force. Despite CISA KEV status (active exploitation), pipeline generated no brute-force detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on N failed login attempts to Cisco FMC within a time window (e.g., >5 failed logins/min from single IP, or distributed pattern across multiple IPs) followed by success. Baseline normal admin behavior to reduce FP on legitimate access patterns.

suggestion.title: Unusual Outbound Connections from Cisco FMC Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker may pivot or exfiltrate. Article does not explicitly rule out lateral movement or C2. Pipeline missed T1071 or exfiltration-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC instances for outbound connections to non-standard ports, unusual destinations, or high-volume exfiltration patterns after successful login from external IP. Correlate with data-access activity (UC 3) to distinguish legitimate backup/replication from compromise.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Attempts Post-Authentication on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker 'log in to affected device using a low-privileged account'; subsequent escalation to higher privilege is typical next step. Pipeline generated no T1548 or T1134 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a successful low-privileged login to FMC (UC 2), monitor for attempts to escalate privileges (e.g., sudo usage, role/group additions, or direct filesystem access). Escalation from low to high privilege in quick succession is highly anomalous.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication with Hardcoded Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hardcoded password—this is the primary attack vector and should trigger authentication anomaly hunts.
log_sources: Network IDS - Inbound SSH/HTTPS to FMC
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from previously unseen source IPs using the documented low-privileged account. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data indicating unpatched FMC instances. Flag any access from non-management networks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states goal is to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-exploitation data collection must be detectable via FMC data export/query logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authenticated database queries or report generation events from the low-privileged account immediately following successful login. Baseline normal data access patterns for this account and flag deviations in scope/volume.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing FMC Asset Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is exploited 'unauthenticated, remote' and CISA KEV context indicates active wild exploitation—asset discovery/inventory of exposed FMC instances on public IPs is a mandatory hunt.
log_sources: Firewall Edge Logs - Inbound to Management IPs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan your internal IP ranges for FMC management interfaces (Cisco default ports 443, 8305) and cross-reference with egress firewall rules. Identify any FMC instances accessible from untrusted networks or with external public IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version Verification for CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Standard vulnerability management detection—article requires patch due 2026-08-01 and states 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Vulnerability scanner evasion is possible, so direct version queries are needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all known FMC management IPs for installed version via REST API, SSH banner, or SNMP sysDescr. Flag any instances running versions below the vendor's patched release for CVE-2026-20316, even if patch compliance reporting shows compliant status.

suggestion.title: Anomalous FMC Configuration/Policy Export
suggestion.rationale: Following successful login with hardcoded credentials, attacker would likely exfiltrate firewall policies or security configurations from FMC—these are 'sensitive data within the impacted systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for policy export, configuration backup, or device state snapshot operations initiated by low-privileged accounts outside normal maintenance windows. Correlate with file transfer logs or syslog egress to identify data movement.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco FMC Inventory (CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and supplies template guidance at `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`. Substitute 'CVE-2026-20316' into canonical Splunk/KQL templates. Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset management systems for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference against patch-compliance baseline and flag gaps with patch due date 2026-08-01. Prioritize externally-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in…using a low-privileged account'. Pipeline omitted credential-access and authentication-anomaly detection despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful login attempts to low-privileged built-in accounts from remote/untrusted IP sources. Baseline normal administrative access patterns and alert on deviations. Correlate timing and source IPs with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner detections.

suggestion.title: Remote Access to Externally-Exposed FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and implies FMC is internet-accessible. Pipeline failed to generate external-access detection despite clear attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to Cisco FMC management interface (typical ports 443, 8305) from untrusted external IP ranges. Establish whitelist of authorized remote-access sources and alert on new geographies, ASNs, or ISP providers. Correlate with failed/successful authentication and CVE-2026-20316 scanner results.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Extraction via Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Pipeline omitted post-authentication collection/exfiltration detection despite explicit impact described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for policy downloads, configuration exports, sensor/device list queries, or audit log retrieval initiated by low-privileged user accounts. Flag unusual access patterns correlating with externally-sourced authentication or newly-detected CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Brute Force Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—establishes hard-coded credential attack vector requiring detection of repeated auth attempts with known default FMC usernames.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed login attempts to Cisco FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305) using known default usernames ('admin', 'maintenance', 'firesight') from external/unexpected IPs. Post-successful-auth, flag sessions originating outside trusted admin ranges.

suggestion.title: Successful FMC Authentication from External/Unexpected Source
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implies successful remote login is the exploitation artifact; requires detection of valid auth sessions to FMC from non-whitelisted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center from IP addresses not in trusted admin/management network. Correlate with password policy changes, API token generation, or ruleset modifications post-auth.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Compromised FMC Session
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of database queries, config exports, or telemetry collection initiated from a low-privileged FMC account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect database reads or bulk config/policy exports performed by low-privileged Firepower accounts. Flag unusual query patterns to tables containing flow data, device inventory, or credentials. Baseline expected access per role and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: FMC to Internal Network Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC (management appliance with broad network visibility) is a high-value pivot point; article implies 'access sensitive data' could include lateral movement to monitored systems post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FMC typically has broad outbound network access for telemetry. Detect unexpected outbound connections from FMC to internal assets outside its normal management scope (e.g., bulk connections to databases, file servers, or application tiers not in baseline).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Attempt Signature
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV explicitly documents this CVE as actively exploited. Article describes hard-coded password in specific product version; detection requires vulnerability-signature match against exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match inbound traffic to Cisco FMC ports (443, 8305) for exploitation payload signatures or known hard-coded password vectors. Cross-reference asset inventory to identify unpatched FMC versions (pre-patch due 2026-08-01) and alert if internet-routable.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Cisco FMC on Public Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attacker' and 'public-facing application' (T1190 context). FMC should not be internet-routable; detection requires port-scanning/banner-grabbing activity against 443/8305.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port-scan patterns probing Cisco FMC default ports (443, 8305) from untrusted IPs. Flag positive banner responses identifying Cisco FMC/Firepower on internet-facing assets. Correlate with vulnerability data to identify unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repointing to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the core obfuscation mechanism enabling the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags (especially semantic version tags like v\d+.\d+.\d+) are moved to commits not reachable from main/default branch, or moved multiple times within a short window. Cross-reference with concurrent commit creation to detect tag-swap patterns.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Exposure in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs' and 'This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.' Secrets exposure is the impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, API_KEY, and other credential patterns. Alert on non-masked secrets appearing in public logs or secrets output to stderr/stdout without redaction markers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This is the detection signal that surfaced the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound DNS queries or HTTPS connections from GitHub Actions runners to infrastructure not whitelisted for the Action. Flag egress to non-GitHub-owned IPs during build steps, especially from Actions using elevated permissions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Write Access Changes on Popular GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker required 'write privileges on the Action repo' and compromised 23,000 dependent repositories. Access-level changes on trusted repos are prerequisite to supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when new collaborators with write access are added to repositories tagged as GitHub Actions (>1000 dependents, public Actions marketplace listings). Flag temporary access grants or GitHub Apps gaining Action execution permissions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Workflow File Modifications in Dependent Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromised Action version injecting malicious behavior into 23,000 repos' workflows. Detection should surface downstream manifestation: repositories using the Action then exhibit modified workflow files or unexpected step execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Actions that reference tj-actions/changed-files@v35 (or other vulnerable tags) with unexpected workflow step additions, new environment variables, or extra script execution steps added by the Action. Flag when Action execution diverges from its documented behavior in the GitHub Marketplace.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commits in CI/CD Repository with Active Release Tags
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes orphaned commits 'added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack' and describes how attacker created orphaned commits then tagged them. Detection of this pattern flags suspicious repository states.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan git repositories for commits reachable via release/version tags but not reachable from any branch head. Flag as anomalous when such orphaned commits have recent timestamps and are tagged with release semantics (v\d+, or pinned SHAs in .github/workflows).

suggestion.title: JFrog Artifactory Zero-Day Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'JFrog Artifactory Zero-Day'—pipeline extracted zero IOCs or kill-chain phases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Artifactory REST API endpoints for exploit patterns (malformed requests, path traversal attempts, unauthenticated access to internal endpoints). Flag unusual artifact metadata modifications or downloads immediately post-CVE publication.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Model Poisoning via Repository Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'OpenAI Models Exploited' and 'Hugging Face Breach'—pipeline missed model integrity attack vectors
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate artifact repository write events (model uploads, version changes) with downstream consumer pull events. Alert on model weights that diverge from published checksums or appear in unexpected build contexts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised ML Training Pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Breach cascaded from Artifactory to OpenAI—pipeline failed to map cross-system propagation phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ML training job submissions for embedded payload injection or unusual model URLs. Track SSH/RDP access from training infrastructure to external or sensitive systems during model download/initialization.

suggestion.title: Exposed API Credentials in Artifact Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Artifactory zero-day likely leaked embedded API tokens or credentials; pipeline did not flag credential-access phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan artifact repository logs and versioned build configs for embedded OpenAI API keys, HuggingFace tokens, or service credentials. Correlate with external token validation services (e.g., Truffle Hog) for real-time credential detection.

suggestion.title: Malicious Artifact Propagation to Downstream Consumers
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates OpenAI consumed poisoned models—pipeline missed collection/impact for end-user detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on organizations pulling or building with artifacts from compromised JFrog namespace during attack window. Cross-reference artifact versions with CVE disclosure timeline; flag any dependency pull post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Model Weights Exfiltration via Training Job Output
suggestion.rationale: Poisoning attack may include silent exfiltration of training data or competitor models—not detected by pipeline
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ML training/inference jobs for unusual outbound connections to non-whitelisted storage, object stores, or C2 domains. Flag process execution of model serialization/upload tools outside normal deployment windows.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline generated zero detections for this core attack vector. Detection must cover successful login attempts to FMC using default or hard-coded account names from unexpected source IPs or at unusual times.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface (port 8305/8307 HTTPS) for successful authentication events using known default account names (admin, root, support). Establish baseline for legitimate FMC admin logins by IP/time and alert on anomalies. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to confirm FMC instances that have not patched CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: FMC Port Enumeration and Exploitation Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' (T1190) implying network reconnaissance precedes exploitation. Pipeline missed initial reconnaissance phase. Detection should identify port scans or service discovery attempts against known FMC ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connection attempts to FMC management ports (8305, 8307, 443 on FMC hosts) from external IP ranges. Cluster multiple failed connection attempts from single source within short time window. Correlate with known FMC vulnerability exploit traffic signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline generated no detection for data collection or exfiltration phase. FMC contains firewall policies, rules, and security configurations—high-value theft targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk data queries or configuration exports post-authentication. Track large HTTP/HTTPS transfers from FMC servers to external IP ranges. Alert on FMC users performing unusual data queries (e.g., pulling all firewall rules, policy exports, credential lists) especially outside business hours or from new session IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Findings
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry explicitly requiring federal patch compliance by 2026-08-01. Pipeline should generate use case correlating vulnerability scanner results (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) against FMC instances in environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest vulnerability scanner results and flag any FMC instances reporting CVE-2026-20316 as unfixed. Cross-reference with patch management system to identify remediation gaps. Prioritize by exposure: FMC instances accessible from internet-routable networks over internal-only instances. Track compliance with federal patch deadline (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: FMC Remote Access Session Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password enables unauthenticated login but may trigger unusual session behavior. Article phrase 'remote attacker' suggests attacker originates from external network. Detection should flag geographically impossible logins, multiple concurrent sessions, or API calls to sensitive endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate FMC admin session patterns (source IP, login time, session duration, API calls). Alert on: logins from new IP ranges, multiple concurrent login attempts using same account, logins followed immediately by configuration queries, or API calls from default account during off-hours.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Remediation Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output should flag this as CISA KEV (actively exploited, federal due-date 2026-08-01). Generate audit-ready compliance query to identify all Cisco FMC instances and patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference patch management logs for CVE-2026-20316 patches applied before federal due-date. Flag unpatched instances for escalation. Track time-to-remediation vs. federal deadline to support compliance reporting.

suggestion.title: FMC Asset Exposure Hunt — Public Internet Visibility
suggestion.rationale: Article states hard-coded vulnerability affects ability to 'log in to an affected device' remotely unauthenticated. Prerequisite detection: enumerate FMC instances with public IP exposure or DNS resolution. Cited: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies network-reachable instances are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory or network sensors for FMC instances (Cisco ports 443, 8305, 8307) with inbound internet routes or public DNS resolution. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify unpatched instances. Alert if FMC is reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication — Hard-Coded Credential Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Detection must hunt for login attempts using known hard-coded credential patterns (if disclosed) or brute-force attempts followed by success. Cited phrase establishes credential access attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs (typically syslog or internal audit trail) for failed login attempts followed by success using specific low-privileged default accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'cisco' if disclosed). Flag sequences of 5+ failed attempts then success within 5 minutes as brute-force-then-compromise pattern.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access — Post-Compromise Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After credential compromise, threat actor will query or export sensitive data (firewall rules, device inventory, threat intelligence feeds, credentials stored in FMC). This establishes data collection/exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FMC data-access patterns: query frequency, data volume exported, export destinations (local, remote, email). Alert on anomalies: unusual query patterns targeting credentials or firewall rules, large export jobs from new low-privileged accounts, exports to external IPs, failed exports followed by retry loops.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Drift — Post-Compromise Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC instances may be used to alter firewall policies, create persistent backdoors, or add attacker-controlled rules. Article phrase 'access sensitive data' does not preclude attackers also modifying system state. Configuration changes are both persistence mechanism and detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Capture FMC configuration snapshots on a known schedule (daily). Compare snapshots for unauthorized additions: new admin accounts, new firewall rules, modified access controls, altered logging settings. Alert if changes occur outside change-control windows or from unusual source IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Admin Access Anomaly — Lateral Reconnaissance or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: After gaining low-privileged access via hard-coded password, attacker may attempt privilege escalation or enumerate FMC objects (firewall rules, protected networks, connected devices). This establishes discovery and possible escalation phase not explicitly mentioned but implied by 'sensitive data access' objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FMC administrative action frequency (rule queries, device inventory access, user management queries) per source IP and account. Alert on deviations: accounts normally silent suddenly executing queries, queries from unusual geolocations or ASNs, API token generation from low-privileged context, password change attempts for high-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: FMC Patching Status Validation — Patch Lag Risk Quantification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'currently being exploited' (CISA KEV) with federal due date 2026-08-01. Patch lag is the primary risk. Operationally, teams must validate patching across their FMC fleet at fixed intervals (weekly or post-remediation window).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch inventory for all FMC instances. Compare reported version against fixed version (typically published in Cisco advisory). Generate list of unpatched instances with age-of-vulnerability in days. Alert or escalate if any FMC remains unpatched 7+ days after advisory publish date or 3+ days before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Exposed Asset Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Detection in Vulnerability Scanner Results
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry requires immediate remediation. Pipeline should flag any Cisco FMC asset detected as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 by scanner tools (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for CVE-2026-20316 matches on Cisco FMC assets. Verify patch status and compliance against federal due date (2026-08-01, per article). Alert on vulnerable assets; escalate to remediation team with priority=CRITICAL if still unpatched.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability core is a hard-coded password in Cisco FMC. If the credential is publicly disclosed, pipeline should detect login attempts using known default/hard-coded credentials via honeypot, authentication logs, or SIEM correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful or failed login attempts to Cisco FMC using a known hard-coded user account (if disclosed in exploit PoC). Flag any authentication success with that account from IP addresses outside trusted ranges. This is the fastest indicator of active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker...to log in to an affected device.' Requires identifying which FMC instances are externally reachable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances on ports 443, 8305, 8307 with public routing. Cross-reference corporate asset DB; flag unexpected internet-accessible FMC hosts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01.' CISA KEV requires immediate remediation confirmation; patch lag is common attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) for CVE-2026-20316 on FMC assets. Correlate with patch logs to verify Cisco FMC version is patched. Alert on vulnerable instances past federal due date.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication on FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hard-coded password vulnerability...unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Authentication logs expose credential misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts using default low-privileged accounts (admin, readonly, netadmin, etc.) from non-corporate sources. Correlate failed login sprays immediately followed by successful compromise.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FMC Low-Privilege Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Attacker objective is data collection post-credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data queries or API calls from low-privileged FMC sessions accessing security policies, user credentials, firewall rules, or threat intelligence. Flag bulk exports, unusual hours, or non-standard API parameters.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application' exploitation requires prior discovery. Scanning for exposed FMC is prerequisite reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify scanning and probing of FMC management ports (443, 8305, 8307) from external sources. Detect: rapid multi-port SYN floods, SSL/TLS banner grabs, HTTP 401/403 responses to admin URIs, Nmap/Shodan user-agents in access logs.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated remote access attempts to Cisco FMC management interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — this is the primary exploitation vector that requires detection of authentication attempts against FMC exposed on network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated failed and successful authentication attempts to Cisco FMC management ports (typically 8305 HTTPS). Alert on successful remote authentication to FMC with low-privilege account access followed by data access. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability status in asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Detect hardcoded credential exploitation against Firewall Management Center
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' — this necessitates detection of credential-based access patterns using default/hardcoded account identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentications to FMC using known hardcoded account names (vendor-specific defaults) from external network ranges. Flag any low-privilege account accessing administrative dashboards or exporting configuration/data.

suggestion.title: Detect sensitive data access from compromised FMC instance
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — requires detection of data collection activities post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for data exports, policy downloads, credential retrieval, or configuration backups initiated from remote or low-privilege accounts. Alert on bulk exports of firewall rulesets, VPN credentials, or network topology data.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure hunt: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry explicitly requires asset inventory correlation — detection depends on identifying which assets are vulnerable versions of Cisco FMC exposed to remote access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 against Cisco FMC instances. Identify any FMC deployments reachable from untrusted networks (internet-facing, not behind VPN/bastion). Priority alert for unpatched versions with management interface accessible from WAN.

suggestion.title: Detect FMC administrative console access from unusual geolocation or timing
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded credential exploitation typically shows anomalous access patterns — article implies active exploitation in the wild, requiring behavioral baselining.
log_sources: FMC login logs with IP/location metadata
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate FMC administrative access (time-of-day, source IPs, geolocation). Alert on successful logins from new geographies, after-hours, or sources inconsistent with your IT operations team. Correlate with failed-login clusters suggesting brute force or credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Cisco FMC exploitation scanner activity and recon
suggestion.rationale: Article notes this is actively exploited in CISA KEV; recon traffic (port scans, service enumeration) typically precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans targeting known FMC management ports (8305 HTTPS, 8307 HTTPS REST API) from external sources. Alert on probes for Cisco FMC service banners or management interface fingerprinting. Correlate with successful exploitation attempts within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'CVE-2026-20316' and classifies as actively exploited (CISA KEV). Immediate scanner detection is table-stakes for critical vulnerabilities with known federal remediation deadlines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances (FMC / Firepower Management Center) flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 by approved vulnerability scanner. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unpatched appliances requiring immediate remediation per August 1, 2026 federal due date.

suggestion.title: FMC: Unauthenticated Remote Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Baseline FMC authentication patterns and alert on successful login without prior legitimate session state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC appliance authentication logs for successful login attempts originating from external IP ranges or lacking prerequisite session tokens. Hard-coded credential abuse typically manifests as rapid authentication attempts from non-standard sources or geographic anomalies relative to baseline admin behavior.

suggestion.title: FMC: Hard-coded / Low-Privilege Account Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes compromise occurs 'using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. Detection must surface known default or hard-coded credentials being exercised on FMC systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for documented default/low-privilege FMC accounts (e.g., admin, service accounts). Alert on login activity using these accounts during non-business hours, from unexpected geographies, or with immediate lateral escalation attempts. Cross-reference against known FMC CVE-2026-20316 credential disclosures in threat intelligence feeds.

suggestion.title: FMC: Sensitive Data Export / Configuration Bulk Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-exploitation objective is data collection; detect unusual retrieval of policies, configurations, or credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk exports of security policies, device configurations, or authentication data stores. Alert on configuration queries from low-privileged account contexts or unexpected data transfers to external hosts. Correlate with authentication anomalies identified in credential abuse hunt.

suggestion.title: FMC: Network Exposure Detection (Internet-Facing Appliance)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV actively exploited implies public attack surface. Article references 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190). Detection must identify FMC management interfaces exposed to untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal network for FMC management IPs (typical ports 443, 8305, 4989) accessible from public/untrusted IP ranges. Cross-reference against external reconnaissance data (passive scans, Shodan). Alert on any FMC listening on internet-facing interfaces given active exploitation rate.

suggestion.title: FMC: Post-Compromise Privilege Escalation / Managed Device Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Low-privileged initial access implies attacker will escalate to full control. Article does not detail post-exploit steps, but FMC compromise enables takeover of all managed firewall devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC logs for privilege escalation attempts by low-privileged sessions (e.g., admin account creation, role elevation). Alert on security policy changes or access rule modifications to managed firewall devices originating from compromised FMC accounts. Look for unexpected command execution or outbound connectivity from managed devices post-policy changes.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entry requiring asset-exposure hunting with template reference. CVE-2026-20316 is the central vulnerability indicator; no scan-based or version-based detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 via vulnerability scanner results or device telemetry. Flag any FMC instance with version <= patched threshold and network-accessible management interface.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' accessing device, implying management console is externally reachable. No network-exposure or external-access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to Cisco FMC management interface (TCP 443, 8305) from untrusted or external networks. Alert on repeated authentication attempts or failed logins followed by success, indicating exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows login 'using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. No authentication anomaly or default-credential-use detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to Cisco FMC with known low-privileged or default account names (e.g., admin-default, readonly-local). Flag logins from unexpected source IPs or geographies and any account privilege changes immediately after authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within impacted systems' via low-privileged account. No data-access anomaly or privilege-misuse detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect queries or data exports of sensitive configuration, firewall rules, or policy data by low-privilege accounts. Alert on accounts accessing policy objects, rule sets, or logging data they should not have access to.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker,' suggesting exploitation bypasses auth or uses default credentials remotely. No pre-auth or bypass-attempt detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco FMC management endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api/fmc) from external IPs that do not include valid session tokens or auth headers, or that attempt known exploitation paths for CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Compromise Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker access to management center. No post-exploitation persistence or configuration-tampering detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of new user accounts, modification of existing accounts, or firewall rule changes made during or immediately after successful exploitation of CVE-2026-20316. Alert on policy disables or logging disables by default/compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can log in, indicating internet-facing exposure is the necessary initial condition. Missing use case for asset inventory sweep and shodan-style queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances (by IP, hostname, or service banner) reachable from internet on typical management ports (443, 8305). Cross-reference with internal CMDB to flag unexpected internet-routable instances. Correlate with vulnerability scanner reports flagging CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article defines the vulnerability as 'use of hard-coded password.' No detection UC for authentication attempts with known hard-coded/default account credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful or repeated failed authentication to FMC using known hard-coded account identifiers (e.g., admin accounts with manufacturer-default passwords, or CVE-2026-20316-specific credential sets published by Cisco). Baseline: zero attempts in clean environments. Any attempt = escalation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Authentication Data Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' but pipeline missed detection for post-breach activity. After hard-coded credential compromise, attacker would harvest policy, rules, topology, or managed device credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for unusual data export/query patterns immediately after authentication with low-privileged or default accounts: bulk retrieval of access control rules, managed device lists, firewall policies, or configuration backups. Flag especially if followed by SSH/API calls to managed devices.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requirement: correlate scanner vulnerability findings with observed exploitation windows. No UC for vulnerability scanner confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner or external reconnaissance tool identifies CVE-2026-20316 on any Cisco FMC instance. High priority if scanned instance is reachable from attacker-controlled IP or appears in threat feeds. Track time-delta between scanner report and patch; patch lag >30 days post-KEV date = escalated risk.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Managed Device Credential Dump
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password grants access to FMC. Attacker with FMC access can pivot via stored credentials for managed firewalls. Article context: 'access sensitive data' includes stored device credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If FMC is compromised via hard-coded credential, monitor for extraction of managed device credentials from FMC's credential store (API calls like /api/fmc_platform/v1/auth/trusted-certificates or credential query patterns). Cross-correlate with SSH/HTTPS outbound connections from FMC to managed devices using those credentials.

suggestion.title: Successful Authentication to Cisco FMC with Hard-coded Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Successful login using hard-coded credentials is the exploitation vector and must be detectable via authentication logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC management interface from external or anomalous source IPs using low-privileged account names. Correlate with prior failed attempts to detect brute force. Baseline legitimate admin access patterns and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access. Detection must identify publicly-accessible FMC instances (ports 8305, 443) that should only be accessible internally or via VPN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Shodan/Censys API results and external port-scan logs against firewall rules to identify Cisco FMC management interfaces with internet-facing access. Flag any instances accessible from WAN or untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Collection or Configuration Export from Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Once authenticated, FMC can be used to exfiltrate firewall configurations, ACLs, and traffic logs from managed devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual queries, configuration exports, or commands issued through FMC to managed firewalls. Baseline typical administrative activities; flag requests pulling access-control lists, traffic logs, or security policies outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerable Version Detected in Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and warns patch-lag remains exploitable. Asset inventory checks are essential vulnerability management hygiene.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output against asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances running pre-patch versions. Prioritize devices with internet-facing access or confirmed management-interface exposure.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Authentication Attempts Against Cisco FMC Login Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password exploitation often precedes successful login with reconnaissance or brute-force attempts. Article notes attacker is 'unauthenticated' initially, implying trial-and-error or known-credential testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for multiple failed logins from single source IPs within short time windows. Establish baseline of legitimate administrative access and alert on spikes in failed attempts, especially targeting known or generic account names.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-20316 affecting 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center'; pipeline must identify FMC systems running affected versions to meet federal remediation deadline 2026-08-01.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center or legacy Firepower Management Center installations. Extract product version, identify systems matching CVE-2026-20316 affected version range, and correlate with network exposure mapping to flag internet-accessible instances.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication from External IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account'; detection must identify authentication events using known hard-coded credentials if disclosure occurs post-CVE publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts by low-privileged built-in accounts from external/internet-routable source IPs. If hard-coded credential is publicly disclosed, alert on any successful login using that credential, particularly if followed by sensitive data access queries.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privilege FMC Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies compromise grants 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'; detection must track unauthorized data exfiltration after hard-coded credential exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within FMC audit logs, monitor for bulk exports, policy downloads, or certificate/credential extraction performed by low-privilege accounts immediately post-authentication. Flag any configuration backups, threat intelligence database copies, or firewall policy exports that would indicate data staging for exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Cisco FMC Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20316 is exploitable via 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access; requires FMC exposed to untrusted networks to be exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC systems accepting inbound connections on ports 8305 (HTTPS management), 8307, or SSH port 22 from internet-routable IP ranges. Validate against patched inventory; flag any vulnerable FMC instances with internet exposure as critical.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: FMC manages backend firewall appliances; hard-coded credential compromise may enable lateral movement to trust firewalls or device shadow IT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC authentication, monitor for SSH/Telnet/HTTPS connections from FMC to managed firewall appliances with unusual timing or volume. Flag any remote code execution attempts or credential dumping from FMC targeting downstream security infrastructure.

suggestion.title: FMC Policy/Configuration Export for Policy Bypass Planning
suggestion.rationale: Attacker with FMC access can extract full firewall policies and rules to identify egress controls and craft bypass traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for policy export operations, rule database queries, or configuration file access by low-privilege accounts. Correlate with network egress monitoring for large data transfers containing firewall configuration artifacts to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Login with Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — core exploitation method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC from external IP ranges or IPs not in asset inventory. Correlate with failed login attempts immediately preceding success. Flag logins using known low-privilege default accounts or credentials matching published CVE-2026-20316 proof-of-concepts.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise via FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — direct data exfiltration indicator post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for database queries, bulk data exports, or API calls by low-privileged accounts accessing policy data, firewall rules, or credential stores. Baseline expected query volume per account and alert on anomalous departures.

suggestion.title: FMC Firewall Rule Modifications via Unauthorized Session
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC management layer enables configuration tampering — implied lateral movement and persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall rule additions, policy changes, or administrative account creation within 1 hour of a successful FMC login from an unexpected source. Require approval/change-ticket correlation for any rule modifications that would bypass security controls.

suggestion.title: External Access to Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: FMC is management plane; 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access indicates exposed management port (typically 443, 8305). Direct asset-exposure indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all inbound connections to known Cisco FMC management ports from external/untrusted networks. Baseline normal management access sources. Alert on new source IPs, credential spray patterns, or exploit payloads in HTTP/TLS handshake inspection.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Findings
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status mandates vulnerability scanning across exposed infrastructure. 'Vendor: Cisco, Product: Secure Firewall Management Center' — direct product match.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances. Cross-reference with Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 scans for CVE-2026-20316. Do not rely solely on version matching — compare detected product signatures against affected versions. Escalate findings exposed on public or DMZ network segments.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can compromise FMC; requires asset inventory of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances exposed to untrusted networks. No asset-discovery use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances listening on ports 443/8305 (admin, event streaming) from external IPs. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for version detection against CVE-2026-20316 affected builds.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Login Attempts to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' No detection for known default credential testing against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for authentication attempts to Cisco FMC (ports 443, 8305) with known default account names (e.g., 'admin') from external IP ranges. Flag successful authentications; correlate with post-login API calls or file-access events.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Access from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies compromise goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No detection for data exfiltration or sensitive collection post-login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once inside FMC with compromised low-privilege account, attacker accesses sensitive configuration, policy, and telemetry data. Hunt for bulk API queries (e.g., /api/fmc_config/v1/domain/*/devices), policy exports, or database table scans from suspicious sessions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article notes FMC can access 'sensitive data within impacted systems' — implies FMC can pivot to managed firewalls or network infrastructure. No lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FMC-initiated connections to managed firewall devices (ports 8305, 22) or administrative interfaces post-compromise. Flag policy pushes or firmware updates initiated from anomalous sessions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable...it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer' and notes federal due-date requirement. This is the baseline detection for any CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-20316 affecting Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) assets. Correlate scanner results with patch deployment logs to identify systems remaining vulnerable beyond the federal due date of 2026-08-01. High confidence indicator of exploitable asset.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation Against FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes core vulnerability as 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' This is the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305) for successful authentication events lacking corresponding login attempts or user session initialization. Flag authentication succeeding with low-privileged default accounts. Detect failed-to-succeeded login sequences from single source IP over short time window indicative of credential guessing or hard-coded credential exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Access to Cisco FMC Console from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device'—successful FMC management access from untrusted networks is direct attack manifestation regardless of how credentials were obtained.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to FMC management ports from IP addresses outside trusted management networks or from unexpected geolocation. Correlate network flows to FMC with successful login events. Flag sessions initiated without corresponding VPN/bastion host access logs.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Cisco FMC Following Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'to access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Threat is not mere access but data extraction; detection must cover post-compromise collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk export operations on threat intelligence databases, firewall policies, device configurations, or network topology. Flag data exports by low-privileged accounts or during unusual hours. Correlate with unauthorized access alerts from previous UC to detect data extraction post-compromise.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Release Tag Repointing to Malicious Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes core attack: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'the attacker could point people to the malicious commit simply by updating the changed-files GitHub Action code's repo.' Direct supply-chain poisoning via tag manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on tag creation/modification events in high-impact Actions (50k+ dependents) where tag is re-pointed to commits not on primary branch or not descended from previous tag's commit. Flag semantic version regressions (v35 pointing to commit before v34). Correlate with modified action.yml, workflow files, or external network calls in commit.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit in High-Risk Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies orphaned commits as critical obfuscation technique: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' and 'are one of the key enabling factors in exploiting the changes-files GitHub Action workflow.' Orphaned commits are anomalous in maintained projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits reachable via tags or in workflows but not reachable as ancestors of any active branch. Flag commits created then immediately orphaned via branch deletion. For high-impact Actions, inspect commit content for unusual patterns: network calls, shell exec, credential handling, environment variable manipulation.

suggestion.title: Encrypted GitHub Secrets Appearing Plaintext in Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Attack impact directly stated: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This could 'lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Action run logs for unmasked secrets matching known formats (AWS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, PEM PRIVATE KEY, base64 strings >64 chars). Alert especially when secrets logged immediately after Action version update or when env vars printed to stdout. Correlate with recent modifications to action.yml or modified Actions.

suggestion.title: External Code Fetch from GitHub Action Execution Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker technique: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Outbound network calls from Actions bypass static code analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS connections from GitHub Actions runners for curl/wget/git clone to URLs not declared in action.yml dependencies. Flag especially for Actions with large user bases. Cross-reference runner IP/hostname with known GitHub runner infrastructure. Alert on DNS lookups to non-CDN, non-GitHub domains from runner contexts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Write Permissions Granted to High-Impact GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Attack precondition: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo.' Article acknowledges 'it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions,' implying detection of access elevation is critical for defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new user/service principal gaining write/admin permissions on GitHub Actions with 10k+ dependent repos. Flag: sudden commit activity from low-activity accounts, commits bypassing branch protection, new SSH/PAT tokens added to org, commits outside business hours or from unusual geographies, direct pushes bypassing PR review.

suggestion.title: Release Tag Deletion Followed by Re-Creation
suggestion.rationale: Attack obfuscation: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them.' Tag deletion is rare in maintained projects and indicates potential supply-chain manipulation, especially when new tag created immediately after.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect tag deletion followed by tag creation with identical name within same week. Alert if new tag points to commit not in ancestry chain of previous tag (indicates replacement, not update). Flag for Actions following semantic versioning when version numbers decrease or semantics break. Correlate with unusual access patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit, proving network exposure path exists. Article references asset-exposure hunt template but pipeline generated zero use cases for initial_access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 443, 8305) responding from untrusted sources or directly from internet. Cross-reference shodan/censys fingerprints against internal asset inventory. Flag any FMC instance accessible from WAN without VPN gating.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation on FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'. Hard-coded password credential access phase completely missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins from external IPs using low-privilege built-in accounts. Flag patterns of repeated failed attempts followed by sudden success. Detect anomalous authentication source geography for known hard-coded or default account names.
