suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-18577 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends substituting this CVE into the asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline generated no scanner-based detection despite this clear directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability management systems for N-able N-central instances flagged with CVE-2026-18577. Alert on any unpatched systems discovered after the 2026-08-06 federal remediation deadline. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify internet-exposed instances in compliance-critical environments.

suggestion.title: Authentication bypass exploitation against N-central
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' as the core attack mechanism. Pipeline failed to generate behavioral detections for this exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central authentication logs for bypass patterns: requests to non-standard auth endpoints, successful logins preceded by failed attempts to alternate channels, auth success from never-before-seen source IPs, or rapid authentication attempts followed by account activity.

suggestion.title: Account takeover post-bypass activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows for authentication bypass and account takeover.' Pipeline missed the post-compromise detection phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful auth-bypass exploitation, detect account takeover via: unauthorized credential resets, API token generation by dormant accounts, privilege escalation or role modifications, or lateral movement patterns from formerly inactive service accounts.

suggestion.title: Incomplete patch correlation: CVE-2026-18556 residual risk
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556.' Systems patched for the prior CVE but still vulnerable to the new one indicate incomplete remediation and residual exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate systems with patch history showing CVE-2026-18556 remediation but vulnerability scanner reporting CVE-2026-18577 as unpatched. Flag for mandatory re-patching as this indicates the vendor's prior fix was incomplete.

suggestion.title: Federal remediation SLA enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-06' and explicitly notes 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors/regulators.' Compliance drift is a detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate escalating alerts for N-central instances unpatched at 48-hour, 24-hour, and 0-hour marks relative to 2026-08-06 federal due date. Correlate with ticketing and compliance systems to flag organizations out of remediation SLA.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repointing to Orphaned Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Changing existing release tags to point to the attack commit' and 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit.' Direct persistence mechanism enabling widespread supply-chain exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect release tags being modified to point to commits not on default branch or with no branch ancestry. Alert on tags (esp. v-numbered releases) consolidating to same recent commit, or tags moving to newly-created commits outside established release workflows.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Supply-Chain Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' as 'one of the key enabling factors' for hiding malicious code. Attackers specifically created branch-less commits to evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits created in high-value repositories (Actions, SDKs, dependencies with >1k downstream consumers) that never merge to any tracked branch. Especially if preceded by tag updates or associated with unexpected principal write access.

suggestion.title: Secrets Leakage via GitHub Actions Log Plaintext Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs...could lead to a devastating breach.' Attacker exploited Action logging to exfiltrate repository secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Action run logs containing values matching configured repository secrets (by pattern or regex) in plaintext. Correlate with modified Actions code or recent version changes in jobs that reference secrets.

suggestion.title: External Code Download from GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Network egress from Actions is detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions for outbound network calls to non-GitHub domains, especially wget/curl in Action logs or GitHub Runner network egress. Flag downloads of shell scripts or binaries during workflow execution.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Tag Modification by Single Principal
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'relocated them [tags] to the malicious commit' across multiple versions and 're-pointed several existing release tags...thereby deepening the attack's impact.' Coordinated bulk tag changes indicate malicious activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >3 release tags modified within 1 hour to point to same commit hash, especially if tags move backward in history or to commits outside master/main. Alert on consolidation patterns typical of supply-chain poison attempts.

suggestion.title: Write Access Grant to External Principal on Critical Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Prerequisite enabling all subsequent attacks: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo' and 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Access control failures in supply chain are detection priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on write permission grants (push, admin, maintain roles) to repositories with >5k external dependencies. Flag if grantor is compromised account or if access precedes unusual commit/tag activity. Correlate with credential compromise signals.

suggestion.title: SFTP session initiation without successful password authentication, followed by file access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'SFTP accepts connections without password.' No existing UC validates that file operations occurred *after* an unauthenticated session. Requires SSH/SFTP auth log correlation showing failed or absent credentials, then immediate file I/O.
log_sources: SSH/SFTP authentication logs (syslog, auth.log, goshs debug output)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SFTP connections to goshs where the SSH session was established but authentication failed, was skipped, or used empty credentials; followed within 10 minutes by file creation, modification, or deletion by the goshs process. Cross-reference session IDs or source IP + destination port tuples to confirm causality.

suggestion.title: Public-IP SFTP connection without password prompt completion, rapid file operations
suggestion.rationale: UC_103_3 correlates file ops post-SFTP but doesn't explicitly verify the session bypassed auth. Article states the vulnerability requires no auth—hunt must detect sessions that complete connection without completing password handshake, then perform reads/writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TCP connections from public-class IPs to port 22 (or custom SSH port) on systems running goshs, where connection is Accepted, but SSH protocol handshake is incomplete (no successful KEX or auth frames observed in proxy/WAF logs), yet file system modifications by goshs follow within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Repeated `-b` flag variants in process execution, indicating CVE-2026-62325 / -40884 scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article notes CVE-2026-40884 fixed empty-username `:pass`, implying attackers may probe multiple variants. No hunt explicitly detects sequential launches of goshs with different empty-credential configurations (empty user, then empty pass) suggesting vulnerability scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events for goshs where `-b` flag appears in two or more commands from same source within 10 minutes, with different empty-credential patterns (e.g., `-b ':password'` followed by `-b 'user:'`). May indicate active probing for known auth-bypass variants.

suggestion.title: goshs SFTP server restart or configuration change post-compromise (indirect indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes starting goshs with vulnerable flags. Hunt should detect goshs process lifecycle events (startup, restart) with `-sftp -b` and absence of `-fkf`, especially if preceded by any suspicious activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag goshs process creation with `-b` containing empty username or password and `-sftp` enabled, without `-fkf` remediation flag. Correlate with timestamp to detect if restart occurred after suspected intrusion window (based on UC_103_3 file ops timeline).

suggestion.title: N-central Public Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes N-central as a public-facing application subject to T1190 exploitation. Pipeline produced no asset-exposure hunt despite CISA KEV implying active scanning by adversaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for N-central service listening on internet-facing interfaces. Check DNS resolution logs for N-central FQDNs. Correlate with authenticated session logs to identify instances reachable unauthenticated. Focus on default management ports (8040, 20000, or vendor-documented ports).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Alternate Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'—the core attack step. Pipeline omitted any detection for lateral or alternate authentication paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication requests to N-central endpoints that succeed despite prior failed attempts or that bypass standard /login paths (e.g., direct API calls, undocumented endpoints, request smuggling patterns). Look for session tokens issued without credential validation in auth logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Account Takeover Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'account takeover'—the impact once bypass succeeds. No use-case targets post-authentication anomalies (privilege escalation, mass account creation, lateral commands).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a successful bypass (identified via timestamp correlation with bypass-channel UC), flag account creation, role escalation, or bulk data access by compromised accounts. Pivot on N-central session tokens appearing in lateral-movement tooling (RDP, SSH, C2).

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Verification (CVE-2026-18556 vs 2026-18577)
suggestion.rationale: Article states this CVE is 'the result of an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'—organizations may have patched 18556 but remain vulnerable to 18577. Pipeline missed this regression-hunt signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch-management and vulnerability-scanner logs for instances where CVE-2026-18556 remediation date is logged but CVE-2026-18577 remains unpatched. Flag N-central deployments at versions ≤ [vendor-specified patched version] as still exploitable.

suggestion.title: DNS Configuration Tampering on Captive Portal Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers manipulate DNS and HTTP traffic on networks served by captive portal equipment, allowing them to intercept user connections.' This is the initial access vector and should trigger detection of DNS settings modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized changes to DNS server addresses or forwarding rules on captive portal equipment and network infrastructure devices. Alert on simultaneous DNS modification across multiple hotel/conference Wi-Fi APs, indicating centralized compromise rather than isolated device failure.

suggestion.title: Phishing Page Hosting for M365 Credential Harvest and Device Code Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'redirect victims to phishing pages that impersonate Microsoft 365 login portals, or to device code phishing pages that abuse Microsoft Entra ID authentication flows.' No detection guidance despite this being the primary credential vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device code authentication flows initiated from guest Wi-Fi networks with IP addresses in hospitality subnets. Alert on M365 logins from phishing domains with legitimate-appearing subdomains (e.g., account-verify-ms365.com); correlate with captive portal redirection timestamps.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Delivery from Fake Update Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fake browser and operating system update pages that deliver malware to Windows via ClickFix prompts.' Explicit execution mechanism that should generate process-creation and file-write detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads and subsequent execution triggered by ClickFix popups appearing on non-HTTPS or self-signed certificate pages. Alert on msiexec.exe, explorer.exe, or powershell.exe spawned immediately after fake Chrome/Windows Update page visits from captive portal networks.

suggestion.title: CornFlake Multi-Mechanism Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: CornFlake 'uses multiple persistence mechanisms on the host, including Windows service registrations, registry run keys, named tasks, and a watchdog routine designed to restore any of the available persistence mechanisms.' Multi-layered persistence deserves specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on simultaneous creation of Windows service, registry run key, scheduled task, and watchdog process with matching binary paths or hashes. Detect 'Cloud Sync Service' service name creation lacking valid Microsoft code signature; monitor for watchdog process recreating deleted persistence artifacts.

suggestion.title: Microsoft 365 and Azure AD Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: CornFlake performs 'Microsoft 365 session token theft' and ChocoShell targets 'Microsoft 365 and Azure AD tokens.' Token theft is the primary attack objective but no detection guidance provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-browser processes accessing browser memory or token cache directories (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials). Alert on M365/Azure AD tokens used from IP addresses or geographies inconsistent with victim's normal login patterns within 24 hours of CornFlake execution.

suggestion.title: FruitStone C2 Panel Outbound Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'an unprotected web-based management panel named FruitStone that the threat actor used to handle infected systems, browse victim files, execute PowerShell commands, and capture screenshots and keystrokes.' C2 communication is the control plane but no network detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS outbound connections from compromised hotel guest machines to FruitStone infrastructure (domain/IP TBD). Correlate with execution of powershell.exe with token/credential-stealing arguments and file access patterns to %AppData% directories.

suggestion.title: Sequelize Oracle queries with TO_DATE/TO_TIMESTAMP in application logs (CVE-2026-69240 execution trace)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The escape function defined in sql-string.js does not escape quotes if the value starts with TO_TIMESTAMP or TO_DATE.' Application-level query logs (if Sequelize is instrumented with DEBUG=sequelize*) would show the exact malicious query before it reaches Oracle. This is the smoking gun for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js application logs for Sequelize dialect=oracle mode and extract queries containing TO_DATE or TO_TIMESTAMP prefixes followed by unterminated string literals, quote characters, or SQL keywords (||, OR, UNION). Flag queries where the value portion deviates from standard ISO-8601 date formats.

suggestion.title: Oracle data exfiltration queries post-TO_DATE/TO_TIMESTAMP SQLi (CVE-2026-69240 impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1565.001 (Stored Data Manipulation) but omits detection of successful exploitation outcome. After injection, attacker can query SELECT * FROM sensitive_tables; this is the impact phase missing from hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Oracle queries (no syntax errors) originating from Sequelize connection pool with TO_DATE/TO_TIMESTAMP prefixes in the preceding error logs. Look for: (1) spike in SELECT queries from app service account over 5-minute window, (2) queries against non-standard tables not in whitelist, (3) result-set sizes anomalously large for app baseline.

suggestion.title: Node.js process crash or restart correlated with SQLi probe patterns (CVE-2026-69240 evasion detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article's UC_2_5 detects Oracle errors, but doesn't account for attacker behavior when queries fail—re-try with mutation, or abandon process. Node.js app crashes when Oracle returns repeated syntax errors. Monitoring for (probe pattern → crash → restart) is an evasion signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences where: (1) HTTP request arrives with TO_DATE/TO_TIMESTAMP + SQL operators, (2) Oracle audit log shows ORA-00911/ORA-01858, (3) Node process restarts or core dump within 30 seconds, (4) same client IP retries within 2 minutes with mutated payload. Pattern indicates iterative SQLi fuzzing.

suggestion.title: Oracle administrative queries from Sequelize application user account (CVE-2026-69240 privilege escalation attempt)
suggestion.rationale: Article's UC_2_2 and UC_2_5 detect syntax errors and data queries but miss the escalation scenario: attacker injecting queries to read SYS tables or execute DBMS_* procedures (Oracle dynamic SQL). This is post-exploitation reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the Sequelize application user's normal query surface (typically simple SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on app schema). Alert on: queries to DBA_* or SYS.* tables, calls to DBMS_SQL or DBMS_SYSTEM, attempts to read data dictionary views, or changes to user privileges—if source is the app user, this is injection.

suggestion.title: Sequelize version downgrade or sql-string.js file replacement in node_modules (CVE-2026-69240 post-compromise artifact)
suggestion.rationale: If Sequelize is patched or reverted by an attacker to an earlier vulnerable version (or vice versa), file-timestamp anomalies in node_modules are detectable. Article mentions the vulnerable version (6.37.3) but doesn't hunt for rollback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node_modules/sequelize/sql-string.js for: (1) modification timestamp regressing to earlier date than expected, (2) file size or hash mismatch with known-good version from package-lock.json registry, (3) write operations from process other than npm/yarn/node installer. Compare file content against upstream GitHub to detect tampering.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-69240 web scanner or exploitation tool invocation (CVE-2026-69240 reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: Article does not suggest detection of pre-exploitation recon tools (SQLmap, Burp, etc.) probing for Sequelize+Oracle+TO_DATE vulnerability. This is initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: HTTP User-Agent strings associated with SQLi tools (sqlmap, Burp Suite, AcuNetix) OR process execution of known exploitation frameworks on the same host running Node.js, OR repeated HTTP requests with permutations of TO_DATE/TO_TIMESTAMP injection payloads within short window (e.g., 10 requests/minute). Correlate with absence of corresponding legitimate business activity.

suggestion.title: Steganographic Payload Extraction from Browser Cache
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'the command searches the browser cache for the PNG based on its exact file size and uses the findstr or certutil commands to recover and execute the hidden first-stage payload inside the image.' This is a recoverable, multi-signal behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or cmd.exe spawning findstr or certutil with arguments targeting browser cache directories (e.g., 'findstr /S /C:' against %LocalAppData%\[Chrome|Edge|Firefox]\Cache or AppData\Local\Temp). Correlate with access to .bin or .tmp files of specific file sizes, followed by base64 decode or deobfuscation patterns. High confidence if followed by in-memory process creation.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Smart Contract Reconnaissance for C2 Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states DeviceManager 'uses blockchain smart contracts to determine the IP address of its command-and-control server' via EtherHiding. Outbound connections to Ethereum/Polygon infrastructure are anomalous for typical enterprise hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS or TLS connections from non-browser processes to Ethereum mainnet nodes (e.g., infura.io, alchemy.com, etherscan.io) or Polygon RPCs. Look for DeviceManager.exe or related Python processes connecting to contract addresses on port 443. Correlate with subsequent C2 traffic to newly resolved IPs within seconds of contract queries.

suggestion.title: DNS-based RAT Command & Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The RAT uses DNS A and TXT records to steal system information, retrieve commands to execute, download payloads, and send command output back to the attackers.' DeviceManager uses DNS as a covert channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalously high volumes of DNS TXT record queries from a single process in short time windows (e.g., >50 lookups/min). Look for query patterns like subdomain enumeration (e.g., <encoded_data>.<attacker_domain>.com) or base32/hex-encoded hostnames. Correlate with known DeviceManager process names or Python interpreter spawned with suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Clipboard-to-PowerShell Command Execution via ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article describes DOUBLECUP 'copies it to the clipboard when the page is opened' and instructs victims to 'paste and run a command automatically copied to their clipboard.' Clipboard reads followed by execution are recoverable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or cmd.exe reading from system clipboard (via Get-Clipboard, xclip, or WinAPI) within 5 seconds of a browser tab becoming active. Especially high confidence if clipboard contains encoded payloads, 'certutil', 'findstr', or other file manipulation strings. Secondary signal: PowerShell execution with -Command or -EncodedCommand immediately after clipboard access.

suggestion.title: Fake SaaS Portal ClickFix Iframe Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code loaded through embedded iframes' on 'fake CAPTCHA prompts on login pages impersonating NetSuite, Odoo, HubSpot, and Salesforce.' Iframe-based redirects to CAPTCHA pages are detectable at proxy/CDN layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP responses containing <iframe> tags pointing to domains not whitelisted for the destination site (especially on login.*, signin.*, auth.* paths). Correlate with domains impersonating Salesforce, HubSpot, Odoo, NetSuite (e.g., salesforce-verify.com). Secondary: Monitor for inline JavaScript on these pages that manipulates clipboard or forces image downloads to cache.

suggestion.title: In-Memory Payload Execution Following Hash Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes dropper behavior: 'After verifying the decrypted payload against a hardcoded SHA-256 hash, the dropper executes it in memory.' Hash computations followed by memory-only execution are distinctive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect second-stage droppers (likely fileless PowerShell or native binaries) computing SHA-256 hashes of in-memory buffers, then spawning child processes without corresponding on-disk executables. Look for patterns like certutil -hashfile, Get-FileHash, or similar hash operations followed by RunPE/hollowing. High fidelity if process tree shows parent as cmd/powershell with no legitimate installer context.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Java Payload Execution (decompiler.exe Variant)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'launches an obfuscated Java payload disguised as decompiler.exe.' Pipeline generated no execution-layer detections for the second-stage malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for java.exe or javaw.exe spawning processes named decompiler.exe, or JAR/Java payloads launched from temp/AppData/Downloads directories. Flag processes loading JRE before executing suspicious child processes or reading local configuration files.

suggestion.title: Browser Profile Credential and Cookie Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Steals browser data including cookies and other stored user data from Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi.' No collection-layer detection for browser database access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-browser processes accessing %LOCALAPPDATA%\[Chrome|Edge|Brave|Opera|Vivaldi]\User Data directories, particularly Local State, Cookies, or Login Data files. Correlate file reads with network exfiltration or compression activity.

suggestion.title: Exodus Cryptocurrency Wallet Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Steals cryptocurrency wallet data, with dedicated functionality targeting Exodus Wallet.' Pipeline missed wallet-specific credential theft detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious processes reading %APPDATA%\Exodus directories, accessing wallet.dat, keystore files, or JSON configuration containing private keys. Flag process access outside of legitimate Exodus application context.

suggestion.title: Keylogger and Input Capture Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article lists: 'keylogging, mouse activity logging, screenshot capturing, desktop streaming, and webcam access.' Pipeline generated no collection detections for input capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious processes hooking keyboard/mouse APIs (SetWindowsHookEx), calling screen capture functions (GetDC, BitBlt, D3D), or creating video files in temp/AppData. Flag processes with no visible window accessing input devices.

suggestion.title: First-Stage Loader JRE Runtime Extraction Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The payload checks for a Java Runtime Environment, and extracts one if necessary, then reads a local file containing the validation keys for the attackers' command-and-control (C2) server.' Distinctive staging behavior should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables from suspicious locations (temp, Downloads, AppData) that check JRE presence, extract or download Java components, and subsequently read obfuscated configuration files or C2 keys before spawning secondary payloads.

suggestion.title: Discord and Roblox Account Credential Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Targets online accounts and payment data, including Discord, Roblox, Minecraft, Microsoft Store tokens, and payment information.' Pipeline missed platform-specific credential theft patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious processes accessing Discord token storage (%APPDATA%\Discord), Roblox client data, Minecraft launcher metadata, or MS Store credential caches outside of legitimate application contexts. Correlate with network exfiltration attempts.

suggestion.title: SonicWall SMA 1000 Remote Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'exploiting SonicWall SMA 1000 flaws'—this is the core initial-access vector. Pipeline generated no detection rule for exploitation attempts despite being the dominant attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SonicWall SMA 1000 remote-access portal for HTTP requests containing known CVE payloads, abnormal response codes, or authentication bypass attempts. Alert on administrative-session creation immediately following malformed requests or crash-recovery cycles.

suggestion.title: INC Ransomware Process Execution and Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'INC Ransomware' but pipeline extracted zero execution-phase detections. Ransomware payload must execute post-exploitation; no use case covers process spawning, service creation, or scheduled-task persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation from SonicWall appliance context (unexpected cmd.exe/powershell spawning from system32, DLL sideload patterns). Correlate with known INC ransomware hashes and behavioral signatures (high-frequency file writes, registry enumeration for volume info).

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption Activity: Mass File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names ransomware but no impact-phase use case detects encrypted-file patterns or ransom-note staging. Encryption events are the most observable ransomware artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file-extension changes to .INC (or INC-associated extensions), rapid file-modification timestamps across multiple directories, and appearance of ransom-demand files in critical shares. Alert on sequential write-close patterns typical of encryption loops.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from SonicWall to Internal Hosts
suggestion.rationale: SonicWall SMA 1000 is an edge appliance; successful exploitation enables pivot into internal networks. Title suggests 'dominant actor' impact across infrastructure—lateral spread should have detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected internal traffic from SonicWall appliance, then alert on anomalous port-scanning activity, RDP/SSH brute-force from appliance context, or SMB enumeration toward domain resources. Correlate timing with initial-access indicators.

suggestion.title: INC Ransomware C&C Beacon and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware must communicate with C&C for key exchange or negotiation infrastructure. Pipeline extracted zero network IOCs despite ransomware groups typically publishing C&C domains or payment portals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference INC-known C&C domains and negotiation portals published in threat intel. Alert on DNS queries or HTTPS connections to known INC infrastructure originating from compromised SonicWall. Monitor for TOR/proxy traffic during encryption phase indicating exfiltration.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18577 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'CVE-2026-18577' as the canonical identifier and notes CISA KEV status implies active exploitation. Pipeline produced zero IOCs despite this being the primary detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) against CVE-2026-18577. Alert on any N-able N-central asset matching this CVE, regardless of reported patch status (patch lag is common for CISA KEV items).

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Public Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass' for a product used for remote access/monitoring. Phrase 'T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application' implies network exposure. Pipeline missed asset-inventory hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for N-able N-central instances reachable on TCP 443 and 8080 (default ports) from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify out-of-policy exposure. Correlate with proxy/firewall logs for sustained access attempts.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' This describes a specific attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit exploitation method disclosed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central application and web server logs for requests to non-standard authentication endpoints or unusual HTTP methods (PUT/DELETE to auth routes). Alert on successful auth responses from requests that should fail (e.g., missing credential headers, unexpected URL paths like /api/v1/auth-bypass or /alternate-login).

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Post-Compromise Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'allows for authentication bypass and account takeover.' Pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation access indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-authentication, hunt for suspicious admin API calls, credential changes, or lateral movement commands executed via N-central console. Alert on: mass privilege escalation, new user/group creation by compromised accounts, unusual asset targeting in RMM commands.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 Incomplete Patch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes CVE-2026-18577 is 'the result of an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556.' Pipeline missed this related CVE as a complementary scan target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Expand scanning to include CVE-2026-18556 alongside CVE-2026-18577. Assets showing remediation for CVE-2026-18556 but not yet patched for CVE-2026-18577 are high-priority (demonstrates patch lag and incomplete vendor fixes).

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Deadline Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-06.' Pipeline produced no compliance or deadline-tracking use case, yet federal agencies must remediate by this date and auditors will correlate to this deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any N-able N-central asset still unpatched for CVE-2026-18577 as of 2026-08-06. Correlate with patch windows and change logs to identify systems where patches were attempted but failed or reverted.

suggestion.title: N-central Asset Exposure and Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of N-central instances; attackers must first discover exposed management interfaces via port scanning and service fingerprinting before attempting auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for network scanning activity targeting N-central default ports and HTTP banners. Correlate scanning patterns with unpatched N-central asset inventory. Look for service discovery probes (version strings, management console fingerprints) from external sources.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel allows for authentication bypass and account takeover'—direct detection requirement for non-standard auth endpoint abuse.

suggestion.rationale: Article highlights caching mechanism as delivery vector; no UC generated. Pipeline should flag execution from browser/system cache directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect binary execution from Windows cache directories (%AppData%\LocalLow, %temp%, %windir%\temp) especially non-standard executables or double-extensions. Alert on process creation where parent is a browser or legitimate utility loading from cache.

suggestion.title: Detect N-able N-central RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'exploited' and customers are compromised. Pipeline failed to generate detection for exploitation phase despite CISA KEV listing. Attack phrase: 'Exploited N-able N-central Flaw' and 'Customer Compromises' establish active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central services (typically n-central.exe or related processes) for abnormal spawning of command shells, script interpreters, or network listeners. Alert on HTTP(S) requests to N-central admin interfaces with unusual verb patterns (PUT/DELETE vs. GET) or rapid sequential API calls indicating automated exploitation.

suggestion.title: Detect N-central Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Customer compromises imply successful RCE execution. Article states active breach occurred but pipeline generated zero execution-phase detection. Critical gap for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process execution originating from N-central parent processes or from SYSTEM context where N-central typically runs. Look for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe spawned with suspicious arguments (encoded payloads, registry modifications, service creation).

suggestion.title: Detect N-central Credential Harvesting and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: RMM/MSP platforms like N-central store customer credentials and access multiple systems. Article mentions 'customer compromises' suggesting lateral movement occurred post-exploitation. No detection generated for this critical post-breach activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate N-central service account usage across multiple remote systems and external IP ranges. Alert on credential access patterns (registry reads for stored creds, LSASS access, SAM reads). Flag N-central initiating new RDP/SMB sessions to customer infrastructure outside established baselines.

suggestion.title: Monitor N-central Configuration and Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Customer compromises on RMM platforms typically involve persistence mechanisms. Article states ongoing compromises but pipeline missed persistence-phase detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central installation directory for unauthorized file modifications (scheduled tasks, startup folders, DLLs). Alert on Registry modifications under HKLM\Software\N-able or startup paths. Track persistence through N-central's native scheduling or task execution features.

suggestion.title: Hunt for N-central Service Account Abuse Across Customer Tenants
suggestion.rationale: MSP breach context: compromised N-central provides access to ALL customer environments. Article implies systemic impact ('customer compromises' plural). Pipeline failed to suggest cross-tenant hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for N-central service accounts authenticating to multiple customer-owned systems outside scheduled maintenance windows. Correlate account usage across administrative interfaces, file shares, and command execution endpoints. Flag bulk reconnaissance (WMI queries, net view commands) using compromised service credentials.

suggestion.title: Detect N-central Backup/Data Exfiltration Activity
suggestion.rationale: N-central stores customer data, credentials, and configurations. Customer compromise implies data access. Article provides no IOCs or exfil detection, critical gap for MSP breach impact assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central database export/backup processes for unusual volume or frequency. Alert on large data transfers from N-central server to external/attacker infrastructure. Detect suspicious queries against credential vaults or configuration databases with results written to external locations.

suggestion.title: DNS Hijacking on Hotel Captive Portal Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers manipulate DNS and HTTP traffic on networks served by captive portal equipment, allowing them to intercept user connections.' This is the initial compromise vector requiring infrastructure monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hotel/conference Wi-Fi captive portal appliances for DNS configuration changes, particularly modifications redirecting *.microsoft.com or *.live.com to attacker-controlled IPs. Alert when DNS responses from captive portal devices resolve legitimate Microsoft authentication endpoints to non-Microsoft IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Phishing Redirects Impersonating Microsoft 365 Login Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'redirect victims to phishing pages that impersonate Microsoft 365 login portals, or to device code phishing pages that abuse Microsoft Entra ID authentication flows.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect redirects from captive portal landing pages to URLs mimicking login.microsoft.com, outlook.live.com, or device.login.microsoftonline.com. Flag HTTP POST requests to fake auth endpoints with Microsoft 365 credentials; correlate with abnormal login geo-locations from hotel networks.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Delivery via Fake Browser/OS Updates
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'using fake browser and operating system update pages that deliver malware to Windows via ClickFix prompts for user verification' and evidence of APK delivery targeting Android.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious .exe and .apk downloads from captive portal domains. Alert on ClickFix campaign signatures (fake CAPTCHA or verification prompts requesting elevated privileges). Correlate suspicious file downloads with fake OS/browser update pages hosted on hotel Wi-Fi infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Windows Service Persistence Masquerading as 'Cloud Sync Service'
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals CornFlake 'disguises itself as Cloud Sync Service to appear as a legitimate Windows component' using 'Windows service registrations' with 'a watchdog routine designed to restore any of the available persistence mechanisms.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of Windows service named 'Cloud Sync Service' or similar masquerading names. Flag service binaries copied to %AppData%\* instead of System32. Monitor for watchdog processes that auto-restart services or registry persistence keys following deletion attempts. Correlate service installation with suspicious initial compromise timestamps.

suggestion.title: Multi-Mechanism Redundant Persistence Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states CornFlake uses 'multiple persistence mechanisms on the host, including Windows service registrations, registry run keys, named tasks, and a watchdog routine' — a behavioral signature of sophisticated persistent malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple persistence artifacts on single host within short timeframe: (1) registry HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entry, (2) scheduled task creation with suspicious action/trigger, (3) Windows service installation, (4) automatic service restart behavior. Alert with high confidence if all four mechanisms present within 60 minutes on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Microsoft 365 Token Theft via In-Memory PowerShell Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article details ChocoShell as 'in-memory PowerShell credential stealer that targets browser cookies, saved passwords, Microsoft 365 and Azure AD tokens, and Wi-Fi credentials' — post-compromise credential exfiltration behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell execution from %AppData% or temporary directories accessing Credential Manager, browser profile folders (AppData\Local\Google\Chrome, etc.), or DPAPI-protected token cache. Alert on in-memory PowerShell operations without corresponding .ps1 file on disk. Correlate with anomalous Microsoft 365 API token refresh requests or Entra ID sign-in anomalies from infected host.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Phishing with Embedded CAPTCHA Overlay
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fake CAPTCHA prompts on login pages impersonating NetSuite, Odoo, HubSpot, and Salesforce, with the malicious code loaded through embedded iframes.' Core attack pattern—zero UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect iframes with suspicious domains on legitimate authentication pages. Monitor for CAPTCHA-like HTML overlays injected via JS. Alert on mismatched CSS classes or DOM elements appearing in credential-submission contexts.

suggestion.title: Browser Cache Steganography Extraction via certutil/findstr
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'browser to download and cache a malicious PNG image' then 'findstr or certutil commands to recover and execute the hidden first-stage payload inside the image.' Classic defense-evasion pattern absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on certutil with -decode or findstr targeting user profile cache paths (AppData\Local\). Detect suspicious PNG file access by non-browser processes. Flag child process spawning from browser with system utility invocations against cache locations.

suggestion.title: Fileless Dropper with Public IP-Derived Decryption Key
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'first payload launches a fileless second-stage dropper, which retrieves the victim's public IPv4 address and uses it to create a decryption key for the final encrypted payload.' No fileless or decryption-based execution UC surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process queries to public IP services (ipify, checkip) followed by crypto function calls. Monitor for memory-only payload execution with hardcoded SHA-256 validation. Alert on processes calling decryption APIs with network-derived key material.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: CountLoader 'establishes persistence through scheduled tasks.' Standard persistence mechanism—completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor schtasks.exe or New-ScheduledTask spawned from suspicious processes. Detect tasks scheduled with random names, PowerShell payloads, or paths in user temp/AppData directories. Alert on startup/logon triggers from non-system processes.

suggestion.title: macOS LaunchAgent Persistence with System Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'installs a LaunchAgent for persistence and uses built-in utilities such as curl, sw_vers, system_profiler, and ioreg to communicate.' macOS-specific persistence and recon chain—no detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect plist creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents with suspicious binaries. Monitor for rapid sequential calls to system reconnaissance utilities by non-standard processes. Alert on LaunchAgent modifications via curl or script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Ethereum Smart Contract Query for C2 Resolution (EtherHiding)
suggestion.rationale: Article: DeviceManager 'uses blockchain smart contracts to determine the IP address of its command-and-control server' via EtherHiding technique. Novel C2 pattern—no detection UC exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ethereum RPC nodes (infura.io, alchemy.com, rpc.ankr.com) from suspicious processes. Flag web3.js library imports or smart contract function call patterns. Monitor for hard-coded contract addresses in malware samples.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Java Process Masqueraded as decompiler.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states first-stage loader 'launches an obfuscated Java payload disguised as decompiler.exe'—direct process masquerading indicator. Key phrase: 'disguised as decompiler.exe, which performs environment checks, registers the victim, and downloads the final malware payload.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Java.exe or javaw.exe processes spawning or renaming to decompiler.exe, or decompiler.exe with Java runtime properties. Correlate with parent process xeno.exe. Look for obfuscated command lines or suspicious working directories.

suggestion.title: Xeno Executor Process Chain with Java Subprocess
suggestion.rationale: Article describes execution flow: 'Once victims launch xeno.exe... they actually run the first-stage malware loader. The payload checks for Java Runtime Environment... then launches an obfuscated Java payload.' Direct attack chain indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on xeno.exe spawning Java process (java.exe, javaw.exe) or renamed variants. Suspicious when xeno.exe is found outside legitimate Roblox modding directories. Correlate with archive extraction activity (7-Zip, WinRAR from temp/downloads).

suggestion.title: Browser Cookie and Credential Theft from Multiple Engines
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'Steals browser data including cookies and other stored user data from Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi. Targets online accounts and payment data, including Discord, Roblox, Minecraft, Microsoft Store tokens.' Multiple browser processes accessed in succession.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process accessing Chrome/Edge/Brave AppData\Local\[Browser]\User Data\Default\Cookies or Cookies-wal. Cross-reference Java-based or unknown parent process. Alert on reads to Discord, Roblox cache/token paths. Look for sequential browser database access.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet File Access from Suspicious Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions: 'Steals cryptocurrency wallet data, with dedicated functionality targeting Exodus Wallet and support for identifying numerous other cryptocurrency wallets.' Wallets are well-known file paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any non-wallet process accessing AppData\Roaming\Exodus, AppData\Local\Coinbase, or %APPDATA% paths containing wallet database files. Alert on reads combined with network exfiltration. Correlate with xeno.exe or Java subprocess.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Java Process with Webcam or Audio Capture API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article lists surveillance capabilities: 'Provides surveillance capabilities, including keylogging, mouse activity logging, screenshot capturing, desktop streaming, and webcam access.' Java-based RAT requesting media device access is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Java.exe or decompiler.exe attempting access to camera/microphone APIs (WinMM, DirectShow) or requesting privacy-sensitive capabilities. In Windows 11+, correlate with camera/mic privacy logs. Flag when these requests originate from process trees starting with xeno.exe.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution from Java-based Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states final RAT 'Enables full remote control, allowing attackers to... execute PowerShell commands.' Java process invoking PowerShell is strong C2 indicator and privilege escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe or pwsh.exe spawned from Java.exe or decompiler.exe. Enable PowerShell command-line logging; inspect for obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads. Correlate with network connections to unknown external IPs.

suggestion.title: Git Hook File Creation or Modification Detected in Gitea Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE mechanism: 'repository writers plant a git hook.' Any creation or modification of files in .git/hooks/ directories is a direct indicator of this attack. Pipeline failed to identify this core persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification events targeting .git/hooks/* paths within Gitea repository directories. Establish baseline of legitimate hook activity (deployment automation, CI/CD); escalate any out-of-band modifications. Include content inspection for shell metacharacters and command sequences.

suggestion.title: Shell Process Spawned from Git Hook Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes shell command execution via git hooks. Detection must trigger when bash/sh/cmd.exe is spawned as child of git processes or from .git/hooks working directories—the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where git or Gitea-related processes spawn shell interpreters. Flag cases where git hooks trigger command execution with suspicious arguments: reverse shells, network utilities (curl/wget with exfil patterns), privilege escalation commands, or base64/encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Permission Granted Followed by Hook Modification and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'repository writers' as the attack prerequisite. Detection should correlate Gitea permission changes with subsequent .git/hooks modifications and git operations—the full attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Gitea permission grant events (user added to repository with write/push permissions) with subsequent .git/hooks file modifications and git command execution within narrow time window. Alert on non-developer accounts or service accounts performing this sequence, especially with unusual timing or frequency.

suggestion.title: Gitea Web Process Executing Native Shell Commands Without Subprocess Control
suggestion.rationale: Git hooks execute in the context of the Gitea application process or git daemon. Gitea spawning bash/sh directly is abnormal—indicates hook exploitation or compromised git integration. Pipeline failed to map this execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell process children of gitea, git, git-daemon, or Gitea SSH service processes. Establish baseline of legitimate subprocess patterns (expected CI/CD hook outputs). Alert on unexpected shell spawning, especially with environment variables suggesting attacker-controlled input (branch name, commit message, hook script path).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Hook Content Scan Before Execution
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires injecting malicious shell commands into hook files. Detection should inspect hook file content for command injection patterns before execution occurs—proactive defense against the stated attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan .git/hooks/* file contents for suspicious patterns: shell command chaining (;, |, &&, ||), network utilities in command args (curl, wget, nc, telnet), credential exfiltration (env vars, /etc/passwd, AWS keys), privilege escalation syntax (sudo, chmod, setuid), or obfuscation (base64, hex encoding, variable expansion). Correlate with developer identity and known CI/CD workflows.

suggestion.title: Gitea Version or CVE Detection for RCE Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'new Gitea RCE'—implies specific CVE. Pipeline must identify affected Gitea versions and detect exploitation attempts. Version discovery and vulnerability scanning are foundational to SOC response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of Gitea deployments with version tags. Cross-reference against Gitea CVE database for RCE vulnerabilities. Monitor HTTP responses containing Gitea version strings; alert on instances running vulnerable versions. Watch for HTTP requests to known exploitation endpoints (if CVE details specify).

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path or Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel allows for authentication bypass.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central for authentication requests using non-standard URL paths, deprecated API endpoints, or authentication channels not matching documented flows. Alert on successful authentications that bypass multi-factor authentication or originate from atypical networks.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Account Takeover in N-central
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact as 'account takeover in N-central' but pipeline generated zero use cases for post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid privilege escalation of newly-authenticated accounts, mass password resets on privileged users, creation of backup admin accounts, or sensitive permission changes occurring within minutes of successful authentication bypass.

suggestion.title: Unpatched N-central Asset Inventory: CVE-2026-18577
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-08-06; article body references 'asset-exposure hunt' template but pipeline generated zero inventory use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-18577 and the related incomplete patch CVE-2026-18556 across N-central appliances. Flag instances vulnerable post-deadline 2026-08-06. Cross-reference with patch deployment logs to identify failed patches or systems evading compliance.

suggestion.title: N-central Auth Bypass — HTTP 401→200 Transition
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel allows for authentication bypass' — requests bypassing standard auth flow return 200 instead of 401.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 401→200 sequences to the same N-central endpoint within 5s from same source IP, without intervening standard authentication, indicating bypass via alternate channel.

suggestion.title: N-central Unauthenticated Admin API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes auth bypass enabling 'account takeover'; API endpoints should reject unauthenticated requests but do not.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to N-central /api/* endpoints from external IPs lacking Authorization header, JWT token, or valid session cookie.

suggestion.title: N-central Managed-Asset Lateral Movement Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: N-central manages remote customer assets; auth bypass enables downstream system compromise via the RMM platform as part of the account takeover chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate N-central auth-bypass indicators (unauthenticated API calls, 401→200 patterns) with remote-management commands (RDP/SSH/RMM protocol) to customer systems within 10m window.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-18556 (Predecessor Vulnerability)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556' — older flaw remains exploitable in partially-patched environments; both CVEs must be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for exploitation patterns matching CVE-2026-18556 (predecessor auth bypass). Alert on requests containing known trigger signatures; essential for detecting incomplete patches.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Account Creation in N-central
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows for account takeover' — attackers typically establish persistent admin accounts post-bypass for long-term access and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on N-central admin-level account creation outside change windows, created by service accounts, or appearing in logs but missing from audit trails.

suggestion.title: N-central Vulnerable Instance Inventory (CISA KEV Compliance)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV protocol and federal directive (patch deadline 2026-08-06) require asset-exposure inventory of all N-central instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-18577.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for N-central versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-18577 (pre-patch versions); cross-check against internet-facing IP scan results to identify exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18577 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>' and 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Vulnerability scanner detection is the primary control for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for CVE-2026-18577 in N-able N-central installations. Alert on any unfixed instances with federal patch due date 2026-08-06. Verify patch version against CVSS base score to eliminate false negatives from incomplete patches.

suggestion.title: N-central Public-Facing Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article characterizes this as 'exploit public-facing application' (T1190) requiring external attacker access. Must identify internet-routable N-central instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify N-central instances exposed to untrusted networks via asset management or network scanning. Monitor firewall/WAF logs for inbound connections to N-central default ports (typically 443) from external IP ranges. Cross-reference with unpatched vulnerability scan results.

suggestion.title: Alternate Authentication Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability as 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'. This describes the actual attack mechanism and requires detection of non-standard auth attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central authentication logs for requests to non-standard login endpoints, debug interfaces, or maintenance accounts. Detect exploitation signature: failed standard authentication attempts followed immediately by successful login via alternate mechanism from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Post-Bypass Success
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows for...account takeover in N-central'. Takeover is the direct business impact requiring post-exploitation monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account takeover by monitoring N-central for anomalous account activity post-successful auth-bypass: unusual login geography, privilege escalation, API token generation, or credential modifications. Correlate with infrastructure team alerts on newly-created admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised N-central
suggestion.rationale: N-central is an RMM platform. Compromise of the management console grants access to all managed endpoints, enabling lateral movement at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual N-central management agent activity post-takeover: unexpected agent deployments, mass remediation actions, or privileged commands sent to large endpoint populations. Detect traffic from N-central to managed systems for command execution or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch (CVE-2026-18556) Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes this CVE is an 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'. Organizations with only the older patch applied remain vulnerable despite believing they are patched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems with CVE-2026-18556 patch applied but lacking CVE-2026-18577 patch. These systems have false-positive patch status and are exploitable. Flag in vulnerability reports as high-risk incomplete patches.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass — Alternate Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for bypass patterns. Need to hunt for HTTP parameter tampering, unexpected authentication endpoints, or API calls bypassing normal login flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central ingress for requests to non-standard authentication endpoints, unusual HTTP verbs/headers on login paths, or parameter manipulation (e.g., bypass tokens, alternate channels). Flag authentication attempts that skip normal 2FA/MFA flows.

suggestion.title: Post-Auth Account Takeover — N-central Unusual Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states outcome is 'account takeover.' Pipeline missed post-exploitation phase. Once attacker obtains valid session, need to detect lateral movement and privilege escalation within N-central management console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-successful auth bypass, hunt for anomalous N-central API calls (unusual agent deployments, policy changes, credential dumps from managed systems). Correlate successful auth bypass exploits with subsequent privilege escalation or cross-system lateral movement.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18577 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry for 'actively exploited' vulnerability. Pipeline failed to generate basic asset-exposure UC. Federal agencies have patch-due date 2026-08-06; enterprises need immediate exposure scan.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-18577 and CVE-2026-18556 matches. Correlate unpatched N-central deployments with outbound egress to known N-able update servers (patch lag indicator). Flag unpatched instances exposed to internet.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Regression — CVE-2026-18556 Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article notes CVE-2026-18577 is 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556.' Pipeline missed the attack-chain implication: defender patched #1, attacker found workaround. Need to hunt for attacks exploiting patch-bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for N-central auth requests matching historical CVE-2026-18556 exploit signatures, then succeeding via alternate vector (e.g., different HTTP header, API version). Signals attacker tested old exploit, pivoted to new bypass.

suggestion.title: N-central Lateral Movement Post-Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Once account is hijacked, attacker gains N-central agent management permissions. Article does not detail post-exploitation, but N-central provides deep system access. Pipeline missed detection for anomalous agent commands, policy pushes, or credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-auth takeover, monitor N-central console for unusual agent deployment commands, reverse-shell payloads pushed to managed systems, or credentials harvested from managed endpoints. Correlate N-central admin sessions with downstream process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: Brute Force or Credential Enumeration Against N-central
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass' but does not exclude credential brute-force as attack precursor. Pipeline missed pre-exploitation reconnaissance: attacker may enumerate valid accounts before exploiting auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for high-volume failed N-central login attempts from single source IP, followed by successful bypass exploits or unusual auth patterns. Flag credential-stuffing campaigns targeting N-central appliances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18577 Patch Compliance & Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV status and federal due date 2026-08-06. Pipeline should have generated standard asset-exposure hunt (referenced in article: '_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure') with this CVE substituted, as article instructs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline all N-able N-central deployments. Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for unpatched or partially-patched instances. Flag gap between CVE-2026-18556 (original flaw) and CVE-2026-18577 (incomplete patch) in patch history, as article warns incomplete remediation remains exploitable.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows for authentication bypass and account takeover'. Pipeline missed the defense-evasion and credential-access phases implied by alternate auth path exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central auth logs and network logs for requests bypassing normal login flow: direct API calls to sensitive endpoints without valid session tokens, malformed auth headers, or requests to alternate authentication paths. Correlate with failed login attempts followed by successful privilege escalation within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Compromised N-able N-central Management Console
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables 'account takeover'. Compromised N-able accounts are high-value for lateral movement and persistence across managed endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for lateral movement patterns: privileged account logins from N-able management server IP ranges; mass password resets initiated via N-able; credentials harvested from N-able vault/secrets store; or lateral connections (SMB, WinRM, RDP) from N-able server to critical assets immediately following authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Detection (CVE-2026-18556 vs. CVE-2026-18577)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-18577 is 'result of an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'. Pipeline missed this dependency; systems patched for prior CVE remain vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch history: flag N-able N-central instances where CVE-2026-18556 remediation is logged but current version is below the CVE-2026-18577 fix version. These systems are likely vulnerable due to incomplete prior patch, as article warns.

suggestion.title: N-central CVE-2026-18577 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states bypass 'allows for authentication bypass and account takeover' via 'alternate path or channel.' This is the primary attack vector and must be hunted in perimeter and application logs for exploitation attempts matching T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central endpoints for HTTP requests to alternate authentication paths that bypass normal login flows. Look for path traversal sequences, double-encoded characters, or requests to non-standard authentication URIs (e.g., /admin, /api/auth/bypass, /login?admin=1). Correlate with successful session creation lacking corresponding failed-auth events.

suggestion.title: N-central Account Takeover Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states bypass enables 'account takeover in N-central.' Post-exploitation, threat actors pivot to lateral movement or privilege escalation. Detect anomalous account activity immediately following successful bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly-authenticated N-central accounts with zero prior login history, accounts accessing administrative dashboards in first session, or sessions initiating outbound connections to managed endpoints within minutes of authentication. Correlate session-creation timestamps with exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing N-central Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV and T1190 ('Exploit Public-Facing Application') imply N-central exposure on perimeter. Inventory internet-facing installations against federal patch deadline 2026-08-06 for prioritized remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for N-central management interfaces (ports 8000–8080, 443, 5900 typical). Flag externally-reachable instances running unpatched build dates or lacking 2026-18577 patch metadata. Alert on any still-vulnerable installations at/past federal deadline.

suggestion.title: N-central Lateral Movement via Compromised Agent
suggestion.rationale: N-central is a centralized remote-management platform. Account takeover via auth bypass enables command execution across managed endpoints, triggering T1021.001 (Remote Services) lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-bypass, monitor N-central agent processes for spawning powershell.exe/cmd.exe with unusual arguments, establishing outbound connections to non-standard ports, or modifying scheduled tasks on managed endpoints.
