Detect mass policy deployments, agent configuration changes, or host modifications by newly-elevated accounts within 6 hours of suspected bypass timestamp.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Regression: CVE-2026-18556 Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-18577 'is the result of an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'. Organizations that patched only the original CVE remain vulnerable. Pipeline ignored this dual-CVE risk entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems with patches applied for CVE-2026-18556 but running N-central versions still vulnerable to CVE-2026-18577. Flag as incomplete remediation and escalate for immediate re-patch.

suggestion.title: Pre-Deadline Exploitation Surge (2026-08-06 Federal Due Date)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides federal patch due date of 2026-08-06. Exploitation intensity typically spikes in 48–72 hours before compliance deadlines as threat actors prioritize unpatched assets before automated remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline exploit attempt frequency for CVE-2026-18577 post-KEV publication. Alert on 3x+ deviation above baseline during 72-hour window before 2026-08-06. Any N-central instance without patch evidence by due date is immediate escalation candidate.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: CVE-2026-18577 Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-18577 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and mandates federal patch due 2026-08-06. Pipeline generated zero scanner-based hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all N-able N-central instances flagged with CVE-2026-18577. Confirm patched vs. unpatched status. Alert on any unpatched fleet members given patch-lag risk noted in article.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Public Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. No external-facing detection provided by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all N-able N-central management interfaces exposed to untrusted networks or internet. Cross-reference with patched inventory to prioritize exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path or Channel
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly described as 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'. Pipeline provided zero detection for this attack vector despite it being the vulnerability mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central logs for successful authentications via non-standard paths, undocumented API endpoints, or bypass-associated parameter patterns. Detect requests to deprecated authentication channels.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Account Takeover Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability results in 'account takeover'. Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized admin actions following authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for administrative credential creation, policy modifications, mass device deployments, or lateral-movement commands issued post-breach from N-central management accounts.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Exploitation (CVE-2026-18556 Regression)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability is 'the result of an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'. Pipeline did not surface the predecessor CVE or re-exploitation of 'patched' systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems patched for CVE-2026-18556 but running N-central builds with incomplete patches. Hunt for exploitation attempts targeting 'already patched' systems to detect regression.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Retargeting to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Changing existing release tags to point to the attack commit' and 'orphaned commits' as the core obfuscation mechanism. Phrase: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect tag re-pointing operations where a release tag (e.g., v35) is moved to a commit that has no parent branch association or exists outside the default branch history. Flag if tag changes occur outside normal release windows or by unexpected actors.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exposure in GitHub Actions Build Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Phrase: 'This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for patterns matching common secret formats (AWS keys, tokens, API keys, SSH private keys) that appear unencrypted. Correlate with known GitHub Secrets rotations to identify leaked credentials.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Detection with Suspicious Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attacker specifically created orphaned commits ('Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch') as obfuscation. Phrase: 'These factors added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify commits with no parent branch that are subsequently tagged with release versions or referenced in Actions workflows. Orphaned commits should be rare in legitimate repos; any associated with v-tags or Action pinning warrant review.

suggestion.title: Unexpected External Network Calls from GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article notes detection mechanism: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections initiated during GitHub Actions job execution to non-whitelisted external endpoints. Flag egress to newly-registered domains, suspicious IP ranges, or outside the organization's vendor allowlist.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Write Access to High-Impact GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Foundational attack enabler: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo.' The attacker exploited existing write access to a repo with 23,000 downstream dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new contributors gaining write access to high-dependency repositories (detect via repository stars/forks/dependents count). Monitor for commits authored by unexpected accounts or from unusual geolocation/time patterns on critical Actions repos.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Version Pinning Drift to Orphaned or Retargeted Tags
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation pattern: users pin to v35, attacker re-points v35 tag to orphaned malicious commit. Phrase: 'The critical bit is the very last line, where a particular tag of the GitHub Action repo is referenced.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when an Action tag version (e.g., v35) referenced in workflows begins executing code substantially different from prior runs (diff commit hash, new outbound calls, new env vars), indicating tag re-pointing. Compare Action SHA pre/post tag update.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18577 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to 'CVE-2026-18577 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs, including the CVE ID itself, which is the foundational detection mechanism for this KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all N-able N-central instances matching CVE-2026-18577 in scanner output. Cross-reference patch dates against instances last updated before 2026-08-06 to identify systems with known lag. Correlate with CVSS 9.8 criticality to prioritize hunt queues.

suggestion.title: N-central Alternate Authentication Path Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' This is the core exploitation mechanism but pipeline mapped no credential_access phase or non-standard auth flow detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central authentication logs for logins arriving via non-primary channels: direct API calls with auth, LDAP/SAML bypass attempts, or requests to undocumented authentication endpoints. Alert when MFA is bypassed or skipped on successful logins.

suggestion.title: N-central Account Takeover Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'allows for authentication bypass and account takeover.' Pipeline omitted all impact-phase detections for unauthorized account control post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account takeover via behavioral anomalies: first successful login to account in 30+ days, login from new geolocation, immediate privilege escalation attempt, or rapid bulk operations (user creation, policy modification, credential rotation) following initial auth.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Detection (CVE-2026-18556 Follow-up)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'—implies systems patched for the earlier CVE but not updated to the full fix remain exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify N-central instances with patches applied for CVE-2026-18556 but running versions below the full CVE-2026-18577 fix. Flag as 'regressed' or 'partially patched' and escalate for immediate remediation against the Aug 6 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: N-central Pivot and Lateral Movement Post-Takeover
suggestion.rationale: N-central is a centralized remote management platform. Account takeover enables lateral movement to managed endpoints. Article does not detail post-compromise flow but article text 'account takeover' implies pivot risk that pipeline did not map.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After account compromise, monitor for unusual N-central management operations: bulk agent policy pushes, mass endpoint configuration changes, deployment of new management tasks to large groups, or execution of commands across multiple managed systems.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'—the pipeline must detect requests to non-standard N-central authentication endpoints or parameter manipulation indicative of path traversal to auth logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central web logs for requests to alternate authentication URIs or parameter sets (e.g., /login.aspx, /auth.php, /api/auth via unusual paths). Detect HTTP 200 responses following failed authentication attempts. Alert on successful login from IP+user after multiple 401/403 responses on non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: N-central Account Takeover Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allows for authentication bypass and account takeover'—hunters must identify logins immediately after bypass exploitation, particularly lateral movement or privilege escalation actions by the hijacked account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful login to N-central with immediate anomalous actions: new credential creation, group membership changes, or lateral movement attempts. Flag logins from IPs not previously associated with that user or outside business hours if the account is an admin.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18577 Incomplete Patch Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes this is 'the result of an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'—post-patch validation must confirm N-central instances have reached vulnerable versions ≥ [X] that re-introduced the flaw after the prior incomplete remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference N-central version inventory against known-vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-18577. Flag any instances that patched CVE-2026-18556 but remain ≤ patched version that re-introduced CVE-2026-18577. Alert on missing or rolled-back security patches.

suggestion.title: N-central Admin Escalation Post-Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of N-central (a remote management platform) via authentication bypass is high-value for lateral movement. Detection must capture privilege escalation or sensitive actions by newly-compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-risk N-central actions (add remote access, push commands, modify client policies) by non-privileged or newly-active accounts within hours of login anomalies. Detect outbound RDP/SSH/WinRM from compromised N-central instance to internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-18556 vs CVE-2026-18577 Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Article references both CVE-2026-18556 (original flaw, incomplete patch) and CVE-2026-18577 (the re-introduced flaw). Detections must disambiguate which version is being exploited, as patch guidance differs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If vulnerability scanners flag CVE-2026-18556 only, investigate whether the scanner is outdated or if the instance patched CVE-2026-18556 but remains vulnerable to CVE-2026-18577. Require explicit version confirmation from software inventory; Splunk correlate CVE IDs in scan output with patch history.

suggestion.title: CSV file upload with prompt injection payload to Flowise CSV Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'A prompt injection sent to a chatflow using a CSV Agent node ca[uses RCE]'—the vector is CSV content with LLM prompt injection syntax. Pipeline should detect file operations for .csv upload followed by suspicious CSV content patterns (newlines with command keywords, comment markers with shell/Python syntax).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST to /api/v1/prediction with multipart/form-data containing .csv file where CSV content includes newline-delimited injection payloads, comment rows with SQL/shell commands, or escaped quotes followed by Python/shell keywords. Correlate with subsequent process spawning from node context within 10 seconds.

suggestion.title: Pyodide WebAssembly Python runtime loading system/subprocess modules
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates RCE leverages pyodide (JavaScript-accessible Python WASM runtime). Exploitation requires importing 'subprocess', 'os', or 'sys' modules within Flowise context. Pyodide module loads appear as specific JavaScript events or runtime initialization patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For sandboxed JavaScript/WebAssembly execution contexts (Flowise CSV Agent runs in pyodide), hunt for import/require calls to system modules (subprocess, os.system, sys) or evidence of module loading in Node.js memory/heap. Correlate with parent process being node/flowise and preceding CSV POST request.

suggestion.title: Flowise LLM model inference with untrusted external CSV data
suggestion.rationale: CSV Agent uses LLM model to interpret CSV headers/content. Prompt injection works by crafting CSV data that breaks LLM prompt structure. Detection should focus on data flow: untrusted input (CSV) → model inference → code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated rapid requests to Flowise prediction endpoint with varying CSV content (polyglot payloads), followed by child process spawning. The attack chain is request → LLM processing → code generation → subprocess execution; cluster on user/IP and correlate POST request count with new process creation count in short window.

suggestion.title: Node.js child process execution with inherited Python/shell runtime from parent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE where Flowise (Node.js app) spawns Python or shell commands. The inherited environment and parent context (flowise) is key discriminator from other Node apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell or Python interpreter spawned by Node.js process with Flowise in parent command line, where child process executes immediately after HTTP request (delivery latency < 5s). Flag cases where env vars contain FLOWISE_PATH or child inherits parent's working directory in /node_modules/flowise.

suggestion.title: CSV Agent node configuration exfiltration or data access post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: After establishing RCE via prompt injection, attacker can access Flowise configuration, database credentials, chat history, or API keys stored in chatflow. Article doesn't detail post-exploitation but implies full code execution → full access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE indicators: spawned shell reading ~/.flowise config, accessing SQLite database files, reading environment variables (FLOWISE_AUTH_TOKEN, API keys), or exfiltrating via curl/wget in child processes from node parent.

suggestion.title: Flowise prediction endpoint access without valid session or rate spike
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires POST to /api/v1/prediction. Normal Flowise usage follows authenticated session patterns. Scripted/automated attack from external tools (python-requests, curl, httpx) without prior auth session or credential establishment is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag prediction endpoint requests from IPs/user agents with no prior login/auth events, or unusual request rate (>10 predictions/min from same source). Combine with presence of suspicious user agents (python-*, curl, Go-http-client, httpx) and look for requests originating from VPS/datacenter IP ranges or Tor exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Ransomware File Encryption Activity Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack aimed to deploy ransomware payload before isolation — encryption or file modification patterns are the defining behavioral signature of impact phase that should trigger detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid bulk file creation, modification, or deletion with suspicious extensions (.encrypted, .locked, ransom note markers). Cross-correlate with process handles to encryption-capable binaries (certutil, wmic, PowerShell encryption cmdlets). Flag when event volume exceeds baseline by >10x in <60s.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Payload Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'multi-stage attack' — should detect sequential child-process spawning, in-memory execution, or staged script interpretation typical of ransomware droppers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process chains with >3 generations originating from network services or Office processes. Flag PowerShell/CMD with suspicious encoded arguments. Alert on unsigned or recently-created DLLs loaded by legitimate processes.

suggestion.title: Endpoint Isolation Trigger (Defender Automated Response)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes automated isolation in 129 seconds — should detect and alert on Defender-initiated network isolation, device quarantine, or remediation actions as early-warning indicator of active threat detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Microsoft Defender isolation events (network disconnect, process termination, remediation). Correlate isolation timing with preceding suspicious activity within 2-minute window. Generate alerts on automated Defender response to enable incident response triage.

suggestion.title: Service Disruption / Security Software Termination
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage ransomware typically attempts to disable security controls before encryption payload deployment — article's 129-second timeline suggests Defender caught this during defense-evasion phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process termination or service stop attempts targeting windows defender (WinDefend, MsMpEngine, etc.), backup services (VSS, NTBACKUP), or EDR agents. Correlate with elevated privilege use and network isolation timing.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Unpatched or Exploited Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Incident begins with 'compromised endpoint' — should profile attack surface: what was the entry vector (RDP, unpatched service, phishing, supply-chain)?
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous inbound RDP sessions from unknown IP ranges, authentication failures followed by success from same source, or failed exploit attempts (CVE patterns in HTTP/network logs). Correlate with OS/application patch status.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement or Persistence Mechanism Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes payload attempted to 'persist or spread' — should detect mechanisms used to maintain access across reboots or propagate to other hosts (scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions, registry run keys, network shares).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of scheduled tasks, registry run/runonce keys, or startup folder entries by process spawned from suspicious parent. Detect WMI event consumer registration. Alert on SMB share enumeration or lateral movement probing (wmic process list, enum shares).

suggestion.title: Malicious CSV Data URI posted to Flowise CSVAgent endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as: 'csvFile data URI base64 segment is interpolated into Python source without validation.' Initial access requires attacker-controlled input sent to Flowise API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests to Flowise endpoints containing 'csvFile' parameter with base64-encoded or data: URI payloads, especially those containing Python syntax (e.g., 'import', '__import__', 'eval', 'exec'). Correlate with subsequent process spawning from Node.js.

suggestion.title: Python code injection detected in Pyodide runtime bridge
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability states: 'interpolated into a Python source-code template that is then executed.' Pyodide js bridge with globalThis exposure allows Python→JavaScript→OS command chaining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Node.js processes loaded with Pyodide module spawning Python subprocess or executing eval()-like patterns. Look for 'eval', '__import__', or similar high-risk Python keywords in HTTP request payloads to Flowise within seconds of unexpected process spawning.

suggestion.title: Flowise Node process with unexpected child interpreter spawning (behavioral)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE leading to OS shell invocation. Under normal operation, Flowise should not spawn shells; spawning is artifact of post-compromise code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Flowise-identified Node.js process (check process command line or parent-child for 'flowise' keyword) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, or other interpreters within 0-5 seconds of unusual network ingress (large POST body, base64 content, unusual headers). Baseline legitimate Flowise behaviors first.

suggestion.title: Base64 data URI in HTTP request body to Flowise, followed by process tree explosion
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector is 'base64 segment' in data URI. Detection should chain HTTP payload inspection with endpoint behavioral response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST requests containing 'data:' URI scheme and base64 encoding (regex: 'data:[^;]*;base64,') to Flowise csvFile endpoint with a spike in process-spawning events (5+ new processes within 2 seconds) from the Flowise Node process.

suggestion.title: JavaScript escape-sequence or Python string-breakout payload in csvFile parameter
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is: attacker 'can break out of the Python string literal, hand a JS string to...' Thus payloads will contain Python string-delimiter escapes or JS exec patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Use regex/yara to detect payloads in csvFile parameter containing Python string-escape sequences (e.g., '\'""', '\"\\n'), triple-quote breaks ('"""'), or JavaScript eval/Function keywords. Correlate with non-200 responses or subsequent error logs from Flowise.

suggestion.title: Pyodide js module interop—OS bridge function calls
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'full OS command execution on the Flowise host via Pyodide's js module interop.' No UC detects the bridge between Python and JavaScript execution. Should monitor Pyodide runtime or process traces for js.eval(), js.sys, or subprocess equivalents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flowise Python execution that reaches into Pyodide's js module to call system-level functions or spawn processes. Look for subprocess calls or os.system equivalents originating from within Pyodide runtime context, or JavaScript eval payloads containing shell metacharacters.

suggestion.title: validatePythonCodeForDataFrame blacklist bypass signature
suggestion.rationale: Article names the exact vulnerable function and states 'blacklist can be bypassed with Unicode homoglyph identifiers.' Hunts should target the specific validation bypass, not generic activity. Monitor for Python dunder identifiers using Unicode substitutes (Cyrillic А vs Latin A, Mathematical Alphanumeric, combining marks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP POST to /api/v1/prediction with Python code containing dunder methods using non-ASCII lookalikes for latin characters. Search for regex patterns like Cyrillic А/Е/О/Х in identifier positions, or Mathematical Alphanumeric symbol blocks (U+1D400–U+1D7FF) adjacent to underscores.

suggestion.title: Re-exploitation of patched Flowise RCE chains (CSV/Airtable Agent)
suggestion.rationale: Article states this 'reopens the RCE paths patched as GHSA-3hjv-c53m-58jj (CSV Agent) and GHSA-v38x-c887-992f (Airtable Agent).' Detections should include monitoring for revival of those attack paths using this new homoglyph bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Requests to /api/v1/prediction or Airtable/CSV agent endpoints with homoglyph-encoded payloads followed by child process spawning from Flowise node process. Correlation: HTTP payload containing Unicode dunders + OS process creation within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: HTTP API request inspection for cross-UTF encoding in identifiers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Unicode homoglyph identifiers' as bypass mechanism. Should detect when a single logical identifier (e.g., '__init__') is encoded with mixed or non-standard UTF representations in parameter or request body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Web requests to Flowise API endpoints where parameter names or values contain Unicode characters from high-order blocks (Mathematical Alphanumeric, Cyrillic, Greek) mixed with ASCII in ways that a naive parser might collapse into dunder or reserved identifiers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Code Flow Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'device code phishing to bypass MFA'—pipeline missed detection for anomalous device code authentication initiation, which is central to the attack vector. Device code flows are typically low-volume and user-initiated; sudden spikes or origin mismatches are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for device code flow initiation requests from unexpected geographies, IP addresses, or timezones relative to user baseline. Flag requests where device code is promptly redeemed by a different IP/user agent than the initiator. Alert on bulk device code requests from a single source.

suggestion.title: Token Exfiltration via Compromised Device Code
suggestion.rationale: Article abstract: 'steal tokens'—the endgame is credential theft. Pipeline failed to propose detection for unusual token acquisition or usage post-device-code-phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline token issuance patterns per user and application. Alert when tokens are issued via device code flow but redeemed from a geographically or behaviorally anomalous context. Detect token usage immediately following device code auth from different IP/user agent.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass via Phishing + Device Code
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'bypass MFA'—the attack specifically circumvents second-factor protections. No detection was proposed for successful auth after device-code phishing attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing delivery events (email/SMS with device code URIs) against successful sign-ins within 5–15 minutes on the targeted account. Alert if MFA was marked as satisfied but the actual MFA provider logs show no challenge or the challenge was skipped/disabled.

suggestion.title: Greatness PhaaS Infrastructure & Phishing Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title names the threat actor/service 'Greatness PhaaS'—pipeline failed to extract this as a threat actor, organization, or malicious service. Should have proposed detection for phishing infrastructure and C2 associated with this service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create indicator set for Greatness PhaaS infrastructure (phishing domains, sender addresses, OAuth device code redirect URIs). Monitor for phishing emails/messages linking to device code authorization flows. Alert on clicks or navigation to known Greatness infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Device Code URI in Phishing Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Attack method described: 'device code phishing.' Pipeline missed detection for device code authorization URIs embedded in phishing messages (email, SMS, chat).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan phishing/email payloads for device code grant flow URIs (login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/devicecode, similar Azure/O365 patterns). Detect and quarantine messages containing device authorization links directed to external phishing domains.

suggestion.title: Node.js spawning shell interpreter from Flowise Record Manager execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes RCE—exploit payload must eventually spawn a shell. Pipeline does not detect child-process spawning from node running Flowise, e.g., node→bash/sh/powershell. Cite: 'Flowise RCE via SQLite Record Manager Node'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe (or nodejs) spawning bash, sh, cmd.exe, or powershell with unusual arguments, especially after HTTP POST to /api/v1/prediction or /api/v1/vector/upsert. Parent process should be node, grandparent may be container engine or http listener.

suggestion.title: Cron job or scheduled task created by Node.js process
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1053.005 (Cron) in techniques, indicating persistence via scheduled tasks. Pipeline detects SQLite writes but not the follow-on cron/task creation. Cite: 'T1053.005 — Scheduled Task/Job: Cron' and 'arbitrary SQLite write to system dir'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron files created or modified (e.g., /etc/cron.d/*, /var/spool/cron/*) by node process, or systemd timer units created by non-root node process. Check for presence of node/npm/exec in cron payload.

suggestion.title: SQLite database file created outside .flowise/ by node process
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'arbitrary SQLite write to system dir' as the exploitation mechanism. UC_9_5 looks for file writes, but specific monitoring for .db/.sqlite files in root-sensitive paths is more precise. Cite: 'Flowise arbitrary SQLite write to system dir via SQLite Record Manager additionalConfig'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .db, .sqlite, .sqlite3 files created by node process in /etc, /root, /usr/local/sbin, /var/spool, or other system directories. Exclude .flowise/ directories. Correlate with HTTP POST requests to upsert/prediction endpoints in preceding 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Flowise API request with malicious additionalConfig database-path parameter
suggestion.rationale: The vuln leverages the 'additionalConfig' parameter to override database paths. Pipeline's UC_9_6 detects HTTP requests to API endpoints but does not look for the additionalConfig payload itself. Cite: 'SQLite Record Manager additionalConfig database-path override'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST/PUT request bodies to /api/v1/prediction, /api/v1/vector/upsert, /api/v1/document-store for JSON payloads containing 'additionalConfig' with 'database-path' or 'sqlite' pointing outside .flowise/ directory. Flag paths like /etc/, /root/, /var/spool/cron, /dev/shm/.

suggestion.title: Reverse shell or data exfiltration command from Flowise node process
suggestion.rationale: RCE enables arbitrary command execution. Pipeline lacks detection of common post-exploitation commands (curl, wget, nc, /dev/tcp). Cite: 'RCE via SQLite Record Manager Node' implies attacker gains shell access and likely exfiltrates or establishes callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections initiated by node process to unusual ports/IPs, or node spawning curl/wget/netcat with suspicious URLs. Correlate timing with SQLite write events detected in UC_9_5.

suggestion.title: POST request to Flowise API without valid authentication token or with bypass payload
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may require bypassing auth or exploiting auth mechanism. Article does not explicitly state if auth is required, but RCE implies attacker can reach the vulnerable endpoint. Cite: 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Flowise /api/v1/* endpoints with missing or malformed Authorization headers, or repeated 401→200 transitions suggesting auth bypass. Pair with subsequent SQLite write or command execution events.

suggestion.title: Base64-encoded Python payload injected into CSVAgent parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Python code injection via base64_string = "${base64String}" (CSVAgent.ts line 161)' but no detection for base64 pattern in CSV agent processing. This is the injection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Flowise CSV agent handling for base64-encoded strings in request parameters (especially `base64String` field). Look for non-ASCII payload encoding in HTTP POST bodies to CSV upload endpoints. Detect decoding operations (base64 -d, atob()) within 500ms before Python interpreter spawning child processes.

suggestion.title: Pyodide JavaScript bridge invocation with process module access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Pyodide js bridge provides access to the host Node.js process' and specifically 'process.mainModule.constructor._load("child_process")' but no signature hunt for this module-loading pattern exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process memory patterns or child-process spawning events where Node.js loads the child_process module via constructor._load(). Alternatively, detect Pyodide library execution (pyodide*.js files loaded) followed immediately by process module abuse within same session.

suggestion.title: Node.js running shell commands as root with Flowise parent context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root shell verified' but existing hunts do not correlate privilege level (root execution) with Flowise parent context. Without root check, FP rate is high.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell spawning (sh/bash/dash) as child of node.js where AccountName=root or UID=0, and either (a) node process path contains 'flowise' or (b) parent chain includes CSVAgent module load. Filter for non-development environments.

suggestion.title: Environment variable or configuration file access from injected shell context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions credential access under '/root/.flowise' but also states credentials are exfiltrated. No hunt for env var enumeration (whoami, id, env, uname) that precedes credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for recon command sequence: id → uname → env → cat /etc/passwd-like patterns, executed as children of shell spawned from node. Particularly flag when shell is grandchild of node AND these commands execute within 10 seconds of shell launch.

suggestion.title: Reverse shell / Meterpreter session establishment from Node.js process
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'Meterpreter reverse shell session as root has been established' but provided UC_10_3 hard-codes port 4444 (unverified). Need detection for shell reversal patterns regardless of port.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate shell spawning from node.js with outbound network connections (any port, unusual destinations). Flag if shell process opens listening socket OR establishes outbound connection to non-standard port shortly after spawning. Include entropy/byte analysis for encoded traffic (Meterpreter uses binary protocol, not HTTP).

suggestion.title: Flowise CSV agent processing anomalies (large payloads, encoding shifts)
suggestion.rationale: The CSV upload to Flowise is the entry point, but no content-based detection for malicious CSV patterns. Article does not detail CSV structure but mentions 'base64 payload injection' which implies abnormal CSV content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CSV uploads to Flowise for content anomalies: (a) CSV rows containing base64 strings (entropy > 4.0), (b) CSV exceeding expected row/column counts for data processing, (c) CSV with embedded Python/code-like keywords (import, exec, eval, __). Correlate with subsequent node child-process spawns.

suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-07' and recommends standard asset-exposure hunt. Explicitly warns: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet—patch lag is the silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for N-central instances without security updates applied by 2026-08-07. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results; flag any showing 'patched' status that was not recently updated. MSP/RMM tools manage fleet-wide access—unpatched instances create highest-severity blast radius.

suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' Article confirms active exploitation. Detection must target bypass mechanisms, not just failed-login hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for requests to N-central endpoints that bypass normal auth flow: direct API calls without session tokens, requests to non-standard authentication paths, malformed or replayed credentials. Correlate successful sessions after anomalous auth patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-compromise lateral movement or discovery from N-central after auth bypass

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After identifying suspicious N-central access, hunt for lateral movement signals: process executions, WMI queries, remote session initiations, or port scans originating from N-central or from accounts recently accessing N-central. Focus on commands executed via typical RMM channels.

suggestion.rationale: N-central is typically accessed as remote service. T1133 (External Remote Services) is missing from pipeline's technique mapping and should be core to this vulnerability's kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline N-central remote access patterns (source IPs, geolocation, connection frequency). Alert on: new external source IPs, geographic anomalies, spike in connection attempts, or access patterns inconsistent with known client behavior.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance & Remediation Tracking: CVE-2026-18556
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors/regulators' and specifies 2026-08-07 deadline. Compliance tracking is required deliverable for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate patch status reports for all N-central instances. Alert on systems not patched by 2026-08-07. Investigate failed deployments. Correlate patch dates against vulnerability scanner results to confirm remediation success.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Vulnerability Scanner Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-18556'. Pipeline must emit scanner queries for this KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner databases (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) for systems reporting vulnerable N-able N-central versions. Filter by product name 'N-central' and CVE-2026-18556. CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation, so patch status must be reconciled against asset inventory.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'. Pipeline must detect malformed or non-standard authentication attempts against N-central endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central web or API authentication logs for: (a) requests to non-standard or undocumented authentication endpoints, (b) failed auth attempts followed immediately by successful access to administrative endpoints, (c) HTTP 401/403 followed by 200 on alternate paths. Baseline normal auth channels first.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Alternate Authentication Channel Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack uses 'alternate path or channel'—suggests non-primary auth mechanism. Detection must discriminate between normal multi-factor flows and bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag access to N-central administrative or sensitive endpoints via uncommon request patterns: direct API calls without session cookies, requests bypassing load balancer, traffic on non-standard ports or protocols, or requests from internal IP ranges inconsistent with normal client distribution.

suggestion.title: Exposed N-able N-central Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: KEV implies internet-facing deployment. Article references asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline must generate discovery use case for exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query passive DNS and internet scanning services (Shodan, Censys, ProjectDiscovery) for exposed N-central instances on typical ports (9000, 8080, 443). Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to identify rogue or unpatched deployments. Federal patch due 2026-08-07 warrants immediate triage.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central: Unauthorized Management Console Access via Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'—the attack vector. Attackers gain console access without valid credentials via non-standard endpoints. Primary detection priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central auth logs for successful logins from unexpected sources, non-standard authentication paths, or bypassed MFA. Baseline legitimate administrator patterns and alert on deviations, especially from Internet-exposed interfaces.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Asset Exposure and CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'public-facing application' exploited in wild (CISA KEV). Organizations must enumerate all N-central instances and scan for CVE-2026-18556 with immediate remediation by federal deadline 2026-08-07.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing networks for N-able N-central services. Cross-reference against inventory to identify unauthorized instances. Run CVE-2026-18556 scanner checks and enforce patch compliance against 2026-08-07 SLA.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly Detection: Alternate Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly leverages 'alternate path or channel' for bypass. Detection must specifically target non-standard authentication endpoints and API routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on auth attempts to non-standard N-central paths (backup endpoints, debug URLs, undocumented routes). Correlate failed auth spikes with successes, indicating brute-force or bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Post-Compromise Behavioral Baseline
suggestion.rationale: If authentication bypassed, post-compromise actions diverge from legitimate administrator behavior. Behavioral anomalies provide best post-compromise detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline N-central admin activities (login times, task patterns, source IPs). Alert on deviations: new accounts, credential exports, policy changes, off-hours access, unexpected geolocation, bulk config modifications.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 Patch Compliance Tracking and Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with active exploitation and federal remediation deadline 2026-08-07. Continuous scanning and compliance tracking against deadline is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run continuous scans for CVE-2026-18556 across all N-central instances. Flag systems remaining vulnerable past 48-72 hour SLA. Generate daily remediation tracking reports targeting federal deadline.

suggestion.title: npm postinstall script execution with suspicious outbound network
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm 'automatically spread across software ecosystems by republishing malicious updates'—indicates execution phase occurs during package install and immediately connects to C2 for credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm/node processes spawning command-line interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash) during postinstall script execution, followed by network connections to non-Microsoft infrastructure. Flag processes with parents matching *npm.cmd, *npx.cmd, or node.exe launching interpreters within 2 seconds of package installation.

suggestion.title: Repeated npm package republishing from single account in short timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'automatically republished malicious updates'—indicates attacker used compromised npm accounts to push multiple package versions in rapid succession across 400+ packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query npm registry access logs and artifact repositories for single authentication token publishing 10+ package versions within 1-hour windows. Flag accounts with unusual geographic origin changes or publishing packages outside their historical maintenance scope.

suggestion.title: Credential file access during npm package post-install execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing worm'—worm must enumerate and access credential stores (.ssh, .aws, .docker, .npmrc, browser profiles) during postinstall phase before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or child processes (spawned by postinstall scripts) accessing paths matching *\.ssh, *\.aws, *\.npmrc, *\.docker, %APPDATA%\npm, or browser credential databases. Exclude legitimate package operations via allowlist of known auth libraries.

suggestion.title: Self-propagating worm dependency injection pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes worm 'self-propagating'—suggests malicious package modifies package.json or publishes new versions that include itself as a dependency, or spreads to other packages via publish-time injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm packages that introduce unexpected new dependencies or versions mid-lifecycle. Flag package.json modifications that add dependencies post-publish or package manifests that differ between registry metadata and installed artifacts. Cross-reference publishing accounts for coordinated changes.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of environment variables and secrets to external C2
suggestion.rationale: Worm steals credentials and must transmit them; article specifies credential exfiltration to attacker infrastructure outside npm ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node.exe or npm-spawned processes with DNS/HTTP requests to non-npm infrastructure during package operations. Flag payloads containing common credential patterns (AWS_SECRET, github token prefix, API key patterns, JWT structures). Baseline C2 infrastructure against known attacker IOCs.

suggestion.title: Spoofed sender accepted despite SPF/DMARC failure via enterprise whitelist
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Although the messages originated from an unknown IONOS mail server, failed SPF and DMARC checks, and had no DKIM signature, they were still accepted by the receiving systems because RingCentral was whitelisted.' This is defense evasion via trusted relationship abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with failed SPF/DMARC validation that originate from non-whitelisted infrastructure but are forwarded by whitelisted domains. Track sender mismatch (From header ≠ Return-Path) combined with whitelist bypass. Baseline legitimate RingCentral forwarding paths.

suggestion.title: MFA-approved sign-ins from VPS/commercial VPN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the attacker replayed Microsoft 365 authentication tokens from VPS and commercial VPN infrastructure to access the compromised accounts.' This is post-compromise token replay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Microsoft 365 sign-in events with valid MFA approval originating from known VPS providers (AWS, Azure, DigitalOcean) or commercial VPN services. Correlate MFA approval timestamp with phishing click timestamp. Alert if same token used from multiple geolocations within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious post-compromise Microsoft Graph enumeration of O365 resources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enumerated Outlook mailboxes, Teams conversations, SharePoint sites, OneDrive files, contacts, calendars, and registered applications through Microsoft Graph, with access persisting for more than two weeks.' This is discovery and collection via GraphAPI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential Microsoft Graph API calls to /me/mailfolders, /me/messages, /me/chats, /me/drive, /me/registeredDevices within 1-hour window. Flag accounts showing GraphAPI activity from VPS/VPN IPs not seen in baseline. Alert on app-based GraphAPI access from non-standard OAuth applications.

suggestion.title: Device-code phishing flow targeting Microsoft 365 with MFA bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states phishing page routed victims 'through a Microsoft adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing flow that captured an MFA-approved authentication token or through a device-code phishing flow.' Device-code abuse is T1187.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device-code flow (oauth2/devicecode endpoint) from non-enterprise IP ranges or suspicious ASNs. Flag device-code MFA approval followed by token issuance within 2 minutes. Detect OAuth consent grants to unusual app IDs immediately after device-code flows. Monitor for user device-code approval events followed by unrelated resource access.

suggestion.title: Prolonged post-compromise account access and persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'access persisting for more than two weeks in some cases.' This indicates undetected persistence despite MFA compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in patterns showing continuous or near-continuous access from phishing-sourced IPs spanning >7 days without corresponding user MFA approval events. Alert on OAuth refresh token reuse across 14+ days from static IP/VPN. Flag accounts with active GraphAPI usage but no interactive user sessions in same period.

suggestion.title: Tenant-specific phishing page serving and MFA token interception
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Microsoft 365 phishing page with tenant-specific branding.' This indicates real-time tenant detection and dynamic page generation typical of AiTM attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries for spoofed Microsoft 365 endpoints (login.microsoftonline.com redirects, mail.office365.com variants). Flag HTTP CONNECT events to phishing infrastructure IPs with certificate CN mismatch. Correlate risky sign-in events (impossible travel, anomalous token claims) with proxy logs showing preceding phishing page visits.

suggestion.title: Flowise: Stolen OAuth token usage against downstream service
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'enables token theft for any connected service' but provides no detection for the final exploitation phase. The kill chain includes lateral movement via stolen tokens: 'It decrypts the stored credential (containing clientId, clientSecret, refresh_token), sends a refresh request to the configured OAuth provider, and returns the new access_token directly.' Missing: detection of those stolen tokens being used to call downstream APIs (Slack, Google, GitHub, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After token theft from Flowise, attacker uses stolen access_token to call downstream OAuth service APIs. Detect by: (1) unusual geographic/IP origin for API calls to integrated services post-refresh, (2) API calls to rare/never-before-called downstream services shortly after Flowise endpoint probing, (3) downstream service grants or data exfiltration triggered by unfamiliar OAuth2 bearer tokens.

suggestion.title: Flowise: Stored OAuth credential decryption or export
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability works because Flowise 'decrypts the stored credential (containing clientId, clientSecret, refresh_token).' This is T1555 (Credentials from Password Store) but no detection covers the decryption/access of the credential store itself. Missing: host-level detection of Flowise accessing its own credential database or exporting credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Flowise application process for: (1) reading credential database files at high frequency, (2) env var exports of decrypted OAuth secrets, (3) file writes to temp directories containing credential material, (4) unusual database queries against credential storage tables.

suggestion.title: Flowise: Unauthenticated endpoint discovery and probing
suggestion.rationale: Before exploiting the token-refresh endpoint, an attacker must discover the Flowise instance and enumerate credentialIds. This is discovery/reconnaissance (T1526, T1087). Missing: detection of probing attempts that come before the actual token-refresh exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance phase: (1) repeated 404s or status-200 responses to common Flowise paths (/api/v1/oauth2-credential*, /api/v1/credentials*), (2) sequential attempts to guess credentialIds before first successful refresh (GET requests or OPTIONS to the endpoint), (3) comparison between failed token-refresh attempts and successful ones in same source IP within short window.

suggestion.title: CSV file upload with prompt injection payload markers
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'A prompt injection sent to a chatflow using a CSV Agent node' but no detection exists for malicious CSV content itself. Requires inspection of uploaded files for jailbreak/injection markers before execution reaches Python validator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Flowise-served file uploads to /api/v1/prediction or chat endpoints. Scan CSV content for prompt-injection keywords: 'exec','system','import','__','subprocess','os.','eval(','lambda', Python string literals with shell syntax, SQL injection markers. Correlate with subsequent Python code validation rejections (UC_6_4) or shell spawning (UC_6_2).

suggestion.title: Flowise API endpoint enumeration or fuzz attempts targeting /api/v1/prediction
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) but current hunts only detect high-volume POSTs, not reconnaissance. Attackers probe /api/v1/prediction variants, parameter names, or HTTP methods before payload submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 404/405 responses to /api/v1/prediction* endpoint, followed by successful POST. Look for User-Agent consistency (single tool), rapid requests (sub-second intervals), or parameter fuzzing patterns (?agent=, ?csv=, ?model=) that precede exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Flowise-spawned Python process with network egress and env-file access in same session
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_5 detects file access independently; needs correlation rule linking file access to network connections in same parent-child lineage. Article mentions exfiltration (T1041) over C2 but no detection connects credential access to data ex-filtration in time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Flowise-parented Python process reading .env or database.sqlite (within 30s) with outbound network connections to non-standard ports or known C2 domains. Flag if egress IP is not in allowlist (e.g., API provider subnets, software repos).

suggestion.title: Flowise database (database.sqlite) file access from web-tier child processes
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_5 mentions database.sqlite but no dedicated detection. RCE child processes should not directly access SQLite—should go through Flowise service. Direct database file access from shell spawned by web request is high-confidence post-RCE indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process (shell, Python, curl, sqlite3) spawned by node/flowise process accessing database.sqlite file directly (not via TCP port 8080 or 3000). Correlate file open/read events with process lineage confirming web-initiated parent.

suggestion.title: Rapid successive Python code validation rejections from same source IP + chatflow ID
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_4 detects rejections but no context on source or pattern. Article describes blocklist bypass (T1027) as iterative: attacker tries many prompt-injection obfuscation variations, each rejected. Clustering rejections per source/chatflow reveals attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Group Flowise security rejection logs by (source IP, chatflow ID, 5m time window). Flag if same source generates ≥5 rejections in 5 minutes, indicating iterative bypass attempts rather than accidental user error.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Ransomware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'multi-stage attack' with execution to detection in 129 seconds. No process execution or command-line UCs despite clear attack progression requiring immediate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect obfuscated command-line execution chains, LOLBIN abuse (certutil, bitsadmin, wmic), or suspicious process spawning that precedes rapid file system I/O or network beaconing typical of ransomware initialization.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Deployment Blocked
suggestion.rationale: Description states attack was stopped 'before the payload could persist'—persistence mechanisms were actively deployed and detectable. Pipeline generated zero persistence-phase UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to HKLM/HKCU Run keys, Startup folders, and scheduled task creation with suspicious binaries or paths; flag service/WMI event subscription modifications deployed by ransomware for reboot persistence.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payload Deployment & Encryption Prevention
suggestion.rationale: Article is fundamentally about ransomware threat; description notes payload blocked from deployment. No impact-phase UCs despite clear encryption/destruction activity to detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass file writes with suspicious extensions, Volume Shadow Copy deletion (vssadmin, wbadmin), boot configuration modifications, or crypto-tool process signatures exhibiting rapid file enumeration and high I/O to user/shared directories.

suggestion.title: AnySign4PC execution from non-standard paths (temp/appdata/downloads)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states backdoors installed 'without prompts'—implies sideloaded, compromised binary executed outside Program Files. This execution context is a hallmark of supply-chain compromise and is not detected by empty pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AnySign4PC process execution from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Downloads, or user temp directories. Validate digital signature and compare hash against known good builds. Cross-reference with recent access to Korean .kr domains in proxy logs.

suggestion.title: Unexpected child processes or DLL loads from AnySign4PC
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor delivery 'without prompts' suggests AnySign4PC spawns malware or loads malicious DLLs. Standard application behavior does not include cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe children.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes created by AnySign4PC or variants spawning LOLBins, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or regsvcs.exe. Monitor for unsigned or suspicious DLL loads within AnySign4PC process space.

suggestion.title: Network beaconing from AnySign4PC to Korean C2
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify C2 infrastructure but backdoor installation implies command-and-control channels. No UC captures anomalous outbound traffic from the compromised application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and outbound HTTPS/TCP connections originating from AnySign4PC process. Flag callbacks to Korean ASNs, recently-registered domains, or IPs hosting known malware. Alert on periodic beaconing intervals.

suggestion.title: Access to hacked Korean government/enterprise sites + AnySign4PC download correlation
suggestion.rationale: Initial-access vector: 'hacked Korean sites'. Article emphasizes this supply-chain entry point. Defenders must detect the moment users visit compromised legitimate Korean domains and correlate with subsequent binary downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish whitelist of legitimate Korean government/corporate .kr domains (banking, telecom, healthcare). Alert on first-time access from endpoints to these domains. Correlate with file downloads (especially .exe, .msi, .zip) or AnySign4PC process execution within 2-hour window on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Registry persistence by AnySign4PC (Run keys, Services, Scheduled Tasks)
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor installation without user interaction implies persistence mechanism. Article does not specify how but scheduled tasks, run keys, or service creation are standard Korean malware patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKCU/HKLM \Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or Services by AnySign4PC process. Monitor for new Windows scheduled tasks executing AnySign4PC, rundll32.exe, or suspicious Korean-named binaries with system privileges.

suggestion.title: Invalid or suspicious digital signature on AnySign4PC binary
suggestion.rationale: Compromised distribution implies modified or replaced binary. Article emphasizes 'hacked Korean sites'—signature validation catches tampering. Pipeline missed signature-integrity detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AnySign4PC execution where authenticode signature fails validation (unsigned, revoked, expired), or subject name does not match legitimate publisher. Flag execution from web-cache or recently-downloaded locations with failed signature verification.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central CVE-2026-18556 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-18556 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and describes asset-exposure hunt as canonical detection. Pipeline produced no vulnerability-scanner-based detection despite this explicit requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanner logs and CMDB for systems flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-18556 (N-able N-central). Cross-reference patch-management records to identify systems without 2026-08-07 federal remediation deadline applied. Prioritize public-facing N-central instances (RMM management consoles).

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' Pipeline omitted detection for suspicious authentication patterns or unconventional N-central login paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to N-able N-central management consoles for requests to non-standard authentication endpoints, unusual URI patterns, or direct administrative function calls bypassing normal login flows. Correlate with failed-then-successful authentication sequences or unauthenticated API calls to privileged functions.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Unauthorized Access and Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass results in valid account compromise; pipeline did not model post-bypass access patterns or RMM lateral-movement activity expected after N-central compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After N-able N-central compromise, look for unusual process execution initiated from N-central agent processes (e.g., spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or script interpreters). Monitor for lateral-movement network connections from N-central management console to endpoints not in baseline RMM management patterns. Flag sessions with mismatched or missing authentication event logs.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Federal Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date of 2026-08-07, creating regulatory compliance requirement. Pipeline did not generate compliance-tracking or deadline-accountability detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track remediation progress for CVE-2026-18556 across all N-able N-central instances with known federal reporting obligations. Generate daily inventory of unpatched systems, identify root-cause delays (blocked patches, incompatibility holds), and escalate systems still vulnerable 24-48 hours before 2026-08-07 deadline.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Beaconing and Command Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: RMM (Remote Monitoring & Management) software is a high-value persistence mechanism for adversaries; active KEV status suggests widespread exploitation risk. Pipeline omitted detection for suspicious RMM agent behavior or command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from N-able N-central agents to non-whitelist IP ranges, non-standard ports, or infrastructure outside typical vendor update/licensing CDNs. Flag execution of scripts or binaries staged through RMM console that deviate from vendor-signed software. Correlate command execution timing with authentication-bypass exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: N-central authentication bypass detection (alternate path)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' — pipeline must detect successful N-central logins that bypass normal credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful N-central authentication events lacking corresponding credential validation steps, or logins from unexpected paths/source IPs. Monitor N-central session creation without prior explicit authentication request.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18556 asset inventory and patch compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status and federal patch deadline (2026-08-07) require scanner coverage. Article names product and vendor explicitly for IOC matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scans for N-able N-central installations below patched version threshold. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances. Alert for all unpatched systems past federal due date.

suggestion.title: N-central lateral movement post-auth bypass
suggestion.rationale: N-central is a management/remote-access tool; successful auth bypass grants attacker foothold to pivot to managed endpoints. Article context implies lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect N-central processes spawning remote execution to internal infrastructure outside maintenance windows: RPC, SSH, WinRM, or psexec from ncentral.exe parent. Correlate with abnormal N-central API usage.

suggestion.title: N-central API abuse and command deployment
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass grants API access; attacker likely uses N-central REST/SOAP APIs to deploy commands to managed endpoints. Article implies capability to execute as authenticated N-central admin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal N-central API patterns: bulk device queries, credential/configuration changes, or mass script deployment outside scheduled maintenance. Flag token creation and bulk API call rates from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: N-central administrative account modification
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attackers often create rogue admin accounts or escalate privileges within the management tool to cement persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for account creation, role assignment, or privilege escalation within N-central management interface post-auth bypass. Flag new N-central admin accounts, especially created post-patch-deadline or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Suspicious child process execution from N-central agent
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated, attackers abuse N-central's remote execution capabilities to run arbitrary code on managed systems via ncentral.exe or agent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or suspicious executables with parent process N-central agent (ncentral.exe) outside expected deployment/patch operations. Correlate with N-central API logs confirming remote command injection.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempt — N-able N-central Alternate Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel' — core attack vector that should generate hypothesis for detecting direct bypasses of login flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central web application logs (default ports 8040/8041) for POST/GET requests to authentication-related endpoints with absent or malformed credential parameters. Alert on HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences, unexpected query parameters (e.g., ?bypass=1, ?auth=0), or direct API calls to user-management endpoints that bypass the login portal entirely.

suggestion.title: Successful N-able N-central Session Post-Failed Auth Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article claims bypass 'allows for authentication bypass' — detection must correlate suspicious/failed login attempts with subsequent authenticated sessions or API calls under the same source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal N-able N-central authentication patterns (credential submission + 200 OK + session token). Flag anomalies: session tokens issued without prior credential POST, authentication success immediately following multiple 40x/50x errors from same source, or tokens granted to known-inactive user accounts.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise N-able N-central Configuration Changes & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article warns federal agencies must patch by 2026-08-07 — implies in-the-wild exploitation for persistence/lateral movement. Once bypassed, attackers will enumerate internal assets and pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central server for outbound connections to internal IP ranges (scanning), RDP/SSH/WinRM traffic to domain controllers/servers, and unsigned executable staging in temporary directories. Alert on N-central process spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell with -NoProfile flags, or net.exe commands for user/group enumeration.

suggestion.title: Scanner Bypass: Vulnerable N-able N-central Versions Post-Patch Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check' — patch lag is endemic; vulnerability scanners may report false-negatives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management tool for N-able N-central instances and cross-reference against Build/Version numbers known-vulnerable to CVE-2026-18556 (vendor advisory will list ranges). Flag instances marked 'patched' but running unpatched build IDs, instances with 'unknown' patch status, or those not scanned within last 30 days.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Web Server HTTP Abnormalities Indicating Bypass Technique
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass techniques often generate anomalous HTTP patterns (missing headers, unexpected methods, encoding tricks) visible in access logs before successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-able N-central IIS/Apache/nginx logs for: PUT/DELETE methods on authentication endpoints, Host-header manipulation, unusual User-Agent strings (e.g., empty, curl without normal browser fields), Content-Length: 0 on POST requests to login, or HTTP/1.0 requests (legacy exploitation technique). Spike in 401/403 errors followed by 200 OK is suspicious.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Unauthorized Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel'—pipeline must detect attempts to reach N-central without valid session. Detection baseline: failed auth followed by successful access from same source within short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 401/403 to N-central admin endpoints (/admin, /api/*) followed by HTTP 200 from same source IP within 60 seconds. Flag requests lacking authorization headers to sensitive paths. Baseline known admin IP ranges first to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Alternate-Path Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'alternate path or channel' bypass. Detect direct API requests circumventing normal login—the exact attack vector described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to N-central /api/agents, /api/admin, or undocumented debug endpoints with missing/invalid auth headers or stale session tokens. Detect referer anomalies (direct endpoint access rather than navigating through UI) and requests from sources never authenticated to N-central.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach N-central Agent Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: After bypassing authentication, attackers pivot via N-central to command managed agents for lateral movement or data collection—article emphasizes bypass but lacks post-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous bulk agent actions: mass policy deployments to agents outside change control, script execution to agent fleet, enrollment of rogue agents from out-of-band sources. Requires N-central audit log ingestion and baseline of normal administrator command patterns.
