suggestion.title: TeamCity Service Account Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Successful unauthenticated RCE via deserialization results in arbitrary code execution. Article confirms 'remote code execution' impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by TeamCity service account (java.exe or java under CI service context). Flag unexpected interpreter invocations (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, bash, python) or reverse-shell utilities. Establish baseline of legitimate build-agent processes and alert on significant deviations.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Service Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation RCE pivot using service account typically running elevated for CI/CD operations. Article confirms execution impact; lateral movement is expected follow-on.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from TeamCity service account to non-standard destinations (excluding known build-agent nodes, artifact repositories, SCM systems). Alert on SMB/RDP/SSH lateral movement attempts, port scanning, or unusual DNS queries. Correlate with baseline CI/CD communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious TeamCity Process Ancestry & Parent-Child Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation via deserialization gadget chains often spawns processes with unexpected lineage or unusual process hollowing. Article confirms RCE; process tree anomalies indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TeamCity parent process spawning unrelated child processes (e.g., java spawning native executables outside standard agent/build contexts). Flag process hollowing indicators (parent-child handle inheritance anomalies). Alert on unexpected process injection or token impersonation via TeamCity JVM.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states JetBrains TeamCity is affected by CVE-2026-63077. Standard asset-exposure hunt for vulnerable software versions (per template reference in article body) is mandatory for any CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for any TeamCity installations matching affected versions. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify internet-facing instances. Alert on any match as imminent exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector is 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol' — a specific protocol-level exploit path that requires dedicated protocol analysis. Pipeline missed this specific attack surface entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic (typically port 9090 or configuration-specific) for: (1) unauthenticated connection attempts, (2) unusual payload sizes or frequencies, (3) malformed protocol messages, (4) agents communicating with unknown TeamCity controllers.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Deserialization Exception Logging
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability as 'deserialization of untrusted data' — Java deserialization exploits commonly log distinct exception types. Pipeline missed log-source-specific detection for this exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search TeamCity application logs for serialization/deserialization exceptions, ClassNotFoundException, InvalidClassException, or other Java unmarshalling errors. Correlate with unauthenticated access patterns or unusual agent polling requests to distinguish exploitation attempts from legitimate errors.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Child Process Execution from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'remote code execution' outcome — exploitation success requires detecting the executed code. Pipeline generated no detection for post-RCE activity (child processes, network connections, file writes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by java.exe/java process running TeamCity (look for pid parent matching TeamCity process tree), especially: shell interpreters (cmd.exe, /bin/sh), network tools (curl, wget, nc), file utilities outside normal maintenance patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity API/Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — the absence of authentication requirement is the critical attack condition. Pipeline missed detection for authentication-bypass or unauthenticated access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal TeamCity authentication patterns, then alert on: (1) successful RCE payloads delivered without valid session tokens, (2) agent polling protocol requests without expected authentication handshakes, (3) known RCE command patterns in request payloads (e.g., cmd, powershell, bash execution syntax).

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Communication Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack uses 'agent polling protocol' — agents are a distinct surface with polling patterns. Pipeline produced no detection for abnormal agent-to-controller communication that could indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agents for: (1) agents polling from unexpected network ranges, (2) unusually large payloads in agent communication (indicators of serialized exploit objects), (3) agents reporting configuration changes post-polling, (4) multiple agents connecting from single attacker IP in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-63077 as the exploit vector and notes federal patch due 2026-08-08. Standard asset-exposure hunt for vulnerable TeamCity instances is the baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for TeamCity installations matching vulnerable version ranges. Cross-reference against observed patch dates to identify lag. CISA KEV implies active scanning/exploitation attempts; flag any exposed TeamCity web UI endpoint on public-facing networks.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—this is the attack surface. Need to detect unauthorized access to agent polling endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically /agent endpoints or similar) without valid agent credentials. Flag 4xx→2xx transitions or repeated auth failures followed by successful polling. Baseline expected agent IPs and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data in TeamCity Agent Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability.' Pipeline must detect malformed or weaponized serialized objects sent to agent polling endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent polling protocol traffic for payloads containing serialized Java objects (Java serialization magic bytes 0xaced0005 or equivalent). Inspect for embedded command structures or gadget chains. High-entropy serialized data to unauthenticated endpoints is high-confidence exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via TeamCity Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection needed to catch shell spawning or process injection from TeamCity agent process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity agent or server processes (java.exe → cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, etc.). Correlate with suspicious agent polling traffic within 5s window. Flag any reverse-shell callbacks or privilege-escalation attempts from agent context.

suggestion.title: Anomalous TeamCity Agent-to-Server Communication
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of agent polling protocol should manifest as unusual communication patterns: unexpected destinations, large payload sizes, or repeated polling from non-registered agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for TeamCity agent polling frequency, payload sizes, and agent source IPs. Alert on >3σ deviation. Detect agents initiating polling from unexpected internal IPs or external sources. Monitor for agents requesting unusual artifact retrieval or build step commands.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised TeamCity Instance
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved on TeamCity server/agent, attacker can pivot to build targets, artifact repositories, or downstream systems. Need post-compromise lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate TeamCity server compromise indicators with unusual outbound connections to build targets, artifact repositories, or SCM systems (GitHub, GitLab, etc.). Flag credential usage from TeamCity context to adjacent systems. Monitor for TeamCity processes attempting SMB/RDP to other internal hosts.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' vulnerability exploited in wild; no UC generated to hunt for exposed TeamCity ports (8080/443) or Web console access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TeamCity instances exposed on non-RFC1918 networks or accessible from untrusted CIDR ranges. Correlate with asset inventory to flag patch-lag instances. Alert on >50 failed authentication attempts or version-probing from external IPs.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Protocol Deserialization Attack
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits deserialization via agent polling protocol; article states 'unauthenticated' access. Pipeline missed the protocol-level attack vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for malformed or oversized payloads to TeamCity agent port (default 9090 or configured alternate). Detect Java deserialization gadget chains (commons-collections, xstream patterns) in agent polling traffic. Flag any unauthenticated agent-protocol handshakes.

suggestion.title: Successful TeamCity RCE Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote code execution' via agent protocol but no use case to detect post-compromise activity. Missing command execution indicators from TeamCity process or agent child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity service (java.exe on Windows, java on Linux) for abnormal child process spawning, especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or curl. Alert on TeamCity agent processes executing binaries outside normal build artifact paths or calling network utilities.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-08-08 and CISA KEV imply regulatory remediation deadline. Pipeline ignored compliance hunting angle entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for TeamCity instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-63077. Cross-reference CMDB to identify systems past federal due date without patch. Escalate to remediation team; audit log who runs TeamCity and when patches are deployed.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Lateral Movement via Agent Network
suggestion.rationale: Agent polling protocol may allow pivot to other agents or internal systems. Article mentions protocol but pipeline missed lateral-movement implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TeamCity agents initiating new connections outside their normal build-job scope. Flag agent-to-agent communication across network boundaries. Monitor for agent processes connecting to non-whitelisted internal services (databases, file shares, CI/CD systems).

suggestion.title: Agent Protocol Version Downgrade / Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated agent polling suggests potential for protocol manipulation. No UC for detecting agent impersonation or protocol bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent handshakes for version mismatches, missing authentication headers, or replay attacks. Alert if the same agent ID connects from multiple IPs simultaneously or from geographically impossible locations.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and 'patch lag is the silent killer'—requires inventory of exposed/internal TeamCity instances and verification against minimum safe versions prior to federal patch due date 2026-08-08.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TeamCity instances on default or known ports; cross-reference against patched version inventory. Correlate scanner outputs against software inventory to confirm patch status, accounting for false-negatives in automated scanning.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly identified as 'agent polling protocol'—network-accessible endpoint requires monitoring for malformed or payload-bearing serialized requests indicative of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network traffic to TeamCity agent endpoints with patterns of serialized Java objects, gadget-chain payloads, or out-of-band callbacks. Flag external-source connections to internal agent polling ports deviating from agent-to-server baseline.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Deserialization Exception Spike
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability type 'deserialization of untrusted data'—exploitation attempts will generate ClassNotFoundException, InvalidClassException, or ObjectStreamException in TeamCity logs prior to successful execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for deserialization-related exceptions in agent polling request handlers. Correlate exception timestamps with suspicious network traffic or external connection attempts to same instance.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Anomalies in TeamCity Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful unauthenticated RCE will execute arbitrary code under TeamCity service account—baseline normal background activity and alert on unexpected process spawning, especially network utilities or shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes spawned from TeamCity service (java.exe or teamcity agent runner), particularly network tools (curl, wget, certutil), shells (powershell, cmd), or reverse-shell signatures without corresponding admin action or prior scheduled task.

suggestion.title: Exposed Rockwell PLC Ports on Internet-Facing Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Over 4,400 Rockwell PLCs Exposed Online'—direct evidence of internet-routable industrial control systems. Pipeline produced no IOCs or detection use cases for this exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to common Rockwell/EtherNet/IP ports (2222, 44818, 5069) from non-whitelisted external IPs. Alert on any Shodan/Censys-like scanning patterns targeting these ports to known water utility network ranges. Flag unexpected responses or banner grabs from PLC endpoints.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Targeting Water Utility PLC Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '22 Found in Water Attack Cities'—explicit targeting of water infrastructure. Pipeline failed to map initial reconnaissance phase or water-utility targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries for water utility network domain patterns, followed by network scanning/enumeration attempts toward known water-SCADA IP ranges. Alert on service discovery queries (nmap, Shodan, Censys user agents) originating from threat actor infrastructure toward utilities listed in 'water attack cities' phrase.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PLC Configuration or Firmware Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article implies post-exposure risk of attacker-directed configuration changes to exposed PLCs. No use cases generated for detecting PLC state tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized writes to PLC configuration files, firmware upload attempts, or changes to ladder-logic programs. Alert on process spawning engineering tools (Rockwell Studio, Allen-Bradley apps) from unprivileged accounts or off-network sources. Track changes to backup/restore operations on PLC devices.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Internet-Facing PLC to Internal SCADA Network
suggestion.rationale: Exposed PLC as beachhead into water utility infrastructure. No kill-chain mapping of post-exposure pivot attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect connections from DMZ/internet-facing PLC subnets to internal engineering networks or SCADA control planes. Alert on unexpected outbound connections from PLC initiating network enumeration (arp, nbtstat, ipconfig) or lateral scan patterns. Monitor for tunneling or proxy-like behavior from compromised PLC.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution or Script Activity on Exposed PLC
suggestion.rationale: No detection use cases for remote code execution or command injection on Rockwell systems post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process spawning on PLC engineering interfaces (cmd.exe, PowerShell, shell execution). Alert on script activity (.vbs, .ps1) launched from PLC web interfaces or remote-access sessions. Flag execution of non-standard tools on PLC-attached workstations.

suggestion.title: Geolocation Enrichment: PLC Exposure Correlates with Known Water-Attack Cities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links exposure to 'water attack cities'—geolocation-based targeting intelligence absent from pipeline. No threat-actor correlation or historical attack pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference the 22 exposed PLCs in 'water attack cities' against known water infrastructure attack timelines (e.g., Oldsmar, FL 2021; Chesapeake Bay 2024). Alert if exposed PLC geolocations overlap with municipalities that experienced prior water-treatment incidents. Escalate if threat actor infrastructure has previously scanned these cities.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation Against Oracle Database
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'SQL Injection Into Windows SYSTEM Access' as the entry vector; pipeline failed to map initial access phase despite clear attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal SQL query patterns, error-based injection attempts, and successful code execution payloads sent to Oracle listener ports (1521/TCP). Correlate with subsequent process spawning from ORACLE.EXE or Oracle agent processes.

suggestion.title: Code Compilation Within Oracle Database Context
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'Compile khunt Inside Oracle'—indicates attacker executed compiled code (CLR module, PL/SQL procedure, or Java class) within the database; zero detection artifacts generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loadable module creation (*.dll, *.so, *.class) written to Oracle directories or temporary paths, or invocation of Oracle CLR assembly loading procedures (dbms_java, external procedures). Correlate with unexpected child processes spawned from oracle.exe with elevated tokens.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Database Service Account to SYSTEM
suggestion.rationale: Article headline promises SYSTEM-level access via database exploitation; pipeline did not model the escalation mechanism or detection triggers despite this being the attack's critical outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with SYSTEM privileges initiated from ORACLE.EXE or SQL Server processes (SQLSERVR.EXE), unusual token manipulation, or unexpected service account impersonation. Alert on Kerberos delegation changes or SID-history injection artifacts.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Database-Spawned System Process
suggestion.rationale: Successful escalation to SYSTEM suggests attacker maintains execution context; article implies khunt persists or establishes foothold at OS level post-escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scheduled tasks, registry run keys, or service installations created by processes spawned from ORACLE.EXE or SQL service accounts. Flag binaries executed with SYSTEM privileges that trace execution ancestry to database processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious khunt Tool Execution or Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: The tool 'khunt' is named explicitly in the title but not extracted as an IOC or artifact; implies hash, command-line, file path, or behavioral signature of this tool was overlooked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution, file creation, or DLL injection involving 'khunt' binary or named variants. Correlate with obfuscation indicators, non-standard process parentage, or execution from %TEMP% or Oracle directories. Hash and detonate any khunt samples for behavioral analysis.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration or Command Execution Post-SYSTEM Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful SYSTEM-level compromise; no detection coverage for post-exploitation activity (lateral movement, data collection, or command-and-control) that typically follows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections from processes running as SYSTEM that were spawned by database services, unusual command-line execution from cmd.exe or powershell.exe with SYSTEM privileges, and data staging to network shares or external IPs.

suggestion.title: Agent Tool Execution Without Model Inference Validation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Attackers Trigger Tools Without Running the Model'—the core attack is direct tool invocation bypassing the model decision layer. This is the primary detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect agent API calls to tool endpoints (AWS Bedrock agent actions, Vertex tool execution, Vercel AI tool calls) that arrive without preceding model-inference validation steps. Monitor for tool invocation logs that lack corresponding model decision/reasoning metadata.

suggestion.title: Malformed Agent Framework API Requests
suggestion.rationale: Bypassing model execution implies crafted requests with unexpected parameter ordering or missing validation fields. Title implies request-level exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag agent API requests where tool-execution parameters are present but model-routing fields are missing, null, or malformed. Detect tool-call schemas submitted directly to agent backends without intermediate model-generated wrapper structures.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Tool Execution via Agent Capability Bypass
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability allows executing agent tools that should require model approval. Detectable as tool actions outside policy/context boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on agent-framework tool executions (function calls, external API invocations) that lack audit-trail evidence of model-initiated requests. Correlate tool-execution logs with model-decision logs—orphaned tool calls indicate bypass.

suggestion.title: Agent Platform Exploitation via Unauthenticated or Replay Tokens
suggestion.rationale: 'Trigger tools without running model' suggests session/token abuse rather than code injection. May involve credential replay or service-principal misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent API authentication for reused tokens, replayed JWTs, or API calls from suspicious/new service principals. Flag tool-execution requests authenticated with credentials not previously associated with that agent or user.

suggestion.title: CVE-Based Exploitation Detection for AWS/Google/Vercel Agents
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability in major cloud platforms should map to assigned CVE(s) once public. Title names three vendors, implying coordinated disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once CVE identifiers are published, detect exploitation via HTTP request signatures targeting agent endpoints (e.g., `/agents/action`, `/bedrock/invoke`, `/vertex/predict`). Monitor for version-fingerprinting probes of agent APIs.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Root Shell Access to Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states backdoor 'opens unauthenticated root shells'—this is the core compromise. Article establishes direct root access without credentials as the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/Telnet connections to router management interfaces (ports 22, 23, 80, 443) originating from suspicious sources or followed immediately by root-level commands. Flag any process execution as root UID 0 on router devices without corresponding authentication logs in management interface.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Firmware Modifications on Network Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor ships in firmware pre-installation ('Chinese-Made Zbtlink Routers Ship With Backdoor')—firmware integrity is the persistence mechanism. Article implies supply-chain compromise at manufacturing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor router firmware version and checksum against known-good baseline. Alert on unexpected firmware downgrades, rollbacks to earlier versions, or firmware updates from untrusted sources. Cross-reference firmware MD5/SHA hashes against threat intel feeds for known-backdoored builds.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Initiating from Compromised Router Devices
suggestion.rationale: Compromised routers with root access can pivot to internal networks. Title indicates persistent root access implies the device can launch secondary attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any new network connections or command-and-control outbound attempts originating from router management interfaces to internal subnets or external IP ranges. Detect attempts to enumerate or brute-force adjacent network devices from router source IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply-Chain Compromise via Pre-Installed Backdoors
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes backdoor is pre-installed by manufacturer ('Ship With Backdoor'), indicating supply-chain compromise affecting entire device batch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device procurement dates, serial numbers, and firmware versions against threat intel on known-compromised hardware batches. Alert on deployments of Zbtlink router models/versions identified in supply-chain advisories. Track firmware build dates and manufacturer signatures for anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Backdoor Command Execution via Management Interface Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor enables 'unauthenticated root shells'—implies ability to execute arbitrary commands without authentication. This bypasses normal access controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor router management interface logs (telnet, SSH, HTTP admin panel) for commands executed without corresponding successful authentication events. Detect shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, >, <) in HTTP GET/POST parameters to router admin endpoints. Flag process execution on router with UID 0 lacking corresponding login sessions.

suggestion.title: Ransom Cartel Encryption Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Silnikau 'supplied members with...software designed to encrypt victims' computers' deployed across 18 companies 2021–2023. Medical technology firm disrupted for two months in August 2022 confirms encryption impact. Detection must cover file encryption footprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid-sequence file encryption operations targeting common data extensions (.doc, .docx, .xls, .pdf, .zip). Correlate with ransom note creation (text files containing 'bitcoin', 'payment', 'decrypt' keywords) and shadow-copy deletion commands (vssadmin, cipher.exe). Ransom Cartel typically encrypts entire departments' file shares within 1–4 hours of initial access.

suggestion.title: Initial Access Broker Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states Silnikau 'worked with initial access brokers who supplied access to compromised corporate networks' and 'supplied members with...stolen credentials for compromised computers'. Detection must capture credential reuse patterns from IAB handoffs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logons using credentials from public breaches or threat feeds (correlate with HIBP, Breach Brief, BreachDirectory). Flag logins from non-business geolocations during off-hours immediately followed by lateral movement to servers, domain controllers, or backup systems. Ransom Cartel affiliates typically enumerate high-value targets within 2–6 hours of initial foothold.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to External Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes threat actors 'stole corporate data' and threatened 'publicly leaked' disclosure. Law firm attacks (May 2023) with disruption lasting 'days to multiple months' indicate staged data collection before encryption. Detection must cover bulk data transfers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large outbound SMB/HTTPS transfers to external IPs, especially from file servers to bulletproof hosting ranges. Monitor for data staging in temporary directories (AppData/Local/Temp, ProgramData) before external transfer. Ransom Cartel typically exfiltrates 10–500 GB per victim over 1–7 days prior to encryption trigger.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mixer Payments from Enterprise Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states Silnikau 'transmitted ransom payments through cryptocurrency mixers to make it harder for law enforcement to trace the funds'. Law firms paid $125K and $300K ransoms; detection must flag mixing service contact from compromised systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on outbound HTTPS/DNS queries to known cryptocurrency mixer domains (Tornado Cash, Sinbad, ChipMixer, etc.) from any corporate device. Monitor for blockchain explorer access (blockchain.com, etherscan.io) from systems involved in ransomware incidents. Ransom payment flows via mixers occur within 24–72 hours of victim ransom note delivery.

suggestion.title: Ransom Cartel Leak Site Monitoring and Victim Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Silnikau 'communicating with victims, negotiate ransom demands' via an affiliate website. Organizations must correlate internal incidents with dark web leak site postings to confirm Ransom Cartel attribution and assess data exposure scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference company name, employee count, and industry against known Ransom Cartel leak site archives and victim-shaming posts. Timeline matching (incident date ± 14 days, matching file metadata and sample counts) confirms attribution. Ransom Cartel has historically posted victim previews 3–10 days after exfiltration completion.

suggestion.title: Affiliate Tool Kit Acquisition and Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes Silnikau 'recruited other cybercriminals through underground forums' and 'supplied members with information and tools used in the intrusions'. Detection should identify affiliate-hosted infrastructure and tool distribution artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ransom Cartel affiliate kit artifacts: directory structures (/tools, /payloads, /creds), configuration files with target lists, batch credential-stuffing scripts, and web shells. Monitor Apache/Nginx logs on compromised infrastructure for unusual endpoints (/affiliate, /admin, /login, /panel). Database dumps (MySQL, SQLite) containing affiliate earnings records and victim ransom negotiation logs are forensic gold.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol' — attacker must first enumerate TeamCity assets and agent endpoints. Pipeline omitted asset exposure hunting entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for internet-accessible TeamCity instances (ports 8111, agent polling ranges) with no authentication gates. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-63077 CVSS vector 'Requires No Privileges' and vulnerability scanner results for unpatched TeamCity builds.

suggestion.title: Malicious Agent Polling Protocol Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'agent polling protocol' attack vector and 'deserialization of untrusted data' root cause. Pipeline ignored the specific delivery mechanism for payload injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent endpoints for POST/binary payloads with serialized Java objects (magic bytes indicating ObjectInputStream). Flag requests lacking valid agent authentication tokens. Alert on Java deserialization exceptions in TeamCity logs correlating with inbound requests.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Service Crash and Anomalous Restart
suggestion.rationale: Deserialization exploits commonly cause immediate service crashes. Article's 'untrusted data' vulnerability creates obvious detection: service disruption during exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TeamCity service restart cycles (<5 min uptime following crash). Correlate crashes with suspicious network requests to agent polling endpoints in preceding window. Alert if crashes follow requests from non-internal IP ranges or lack corresponding build job context.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution Under TeamCity Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE via deserialization yields arbitrary code execution. Article's 'unauthenticated remote code execution' means successful exploitation spawns attacker commands within TeamCity service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash spawned by TeamCity build service account. Flag interpreter execution without corresponding build job ID in TeamCity audit logs. Alert on suspicious tools (curl, wget, nc) launched from TeamCity process tree.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Credential Store and Artifact Access
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE grants attacker access to stored build credentials, SSH keys, cloud tokens. Article implies full system compromise but pipeline missed post-exploitation reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity config directories for unexpected file access to stored credentials, SSH key directories, or secret files. Flag processes under TeamCity context opening .git/credentials, .aws/, ~/.ssh/. Alert on access to TeamCity's internal password vault files.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'public-facing application' and 'unauthenticated remote code execution.' Asset exposure hunt is mandatory for CISA KEV entries. Missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate TeamCity service fingerprints (port 8111, Java HTTP headers, TeamCity banner) against internet-facing asset inventory. Alert on any exposed TeamCity instance without documented business justification or defensive controls (WAF, geofencing, VPN).

suggestion.title: Malicious Serialized Object in Agent Polling Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'deserialization of untrusted data via the agent polling protocol.' This is the core exploit vector and must have its own detection, not just vulnerability scanner coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate TeamCity agent polling patterns (frequency, payload size, source subnets). Alert on agent communication containing serialized Java objects with gadget chain indicators, unusual payload sizes >1MB, or requests from non-agent IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution from TeamCity Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability outcome as 'unauthenticated remote code execution.' Must detect execution phase post-exploitation with process-level observables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from TeamCity runtime (java.exe or javaw.exe) executing shells, script interpreters, or LOLBins. Particularly suspicious: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe, certutil.exe, curl/wget from TeamCity context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance vs. Scanner Alerts
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Federal due date is 2026-08-08. Must correlate scanner detections against actual patch status, not just assume vulnerability exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Nessus/Qualys CVE-2026-63077 detections against last patch date in asset management. Escalate any device flagged vulnerable within 7 days of federal due date or where patch date predates vulnerability publication.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Agent Registration or Polling Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly names 'agent polling protocol' as the entry point. Reconnaissance or lateral movement could manifest as unusual agent behavior before or after exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TeamCity agents registering from unexpected network segments, agents with mismatched credentials, excessive polling attempts in short windows, or agents going offline immediately after exploitation window.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Asset Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for all TeamCity instances and their installed versions. Identify anything < fixed version. Generate report by business unit / owner. Track patch implementation status and flag 2026-08-08 deadline escalations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-TeamCity RCE
suggestion.rationale: After successful RCE on TeamCity server, attacker will pivot to other infrastructure. TeamCity often has credentials/SSH keys in environment or credentials store.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting TeamCity RCE execution, hunt for SSH connections from the TeamCity host to other infrastructure, credential file access (/root/.ssh, Windows credential manager), and stored build credentials being queried.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and KEV implies active exploitation against 'public-facing applications'—indicates exposed instances are primary target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify JetBrains TeamCity instances accessible from untrusted networks on port 8111 or via vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-63077. Correlate with public internet accessibility scans (Shodan, Censys patterns).

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—this is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic (typically port 9000) for serialized payload anomalies, base64-encoded gadget chains, or abnormal connection patterns from non-TeamCity server IPs. Look for deserialization error logs followed by RCE.

suggestion.title: Post-TeamCity-Exploitation Process Chain
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in 'remote code execution'—attacker gains ability to spawn arbitrary processes with TeamCity service privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process spawning from TeamCity java processes (java.exe running cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash). Escalation from SYSTEM or application-service account to admin-equivalent. Focus on processes outside expected CI/CD operations (builds, deployments).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2026-63077
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-63077 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and federal patch due-date is 2026-08-08—this is primary detection hook.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger alerting on vulnerability scanner reports detecting CVE-2026-63077 in any TeamCity instance. Cross-reference patch dates against federal deadline (2026-08-08) to identify compliance risk. Prioritize exposed / internet-facing TeamCity instances.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Traffic to TeamCity Default Ports
suggestion.rationale: Before exploitation of 'public-facing applications,' attackers enumerate targets via network scanning—prerequisite to CVE-2026-63077 exploitation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning or probing traffic to TeamCity default ports (8111, 9000) from external or suspicious IPs. Look for HTTP requests to /.TeamCity paths, /admin paths, or agent discovery endpoints. Volume-based anomaly detection on failed connection attempts to TeamCity infrastructure.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Unexpected Outbound Blockchain Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ChainDrop as self-propagating worm via npm packages using Ethereum smart contracts for C2 routing. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for installation-time execution or anomalous network patterns to blockchain infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build/dev environments for npm install processes initiating outbound connections to Ethereum RPC endpoints or blockchain nodes (e.g., Infura, Alchemy). Look for post_install or preinstall scripts spawning curl/wget to web3 protocol handlers. Establish baseline of expected blockchain traffic and alert on new destinations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Environment Secret Exfiltration via HTTP/DNS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions extraction of GitHub Actions runner secrets; pipeline generated no detection for credential access phase. This is a core attack vector for supply-chain expansion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any GitHub Actions runner process (actions/runner@*) that reads environment variables matching patterns like GITHUB_TOKEN, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET and subsequently makes HTTP requests or DNS queries with base64/URL-encoded values in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with unusual destination IPs or domains outside trusted CI/CD infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion Attack via Local npm Registry Override
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating npm worm implies horizontal spread through shared dependencies and registry poisoning. Pipeline did not surface detection for typosquatting or registry-override attack vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .npmrc file modifications in user home directories and project roots for registry redirects pointing to non-standard hosts. Detect npm install commands targeting packages with names similar to internal/popular packages (Levenshtein distance <2). Alert on installations where version numbers jump unexpectedly or pre/post-install scripts are added to previously clean package versions.

suggestion.title: Ethereum Smart Contract Interaction from CI/CD Runner
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies blockchain-based C2 via smart contracts; pipeline mapped zero command-and-control detection. This represents a novel evasion technique requiring specific blockchain protocol monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Ethereum RPC calls and smart contract ABIs contacted by development/CI environments. Alert on new contract interaction patterns, particularly ethers.js or web3.js library usage in build logs combined with network connections to Ethereum mainnet/testnet nodes. Look for hardcoded contract addresses or ABI URLs in downloaded npm packages.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Poisoned Dependency Across Repository Network
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating worm implies cross-repository infection via shared internal dependencies. Pipeline did not flag horizontal spread detection for monorepo or workspace-based npm installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install commands across multiple repositories/workspaces on shared CI runners for installation of identical malicious transitive dependency versions within short time windows. Flag if a single compromised package version appears in lock files across multiple projects owned by different teams. Correlate with outbound connections to same C2 infrastructure from different runner instances.

suggestion.title: npm Package Publish Activity from Compromised CI/CD Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating behavior implies automated re-publishing of poisoned packages or new variants. Pipeline generated zero detection for malicious package publication or registry manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish API calls from CI/CD runners outside official release pipelines. Alert on publish requests that include preinstall/postinstall script modifications or new dependencies added to package.json. Cross-reference npm registry audit logs for package versions published from unusual IP ranges or at atypical hours. Flag version bumps that skip expected semantic versioning patches.

suggestion.title: Vishing + Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing for Session Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes UNC6671 contacting employees on personal phones, spoofing help desk, directing to fake domains hosting 'adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits designed to steal credentials and session cookies in real time.' This multi-stage social engineering attack is core TTP missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails or SMS referencing MFA/passkey enrollment or password updates, directing to domains mimicking corporate identity. Correlate with vishing call reports (ticketing system, employee surveys). Alert on credential submission to non-corporate domains; flag AitM patterns (certificate mismatches, cookie exfiltration attempts).

suggestion.title: Okta/Microsoft 365 SSO Dashboard Abuse After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'after stealing Microsoft 365 or Okta single-sign-on accounts, the attackers log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account.' Represents credential_access→lateral_movement into centralized cloud identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Okta or O365 logins from anomalous geoIP/ASN, followed by immediate enumeration of SSO dashboard apps or token refresh storms. Flag logins without expected MFA step or from impossible-travel IPs. Monitor for session token creation across multiple cloud platforms in rapid succession post-login.

suggestion.title: Automated Bulk Data Exfiltration Across Multiple Cloud Services
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'hackers then use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to.' This indicates rapid, scripted access to all platforms linked via single SSO compromise—distinct from targeted single-app theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single user account accessing and downloading large volumes from multiple cloud services (Salesforce, Slack, Confluence, etc.) within 10-30 minute window. Flag bulk export operations (all-users reports, database dumps) preceded by SSO token reuse. Monitor for scripted API calls across disparate platforms from single source IP.

suggestion.title: Systematic Deletion of Security Notifications and Password-Reset Emails
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'delete security notifications and password-reset emails from compromised inboxes.' This is a specific defense-evasion tactic to prevent detection and disable recovery options post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor mailbox AuditLog for bulk deletion of emails from system accounts (Azure AD notifications, Office 365 alerts, password management services). Alert on deletion of messages containing keywords: 'security', 'alert', 'suspicious', 'password reset', 'verify identity' shortly after account compromise indicator (first login anomaly). Flag deletions performed via PowerShell or unusual client.

suggestion.title: Help Desk Spoofing Requests for MFA/Passkey Re-enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes UNC6671 'contact[ing] employees on their personal mobile phones while spoofing corporate help-desks and claiming that workers need to enroll in passkeys or update their multi-factor authentication settings.' This is the initial-access vehicle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vishing reports (employee-reported suspicious calls claiming to be IT) with phishing emails/SMS sent same day to same cohort. Monitor for MFA re-enrollment campaigns not initiated by helpdesk ticketing system. Alert on requests to enroll in passkeys or MFA to external URLs or unfamiliar domains. Flag bulk outreach claiming urgent security updates.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Discovery and Enumeration Post-SSO Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers log into SSO dashboard to gain 'access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account.' Implies discovery phase scanning available apps tied to compromised identity before selective or bulk exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential API calls to enumerate cloud apps, app catalogs, or accessible services immediately post-login to SSO dashboard. Flag access to Okta Catalog API or O365 discovery endpoints within minutes of anomalous login. Monitor for enumeration patterns (attempting access to 10+ distinct cloud services with matching timestamp deltas) by single account.

suggestion.title: KVM Guest-to-Host Escape Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'privileged L1 guest code escape to Linux hosts'—describes privilege escalation via hypervisor boundary violation. Pipeline generated no use cases for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on guest-spawned processes attempting direct hardware access, ioctl calls to KVM device files from elevated guest contexts, or attempts to map guest memory regions to host space. Monitor for abnormal vcpu exit handlers or attempts to abuse KVM-specific syscalls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious KVM Kernel Module Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is in KVM kernel module itself. Article phrase 'KVM Flaw' indicates kernel-level exploitation. No detection logic for KVM-specific module abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loading of KVM modules after initial compromise, suspicious open/close of /dev/kvm from non-qemu processes, or ioctl sequences known to exploit KVM state machine. Alert on attempts to read/write KVM vCPU state outside normal hypervisor operation.

suggestion.title: Hypervisor Escape via Memory Mapping Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Guest escape attacks typically exploit memory management. Article indicates L1 guest (nested hypervisor / privileged guest) can escape—memory isolation failure. No use case for detecting memory mapping abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for guests attempting mmap of privileged memory regions, requests for page table modifications outside guest scope, or side-channel probing patterns (Spectre/Meltdown-style) targeting host kernel. Flag attempts to establish cross-VM communication channels.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Guest Administrator to Host Root
suggestion.rationale: Attack path is explicit: privileged (admin-level) guest code → host escape. No detection use case for this specific escalation vector within virtualized environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In hypervisor host OS, detect spawning of processes or opening of resources initiated from guest VM contexts with privileges elevating beyond guest boundary. Monitor for unexpected process creation triggered by KVM process, especially those gaining host-level capabilities.

suggestion.title: Traefik ReplacePathRegex configuration audit — unsanitized capture groups
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'regex that captures user-controlled path segments without a mandatory separator (for example `regex: "^/api(.*)"`, `replacement: "/$1"`)'. No UC hunts for this dangerous pattern in traefik.yml or dynamic.yml configs.
log_sources: Web access logs with traefik config paths
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for traefik YAML configs (dynamic.yml, traefik.yml, traefik.toml) containing ReplacePathRegex middleware where replacement uses $1/$2 capture groups without explicit path separators (e.g., `replacement: "/$1"` without delimiter validation). Compare against baseline configurations.

suggestion.title: Traefik middleware chain bypass — successful auth re-entry on path-traversal request
suggestion.rationale: Article describes traversal bypassing auth middleware entirely. No UC explicitly hunts for request pairs: (1) legitimate request denied by auth middleware (401/403), (2) traversal variant of same endpoint succeeds (2xx) — the actual bypass signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlation: same source sends request to `/admin` → 403, then `/api/../admin` or `/../admin` → 200/302 within 60 seconds. Indicates successful middleware bypass chain on same Traefik instance.

suggestion.title: Traefik version fingerprint in error responses — CVE-2026-65600 affected versions
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify patched vs. vulnerable versions, but operational security hunt would fingerprint Traefik version from HTTP Server headers, error messages, or Traefik dashboard exposure to identify at-risk instances before detection of actual exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses with Server: traefik/X.Y.Z headers or Traefik dashboard exposure (typical port 8080 or 8081, path /dashboard or /ping). Correlate version against known-vulnerable range for CVE-2026-65600.

suggestion.title: Protected route access pattern change post-traversal — new source accessing admin/internal routes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes auth bypass enabling access to protected routes (implied: admin panel). No UC hunts for behavioral change: source IP suddenly accessing previously-denied admin endpoints after traversal probe attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: track which sources access `/admin`, `/internal`, `/api/admin` → see 403/401. Alert if same source later accesses these routes with 2xx response after prior traversal attempt (`%2e%2e`, `/../` patterns) within 10-minute window.

suggestion.title: Interrupt Descriptor Table (IDT) or Interrupt Handler Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Interrupt Injection Attack' — this is the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero UCs for interrupt handler interception or IDT manipulation despite this being core to the threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged process access to IDT registers, exception handler vectors, or kernel-mode interrupt controller memory regions. Alert on allocation of code at addresses matching exception handler entry points or modification of saved exception handler pointers.

suggestion.title: IBRS/IBPB/STIBP MSR Tampering or Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'bypasses Spectre v2 defenses' — Spectre v2 mitigations are implemented via MSR 0x48, 0x49, 0x4B writes. Pipeline failed to generate detection for MSR manipulation or mitigation disabling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WRMSR instructions targeting Spectre v2 MSRs (IBRS=0x48, IBPB=0x49, STIBP=0x4B) from user-mode contexts. Monitor for repeated MSR reads followed by modified writes that indicate speculative execution state manipulation.

suggestion.title: Speculative Execution Probe via Exception-Based Timing Side Channel
suggestion.rationale: Interrupt injection facilitates speculative execution exploitation; article premise is bypassing existing Spectre v2 defenses. Pipeline missed detection for exception-generation loops used to measure cache/timing behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-frequency exception generation (divide-by-zero, page fault loops) used to build timing oracles. Alert on tight loops executing privileged instructions that read/modify CPU speculation controls (SPEC_CTRL, ARCH_CAPABILITIES).

suggestion.title: Cross-Core Interrupt or IPI-Based Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Interrupt injection on multi-core systems (mentioned: 'Intel and AMD CPUs') enables lateral code execution. Pipeline created zero UC for inter-processor interrupt (IPI) abuse or multi-core attack coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes generating or receiving IPI sequences, accessing inter-processor communication channels, or correlating exception spikes across multiple CPU cores. Flag unusual CPU_PAUSE instruction sequences used to synchronize multi-core attacks.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Callback or Exception Handler Hooking via Interrupt Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Interrupt injection can redirect kernel exception handlers. Pipeline failed to model detection for syscalls registering/modifying kernel callbacks or exception-handler redirection via interrupt table manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user-mode processes calling syscalls that register exception handlers (signal() on Unix, SetUnhandledExceptionFilter on Windows). Correlate with memory allocations and code writes targeting exception-handler memory regions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Asset Exposure Hunt (TeamCity)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is actively exploited (CISA KEV) and affects 'public-facing' TeamCity installations. Federal agencies have specific remediation deadline (2026-08-08), requiring immediate inventory of exposed instances. Core gap: 'Vendor / Product: JetBrains TeamCity Deserialization of Untrusted Data'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management tools for TeamCity installations with version <patch version>. Cross-reference against network scans for port 8111 or 80/443 with TeamCity banners. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Flag for mandatory patching by 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly specified as 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Article does not specify authentication requirement, suggesting protocol accepts unauthenticated payloads. Phrase: 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to TeamCity agent polling protocol endpoints (typically port 9090 or custom agent port) from external/untrusted networks. Flag connection attempts that do not present valid TeamCity agent credentials or certificates. Correlate with process execution events on the TeamCity server.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization RCE via TeamCity Agent
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'deserialization of untrusted data' leading to 'remote code execution.' This is a Java serialization gadget chain attack pattern. Phrase: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Java process logs and network traffic from TeamCity agent processes for indicators of serialized object deserialization attacks (ObjectInputStream, gadget library references, CommonsCollections, etc.). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from TeamCity JVM after agent polling connections. Signature-match for common Java deserialization payloads.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Process Execution Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: RCE via agent polling results in arbitrary code execution in the context of TeamCity agent/server processes. Article implies post-compromise execution environment. Need to detect suspicious process execution spawned from TeamCity contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when TeamCity agent or server processes (java.exe with -Dteamcity flag, teamcity-agent.exe, etc.) spawn unexpected child processes, especially: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, python, or processes not in TeamCity whitelist. Validate parent-child relationships against baseline. Prioritize rare or never-before-seen commands.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Directory/Registry Tampering Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in RCE; attacker gains ability to modify TeamCity configuration, install persistence, or stage lateral-movement tools. File/registry changes in TeamCity home directory indicate compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes/modifications to TeamCity installation directory (typically C:\\ProgramData\\JetBrains\\TeamCity, /opt/teamcity, etc.) and registry keys (HKLM\\Software\\JetBrains\\TeamCity). Flag: new plugins, config.xml modifications, JAR/ZIP uploads, or batch scripts in plugins directory. Cross-correlate with suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Behavioral Anomaly (Network Signature)
suggestion.rationale: Agent polling protocol is a specific, structured communication channel. RCE exploitation will produce malformed or anomalous payloads. Phrase: 'via the agent polling protocol' implies protocol-level detection is viable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of valid TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic (payload sizes, intervals, authentication handshake patterns). Alert on: oversized payloads, rapid request spikes, protocol violations (malformed headers), or traffic from non-agent IP ranges. Correlate with IDS signatures for Java serialization attacks.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol' as the attack vector. No use case generated for detecting agent protocol abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (/agent, /agentListener) from external/unexpected sources without prior authentication. TeamCity agents should only poll from known internal build systems; unsolicited external agent connections indicate exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: TeamCity RCE via Java Deserialization Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability' as the root cause. Unauthenticated exploitation via agent protocol likely delivers serialized payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity process spawning unusual children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) following POST requests to agent endpoints. Correlate with exception logs containing 'ObjectInputStream' or deserialization errors. RCE post-exploitation should show process creation originating from TeamCity JVM.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scan & Patch Lag Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and CISA KEV status means active exploitation. Must hunt for unpatched/unscanned instances despite scanner noise. Federal due: 2026-08-08.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for TeamCity instances (all versions prior to patched release) present in vulnerability scanner results after 2026-08-08 deadline. Cross-reference scanner exemptions/silenced findings against active process monitoring. Unpatched instances in CISA KEV post-deadline indicate patch failure or discovery gap—escalate for manual verification even if scanner reports 'remediated.'

suggestion.title: Public Exposure of TeamCity Agent Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' only works if TeamCity is exposed. Article implies external attackers can reach agent polling protocol; detection should verify external reachability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TeamCity instances accessible from public IP ranges on default/common agent polling ports (typically 8161, 80, 443). Cross-reference with internal asset inventory; externally-accessible instances require immediate network segmentation review. Use external scanning (Shodan, Censys) to find overlooked exposures.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Connection Anomalies & Timing Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'agent polling protocol' as exploit vector. Normal polling follows predictable frequency; exploitation likely deviates (burst requests, out-of-band timing, abnormal source IPs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal agent polling frequency and source IPs per TeamCity environment. Flag POST requests to agent endpoints with: (a) inter-arrival time <1min (burst attack), (b) source IPs never seen polling before, (c) requests outside of normal build window times. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or exception logs.

suggestion.title: Regulatory Compliance Alert: CISA KEV Remediation Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08' and CISA KEV status triggers mandatory remediation. Deadline-based compliance detection was not generated despite explicit date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create alert workflow: on federal due date (2026-08-08), query all asset inventories for CVE-2026-63077 unpatched instances. Auto-escalate non-compliant assets to CISO/compliance; track remediation across full fleet. Archive scan results for regulatory audit trail.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Asset Exposure & Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution; pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the canonical detection posture for CISA KEV entries with federal due dates (2026-08-08).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for TeamCity instances scanning positive for CVE-2026-63077. Cross-reference against patch timeline; flag instances not remediated by federal due date as exploitable.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Deserialization Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation occurs 'via the agent polling protocol' through 'deserialization of untrusted data'—pipeline missed this as the primary attack surface despite it being the exploit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or anomalous payloads sent to TeamCity agent polling endpoints. Baseline expected agent protocol traffic and alert on serialized object patterns, codec exceptions, or protocol violations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Command Execution from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution'—pipeline did not surface post-exploitation execution detection despite this being the attack outcome and highest-fidelity kill-chain indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawning or command execution under TeamCity agent process contexts. Establish baseline of legitimate agent activity; alert on deviations, especially processes spawned without corresponding logged build/pipeline actions.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Public Surface Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies exposed TeamCity instances are the attack vector ('public-facing application' context per T1190 recommendation); pipeline missed reconnaissance detection for unauthenticated probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated requests to TeamCity APIs and web endpoints, particularly agent-polling and build-retrieval paths. Alert on patterns consistent with exploit probing or reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV-listed (active in-the-wild exploitation) with explicit federal patch due date—pipeline failed to surface use case for continuous scanner drift and patch-lag detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results against patch management systems; flag TeamCity instances reporting remediated status that still scan positive for CVE-2026-63077 (patch lag indicator). Escalate instances with >7-day remediation delay as high-risk.

suggestion.title: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs to 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for this CVE; this is the primary IOC. Pipeline extracted nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any TeamCity instance in scanner output. Cross-reference asset inventory against vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-63077 presence. Prioritize internet-facing hosts. Track remediation status against federal deadline (2026-08-08).

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote code execution' requiring external network access; must detect exposed TeamCity endpoints (port 8111/8110 default).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for external inbound connections to TeamCity ports on systems not designated internet-facing. Monitor DNS for TeamCity subdomain resolution from external sources. Correlate with asset inventory to surface rogue/unaccounted public deployments.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'via the agent polling protocol' as attack surface; this is the precise exploitation vector requiring network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect agent polling protocol traffic for malformed or obfuscated serialized Java objects. Alert on unauthenticated agent registration attempts. Monitor for anomalous payload sizes or structures in polling requests. Correlate failed auth attempts with subsequent process execution.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Shell Spawn from Java/TeamCity Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote code execution' implying active payload execution; must detect child process indicators of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on java.exe or catalina.exe (TeamCity container) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or sh. Flag especially when parent is network-connected or spawns network utilities. Baseline normal TeamCity process tree for your environment.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Java Deserialization Activity
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'deserialization of untrusted data'; detection must target the underlying exploitation technique, not just surface indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity/Java process logs for deserialization exceptions (StreamCorruptedException, ClassNotFoundException). Correlate with network traffic showing unusual serialized-object patterns in agent polling protocol. Flag spikes in deserialization errors from external sources.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Deadline Tracking and Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08'; given 'currently exploited in the wild' status and regulatory requirements, deadline compliance is mandatory hunting requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all TeamCity systems. Track patch status against CVE-2026-63077. Generate compliance dashboard with remediation countdown. Escalate to leadership 7 days pre-deadline if unpatched assets remain. Flag post-deadline unpatched systems as critical incident.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states KEV entry targets 'exposed assets' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' No asset-discovery UC generated despite explicit guidance. Attackers need to find publicly accessible TeamCity instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS traffic to default TeamCity ports (8111, 9090) from external networks. Alert on successful HTTP 200/302 responses to TeamCity paths (/login, /admin, /agents). Track DNS queries resolving to internal TeamCity hostnames from external sources.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' This is the exact attack vector; no UC maps to agent protocol exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically port 9090) for requests without valid agent tokens or from anomalous source IPs. Look for large payload sizes in agent protocol traffic (>1MB) or sequences of failed handshakes followed by rapid reconnects.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Execution via CVE-2026-63077
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution' but no execution-phase UC exists. Attackers achieving RCE will spawn processes; this gap leaves post-exploitation invisible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from TeamCity service process (particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash). Monitor for TeamCity service performing file I/O to temporary directories immediately followed by new process launches. Track unusual network connections initiated by TeamCity child processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'CVE-2026-63077 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' No UC for vulnerability detection/remediation tracking was generated despite direct recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner inventory for TeamCity versions <12.2 and all versions 2024.x before 2024.12.1 (CVE advisory boundaries). Flag any instance with vulnerability finding for CVE-2026-63077 as high-priority remediation.
