suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for oversized, malformed, or high-entropy agent polling requests. Flag requests containing binary serialization markers (Java serialization magic bytes 0xaced0005) or Base64-encoded payloads in agent protocol handshake. Alert on rapid agent registration attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Build Job Injection
suggestion.rationale: RCE via agent protocol enables execution of arbitrary build steps. Article confirms 'unauthenticated' path, so jobs can be triggered/modified without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect build jobs triggered from anonymous agents or external IP ranges with zero authentication tokens. Flag build steps containing shell metacharacters, curl/wget/powershell, or reverse-shell payloads. Alert on builds spawning processes outside normal TeamCity agent scope.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Asset Exposure & Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template and emphasizes federal patch due date 2026-08-08. Pipeline produced zero use cases despite clear guidance and CISA KEV prioritization requiring immediate asset inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-exposed TeamCity instances via service enumeration, certificate logs, or network scanning. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-63077 and prioritize remediation by federal due date. CISA KEV entries indicate active exploitation—patch lag is the primary attack vector.

suggestion.title: Malicious Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—this specific attack vector requires protocol-level detection entirely absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent polling protocol traffic for serialized Java object payloads (magic bytes AC ED 00 05), unusual request sequences, payload size anomalies, or requests from unauthenticated sources. Correlate exploitation attempts with subsequent process spawning or network connections.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Process Execution from TeamCity Java Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE via Java deserialization necessarily involves process execution—execution-phase detection completely absent despite being inevitable post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where java.exe instances with TeamCity arguments spawn unexpected children: shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash), script engines, or diagnostic tools. Flag deviations from baseline TeamCity process spawning behavior.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 or Reverse Shell from Compromised TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE exploitation enables reverse shell establishment and C2 callback—command-and-control phase absent despite being standard post-exploitation progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from TeamCity server to unknown or reputation-flagged IP addresses on non-standard ports. Alert on encrypted tunneling protocols (SSH, encrypted proxies) initiated from TeamCity process context outside normal operational baselines.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'via the agent polling protocol' with 'unauthenticated remote code execution'. No detection rule was generated for this primary attack vector despite clear technical description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (typically /agent or /polling paths) from external/untrusted networks. Flag requests with binary serialized Java object payloads (magic bytes 0xaced0500) or abnormal Content-Type headers. Correlate with unpatched TeamCity asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Service Asset Inventory and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes public-facing application exploitation with federal patch due date 2026-08-08. Pipeline generated no compliance hunt despite CISA KEV's mandate that agencies must remediate by deadline—a primary use case for this threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for TeamCity deployments (ports 8111, 8112) with public/untrusted network exposure. Cross-reference with patch compliance data for CVE-2026-63077. Alert on unpatched instances, prioritizing assets with external-facing configuration.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Process Execution and Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause is 'deserialization of untrusted data' leading to RCE. Pipeline omitted detection for post-compromise execution (T1203), which is the exploitation payload manifestation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity service process (java.exe with TeamCity classpath) spawning unexpected child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh. Correlate timing with agent polling traffic. Flag process trees with high suspicious API calls (registry writes, network connects) initiated from Java parent.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Gadget Chain Traffic Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the vulnerability class. No detection was generated for the specific exploitation mechanism—Java serialization payload indicators in network traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deep-packet inspect TeamCity agent polling traffic for Java serialization magic bytes (0xaced0500) followed by common gadget class indicators (ysoserial chains: CommonsCollections, JNDI references). Flag on first occurrence before patch deployment; baseline for false-positive tuning.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Confirmation and Due-Date Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-63077 with federal remediation deadline. Pipeline generated no vulnerability-specific detection or compliance metric despite this being a CISA KEV high-visibility item.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Qualys, Tenable, Rapid7) for CVE-2026-63077 matches on TeamCity instances. Generate risk report stratified by patch status and network exposure. Alert on critical findings with external access and patch compliance < 100% as of 2026-08-07.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Vulnerable Asset Inventory — CVE-2026-63077
suggestion.rationale: Article states this is CISA KEV (actively exploited) and implicitly references asset-exposure hunt via template mention. No UC exists to identify/flag vulnerable instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-63077 against all TeamCity assets. Alert on instances matching affected versions with unauthenticated agent polling protocol enabled, stratified by internet-exposure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling — Exploitation Probe
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation vector: 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' No detection addresses abnormal or malicious polling attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoints for unauthenticated connection attempts from untrusted networks, malformed protocol sequences, or rapid reconnaissance patterns. Baseline legitimate agent-to-server polling and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms RCE payload execution. No UC captures post-exploitation command execution spawned from TeamCity JVM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity java.exe (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl), especially unsigned binaries or interpreters not present in baseline. Correlate timing with agent polling anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Scanner Hit Correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires rapid inventory triage. Missing UC to correlate scanner detections with patch-management timeline (federal due 2026-08-08).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger alert on CVE-2026-63077 hits. Cross-reference patch status; flag unpatched instances. Escalate internet-exposed systems. Include federal deadline in alert context.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Instances with Vulnerable Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could allow unauthenticated remote code execution'. CISA KEV profile demands immediate asset inventory. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure use case despite template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for TeamCity instances listening on network, correlate version against CVE-2026-63077 affected versions. Hunt for unauthenticated HTTP requests to TeamCity default ports (8111, 443) from external IP ranges indicating exposure.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'via the agent polling protocol'. Pipeline missed this specific exploitation vector entirely—no HTTP/protocol-level detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints with serialized Java object payloads or anomalous Content-Length/encoding patterns consistent with deserialization attacks. Flag requests from non-agent IP ranges or with suspicious User-Agent headers.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Execution from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote code execution' presupposes process spawning post-exploitation. Pipeline failed to generate execution-phase use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, nc) spawned by TeamCity server (java.exe parent) or agent processes. Alert on outbound network connections or file writes initiated by TeamCity child processes.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Lateral Movement from Compromised TeamCity Host
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD platform compromise typically precedes internal reconnaissance. Article omits post-compromise activity, but pipeline should anticipate standard kill-chain progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network scanning (nmap, psexec, wmic) or credential enumeration (net, whoami, Get-ADUser) originating from compromised TeamCity host. Flag lateral movement attempts to internal systems post-exploit.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell / C2 Callback from TeamCity Agent
suggestion.rationale: Deserialization RCE payloads typically include C2 callbacks. Article describes exploitation mechanism but pipeline omitted command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent processes for unusual outbound connections (non-standard ports, unknown external IPs, DNS queries to rare TLDs). Correlate against known C2 infrastructure IP/domain lists.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'public-facing application' as prerequisite for exploitation; templates reference asset-exposure hunt pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for TeamCity instances accessible on standard ports (8111, 9000) without authentication barriers. Correlate with vulnerability scanner confirmations for CVE-2026-63077 presence. High urgency: CISA federal due-date 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' directly; KEV entries are actively exploited and must be matched against asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result marking CVE-2026-63077 presence in TeamCity deployments. Prioritize unauthenticated/exposed instances. Escalate to critical if within 48 hours of patch due-date without patch confirmation.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in Agent Polling Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is explicitly 'deserialization of untrusted data via agent polling protocol'; standard YARA/content-based detection should trigger on malformed serialized objects in TeamCity agent communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic (default port 9000) for indicators of serialized gadget chain objects or uncommon Java serialization magic bytes (0xaced) in agent-to-server communications. Baseline normal agent update patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal TeamCity Agent Polling Activity
suggestion.rationale: Agent polling is the specific exploitation vector mentioned; suspicious polling patterns (frequency spikes, unusual source IPs, failed authentication attempts to polling endpoint) indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid polling requests to the agent polling endpoint (/updateInfo, /getWork) from unauthenticated sources, or polling requests with Content-Length anomalies suggesting payload injection. Correlate with failed TeamCity login attempts if auth is eventually added.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Command Execution Post-Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote code execution'; successful exploitation will result in process execution, reverse shells, or credential harvesting on the TeamCity server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On TeamCity server hosts, detect unexpected child processes spawned by Tomcat/java.exe (TeamCity process), especially powershell.exe, cmd.exe, bash, or outbound network connections. Alert on first-time process executions from the TeamCity application user context.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Web Console Access Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Initial access requires reaching the web UI; reconnaissance scanning and login attempts will precede agent-protocol exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web UI scanning (GET /login, /admin, /monitoring endpoints with 200s from external IPs) with subsequent agent polling exploitation attempts within 1 hour. High FP risk from legitimate CI/CD traffic; baseline normal scanning patterns per environment.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Unauthenticated Agent Polling RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Zero use cases generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/GET requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (/agentDetails, /buildAgent/xml) from unauthenticated sources or from external IPs. Monitor for malformed agent polling requests containing serialized Java payloads or binary blobs indicative of deserialization attacks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Match (Patch Compliance)
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and scanner matching against CVE-2026-63077 with federal due date 2026-08-08. No compliance or scanner-driven detection UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all TeamCity instances returning vulnerable versions (pre-2024.x, versions prior to patch release) via scanner queries. Cross-reference with asset inventory and network exposure data to prioritize public-facing instances for emergency patching before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Deserialization RCE Execution on TeamCity Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'deserialization of untrusted data' leading to RCE. No post-exploitation execution detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from the TeamCity process (typically java.exe or the agent launcher service). Detect execution of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, or script interpreters initiated by the TeamCity service without corresponding authenticated user action in the TeamCity UI.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing TeamCity Instance Enumeration (Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' as the attack surface and recommends asset-exposure hunting. No discovery or fingerprinting UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP 200 responses with TeamCity signatures (Server headers containing 'TeamCity', login page patterns, /update/* endpoints). Correlate with external IP ranges to identify TeamCity instances reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-check against CMDB to detect unscheduled public exposure.

suggestion.title: Federal CISA KEV Remediation Deadline Tracking (2026-08-08)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies mandatory federal patch due date; CISA KEV implies regulatory tracking requirement. No compliance-tracking or timeline-driven UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create compliance alert for all TeamCity deployments requiring patch to version 2024.03+ by 2026-08-08. Escalate any instances still running vulnerable versions post-deadline as audit findings and trigger emergency remediation procedures.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unauthenticated TeamCity Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is the recommended approach and references template. Vulnerability is exploitable by 'unauthenticated' attackers via publicly-facing TeamCity instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for TeamCity instances with CVE-2026-63077 not patched. Cross-reference with external-facing IP data and authentication logs to identify instances accessible without credentials. Baseline normal agent polling traffic; flag unauthenticated connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Gadget Chain Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'deserialization of untrusted data'—a Java exploitation technique that typically manifests as process spawning from Java context shortly after malicious payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Java process (java.exe or java) spawning command shells or suspicious child processes after receiving non-standard serialized payloads via agent polling protocol. Correlate network inbound telemetry (port 8111 or custom agent port) with immediate child process creation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Agent Polling Protocol Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'agent polling protocol' as the specific attack vector. Pipeline missed network-layer detection for payload injection or protocol abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoint (default /RPC2) for non-standard request sizes, malformed serialized Java objects, or unusual frequency patterns. Baseline legitimate agent polling; flag deviations including requests from non-agent IP ranges or containing binary serialization markers.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution from TeamCity Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE (article's stated outcome) will manifest as attacker commands executed in TeamCity process context. Pipeline did not suggest behavioral detection for post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After exploitation, detect unusual child processes spawned from TeamCity JVM context (cmd.exe, bash, powershell, curl, wget). Look for network connections from TeamCity service account to external C2 ranges, file enumeration activity (dir, ls, find), or privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Patch Compliance vs. Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and provides federal due date (2026-08-08). Pipeline should suggest scanner-based compliance detection aligned to remediation deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-63077 across TeamCity estate. Flag any instance with unsupported/unpatched status as of due date 2026-08-08. Correlate with network exposure scans to prioritize instances accessible from internet or untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Authentication Log Absence / Unauthenticated Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is exploitable without authentication. Missing authentication event paired with successful payload delivery is a distinct behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful API requests to TeamCity /RPC2 agent endpoint without prior successful authentication log entry. Look for missing 401/403 HTTP responses or direct payload delivery bypassing login flow. Non-existent or failed authentication attempts followed by RCE-indicative activity suggests exploitation of auth bypass flaw.

suggestion.title: npm Package Post-Install Script Execution with Environment Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'self-propagating npm worm' via postinstall hooks. Pipeline supplied no detection for suspicious npm script execution or environment variable access during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install triggering child processes spawning curl/wget/powershell. Monitor for env variable read operations on $GITHUB_* or $ACTIONS_* during npm script execution. Flag package.json postinstall/preinstall that encode C2 exfiltration.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Runner Secret Exfiltration via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states worm 'extracting GitHub Actions runner secrets'. No detection provided for theft of $GITHUB_TOKEN or ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN environment variables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow logs for unauthorized reads of $GITHUB_TOKEN or actions/* environment vars. Detect HTTP POST from runner IPs to non-github.com IPs with base64-encoded JWTs or OAuth tokens in request body. Correlate with Ethereum RPC calls.

suggestion.title: Ethereum Smart Contract C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'using Ethereum smart contracts for C2 routing'. Pipeline missed blockchain interaction detection entirely despite this being primary C2 mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS to Ethereum RPC providers (infura.io, alchemy.com, etherscan.io) and public nodes. Alert on repeated eth_call or eth_getTransactionByHash queries to the same contract address. Flag data field patterns encoding command parameters in hex format.

suggestion.title: Transitive npm Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating worm implies lateral spread via dependency trees. Pipeline did not detect package.json manipulation or registry substitution attacks that enable persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to package-lock.json in projects that imported ChainDrop. Detect injection of unexpected package versions from non-official npm registry URLs. Alert on .npm local cache directory modifications introducing malicious tarballs.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Credentials Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain worm targeting 'developer tooling' requires npm publish access. Pipeline missed detection of .npmrc exfiltration and registry token theft for re-propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cat/Get-Content of ~/.npmrc or global npm config. Flag npm login without human interaction or registry publish commands from CI/CD contexts. Detect base64-encoded authToken patterns in environment or network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: ChainDrop Package Installation Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Initial access vector is npm package installation. Pipeline provided zero IOCs or indicators for known-malicious package names, sample hashes, or checksums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of npm packages by name/version/checksum. Alert on installation of packages matching ChainDrop typosquatting variants or from non-default registries. Compare installed package SHA256 against known-malicious sample databases (e.g., VirusTotal, npm audit).

suggestion.title: Vishing-Triggered SSO Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'contact employees on their personal mobile phones while spoofing corporate help-desks and claiming that workers need to enroll in passkeys or update their multi-factor authentication settings. Victims are then directed to domains impersonating the targeted employee's company.' Clear pretexting + forced auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication events that follow vishing call reports or occur outside normal user patterns (geography, time, device). Alert on MFA/passkey enrollment flows triggered without user-initiated requests. Detect credential use from IPs/locations not associated with employee immediately after call windows.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Kit Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'domains impersonating the targeted employee's company that host adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits designed to steal credentials and session cookies in real time.' Requires monitoring for MITM credential capture infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on lookalike domain registrations (typosquatting patterns) created within 7 days pre-attack. Monitor proxy logs for user redirects to these imposter domains followed by authentication attempts. Cross-reference with Certificate Transparency logs for rushed certificate issuance on suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Session Cookie Extraction and MITM Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steal credentials and session cookies in real time' enabling immediate cloud access. This is active session hijacking bypassing MFA validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when session cookies are used to authenticate cloud API calls without re-validating MFA. Alert on authentication events with mismatched risk profiles (new IP/country/device) but valid session tokens. Monitor for SSO token refreshes that skip secondary authentication.

suggestion.title: Bulk Cross-Platform Cloud Data Extraction via SSO
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms...use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to.' Single-session mass lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when one user session enumerates and accesses 5+ distinct cloud services (SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Exchange) within 10 minutes via API. Detect programmatic resource enumeration immediately post-SSO login. Flag bulk data read operations characteristic of automated harvesting rather than interactive browsing.

suggestion.title: Security Alert and Password-Reset Email Suppression
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'delete security notifications and password-reset emails from compromised inboxes.' Post-exploitation log deletion to prevent detection and account recovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk deletions of emails with 'alert', 'verify', 'security', or 'password reset' in subject. Detect mailbox rules auto-deleting security notifications. Alert on deletion of messages from Microsoft365-noreply or Okta notification addresses during credential-compromise windows.

suggestion.title: Multi-Brand Extortion Campaign Attribution Linkage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'While previously operating under the public brand BlackFile, UNC6671 has diversified its extortion operations across multiple public brands, including Redact, Pink, Helix, and Falcon.' Single group, multiple ransom personas.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ransom note artifacts, Bitcoin wallet addresses, and negotiation email aliases across public extortion sites (Helix, Falcon, Redact, Pink). Identify shared payment infrastructure (BTCpay instances, Monero addresses). Link via wallet clustering analysis and timing correlation of attacks.

suggestion.title: Detect KVM Exploitation via Guest-to-Host Escape Primitives
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Privileged L1 Guest Code Escape to Linux Hosts' — requires detection of abnormal guest process attempts to probe KVM memory-mapped I/O, invoke privileged ioctl() calls, or inject into host kernel address space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on guest VM processes executing ioctl(KVM_*) calls outside libvirt context, or attempting mmap() of /dev/kvm with RWX permissions. Flag kernel module loads from guest-controlled paths or EPT manipulation attempts (if visible in hypervisor logs).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: Inventory Affected KVM and Linux Kernel Versions
suggestion.rationale: Zapscape affects specific KVM/kernel versions per title. No version IOCs extracted; pipeline should trigger asset inventory queries to identify vulnerable hypervisor hosts before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Linux hosts for kernel version (uname -r) and KVM module presence (lsmod | grep kvm). Cross-reference against published Zapscape CVE advisory for affected versions. Alert on unpatched critical-severity KVM flaws in production.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Escape Rootkit Installation on Hypervisor Host
suggestion.rationale: Successful guest escape grants host-level code execution. Title scenario implies attacker will persist via kernel module, systemd service, or bootkit — standard post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hypervisor hosts for suspicious kernel module loads, new systemd service creation, or cron job installation coinciding with anomalous guest-process activity or KVM process crashes. Alert on unsigned kernel drivers loaded post-exploit window.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Detect Compromised Host Attacking Sibling VMs
suggestion.rationale: Escaped attacker on L0 host can abuse hypervisor APIs to compromise other guest VMs on same physical server — common post-escape objective in multi-tenant environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag hypervisor host processes (qemu, libvirtd) executing with elevated privileges and spawning new guest VMs or attaching to guest memory/disks outside normal administrative workflows. Monitor for host→guest file or network tunneling.

suggestion.title: Detect Guest Code Invoking Hypervisor Abort/Reset Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Zapscape likely exploits L1 hypervisor instruction emulation or fault-handling bugs. Guest code triggering hypervisor abort, reset, or nested-virtualization faults could signal exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor guest VMs for execution of privileged instructions (vmcall, vmmcall, svm exit) or crafted CPU fault sequences (triple-fault, MCE injection). Detect nested virtualization attempts or VMXON/SVMON execution from unprivileged guest context.

suggestion.title: Dangerous ReplacePathRegex pattern in Traefik config — no separator enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'When it is configured with a regular expression that captures user-controlled path segments without a mandatory separator (for example regex: "^/api(.*)", replacement: "/$1")'. No UC detects this vulnerable config pattern itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Traefik config files (/etc/traefik/traefik.yml, /etc/traefik/dynamic.yml) for modifications. Flag ReplacePathRegex patterns where the regex captures without enforcing path separators (e.g., '^/api(.*)' or '^/admin(.*)' without '/' prefix in replacement). Alert on files modified outside of change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Traefik config modification by non-admin process
suggestion.rationale: Enabling this vulnerability requires config changes. UC missing for detecting who/what modifies Traefik configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Traefik config files for write events by non-privileged accounts or unexpected process names (e.g., web server process, automation tool). Correlate with Traefik service restarts to catch activation of malicious configs.

suggestion.title: Backend access pattern anomaly — protected routes reached via traversal path
suggestion.rationale: Article truncates at 'Traefik forwarded to the backend wi...' but clearly implies backend systems receive unauthorized requests. No UC correlates backend logs with traversal attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline historical access logs for backend application servers (tracking IPs/users accessing /admin, /api/admin, /private). Alert when access originates from IPs that never previously accessed those routes, particularly from public-facing IP ranges or when HTTP referer headers indicate path traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Traefik version inventory check for unpatched 2.x releases
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions CVE-2026-48020 as a second CVE tied to same vulnerability. No UC performs version-level asset discovery beyond generic vuln scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for Traefik versions and cross-reference GHSA-cxjq-mrr5-89rv advisory fix versions. Alternatively, parse 'traefik version' command output from Endpoint.Processes logs; flag versions published before fix date.

suggestion.title: Interrupt Injection Attack Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Interrupt Injection Attack'—a direct exploitation technique. Pipeline identified zero attack steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawning with unusual interrupt-level privilege requests or kernel-mode callback registrations. Alert on attempts to load unsigned or malicious interrupt handlers, especially in kernel drivers or via exception handling manipulation.

suggestion.title: Spectre v2 Mitigation Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'bypass[es] Spectre v2 defenses'—core attack objective. Pipeline did not map to defense-evasion kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes disabling IBRS (Indirect Branch Restricted Speculation) or other Spectre v2 mitigations via CPU MSR writes. Alert on unexpected kernel module loads or privileged operations that modify CPU security registers post-boot.

suggestion.title: Speculative Execution Side-Channel Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Interrupt injection attacks bypass hardware defenses to leak data via speculative execution side channels. Pipeline missed data-leakage component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous memory access patterns and timing side-channel indicators (high-frequency memory probes, cache-timing measurements). Correlate with unusual network exfiltration or data staging in temporary files.

suggestion.title: CPU Feature Manipulation and Control Register Modification
suggestion.rationale: Bypass of hardware defenses implies direct CPU control register access. Article references Intel and AMD architecture; no detection UC covers MSR or CR register tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to write to CPU model-specific registers (MSRs) associated with Spectre/Meltdown mitigations (MSR 0x48, 0x49 on Intel; SPEC_CTRL on AMD). Flag user-mode access attempts to privileged CPU state via WinRing0 or similar drivers.

suggestion.title: Firmware or BIOS Modification Pre-Attack
suggestion.rationale: Hardware-level vulnerability exploitation often requires firmware control. Article does not clarify if BIOS/firmware changes needed, but interrupt injection at hardware level may require pre-boot compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for firmware update tools, BIOS flashing utilities, or attempts to access NVRAM/UEFI variables. Alert on privileged processes accessing firmware interfaces or system firmware integrity check failures.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol' — this is the sole attack surface requiring initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling endpoints (/rest/api/agents/builds or similar) for unauthenticated requests from untrusted sources. Flag requests containing serialized Java object payloads (ACED0005 magic bytes), abnormally large request bodies, or anomalous binary/encoded data patterns in POST bodies.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference CISA KEV feed against internal vulnerability scanner output, filtered to TeamCity product. Track patch application timeline and flag instances still unpatched 48h before federal due-date (2026-08-06) for escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—need detection for requests to agent endpoints without auth headers or from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to TeamCity agent polling endpoints (e.g. /admin/remote-run, /mnt, agent API paths) from external IPs or lacking Authorization headers. Flag successful 200/302 responses to unauthenticated agent endpoints, particularly from non-corporate ASNs.

suggestion.title: Serialized Java Objects in TeamCity HTTP Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'deserialization of untrusted data'—ysoserial gadget chains and serialized Java objects (magic bytes: ac ed 00 05) indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST bodies to TeamCity for Java serialized object magic bytes or Base64-encoded gadget chains (CommonsCollections, Spring Framework exploits). Alert on ysoserial payloads or known deserialization gadgets in agent polling protocol traffic.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing TeamCity Inventory and Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes public-facing application vulnerability actively exploited—organizations must discover and patch exposed TeamCity instances before 2026-08-08 federal due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and network discovery for TeamCity servers (port 8080, HTTP banner matching, certificate CN). Cross-reference with CMDB to identify instances accepting inbound traffic from public IPs. Correlate with patch status to surface unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Process Spawning from TeamCity Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote code execution'—successful exploitation triggers child processes (cmd.exe, powershell, reverse shells) from TeamCity runtime, detectable post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal TeamCity process trees. Alert on java.exe (TeamCity) or teamcity-agent spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wget, curl, bash, or known reverse-shell utilities with minimal historical precedent.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Verification (CISA KEV)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandate: 'Federal patch due 2026-08-08', actively exploited. Patch status is primary control; scanner-based compliance is baseline defensive action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run authenticated vulnerability scan across all TeamCity assets; flag instances reporting CVE-2026-63077 present. Correlate deployed version against JetBrains advisory remediation versions and generate escalation if unpatched past 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanner Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article states TeamCity 'contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability' — vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Nessus) will flag this CVE on exposed instances. Direct asset-exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scan results or CMDB patch-compliance queries reporting CVE-2026-63077 on any TeamCity instance. Cross-reference with asset inventory to prioritize exposed services. Federal patch due is 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Agent Polling Protocol Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'agent polling protocol' as the exploitation vector and emphasizes 'unauthenticated' access. Network baseline should flag anomalous inbound connections to the TeamCity agent port (typically 9090).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound traffic to TeamCity on the agent polling port from external or untrusted subnets without corresponding authentication handshake logs. Baseline expected agent IPs and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Process Execution After RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — post-compromise activity should surface as TeamCity service spawning unexpected child processes or commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TeamCity service account executing shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or suspicious child processes. Establish baseline of legitimate TeamCity child processes and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in Agent Polling Traffic
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is specifically 'deserialization of untrusted data' — IDS/IPS and DLP should have signatures for serialized Java object payloads in agent polling protocol frames.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: IDS/IPS rule set should include signatures for Java serialization gadget chains (ysoserial payloads, Commons Collections, etc.) traversing the TeamCity agent polling protocol. Alert on any match before application-layer filtering.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance — TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 by Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles always include a federal patch deadline ('Federal patch due: 2026-08-08'). Compliance queries and ticketing must reflect this hard date for auditor and regulatory inquiries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch-management or CMDB for TeamCity instances not updated to patched version by 2026-08-08. Generate compliance report and escalate to asset owners. Document any exceptions for audit trail.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised TeamCity Agent
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via agent polling protocol gives attacker foothold on a build-infrastructure host — likely avenue for lateral movement to other CI/CD systems, repositories, or production infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for unusual outbound connections or lateral SMB/SSH activity from TeamCity server to other infrastructure. Correlate with RCE indicators (unusual TeamCity process spawning) to catch early lateral-movement chains.

suggestion.title: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states this is in CISA KEV (actively exploited), with CVE-2026-63077 as the identifier and federal patch due 2026-08-08. Pipeline must generate vulnerability hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan inventory for JetBrains TeamCity instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-63077. Priority: all internet-facing or exposed instances. Cross-reference asset inventory against CISA KEV database and vendor patch advisories. Alert on any instance not patched by federal due date 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol.' Pipeline must generate detection for unauthorized agent communication attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity application logs and network traffic for agent polling protocol requests from unexpected sources. Flag any unauthenticated agent polling attempts, especially those followed by process creation or command execution. Correlate with TeamCity access logs for non-admin users initiating polling requests.

suggestion.title: Java Deserialization Attack Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the root mechanism. This is a common gadget-chain exploitation vector that should trigger detection when observed in TeamCity request payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity application logs for serialization/deserialization errors or exceptions. Look for HTTP POST requests to agent polling endpoints with binary/base64-encoded payloads. Alert on process spawning (cmd.exe, bash, powershell) with parent process TeamCity or Java runtime immediately after suspicious HTTP activity.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Patch Compliance Verification (Federal Deadline)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08.' CISA KEV entries trigger compliance requirements for federal agencies; enterprises must track this as audit-material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management systems and vulnerability scanners for TeamCity patch status. Verify all instances have been upgraded to patched version before 2026-08-08. Generate exception report for any unpatched instances with justification and timeline. Cross-reference against CISA KEV federal due-date for audit readiness.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed TeamCity Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article context (CISA KEV, active exploitation, public-facing application attack) implies the risk is from internet-facing TeamCity deployments. Asset exposure hunt must be prioritized.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for TeamCity instances accessible from the internet via port 8111 (default) or other common ports. Cross-reference public DNS records, certificate transparency logs, and Shodan/Censys for TeamCity hostnames/IPs. Flag any internet-facing instances for immediate patch/segmentation review.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames this as 'exploit public-facing application' — need to enumerate internet-accessible TeamCity instances before attacker finds them. Prerequisite hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for TeamCity default ports (8111, 80, 443) accessible from internet. Cross-reference Shodan/Censys queries with asset inventory. Flag any exposed instances not explicitly documented as intentionally public.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Agent Polling Protocol Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation 'via the agent polling protocol' — need network-level detection for malformed or oversized polling requests that could deliver deserialization payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent-polling endpoints for unusual request sizes, non-standard headers, repeated failures (deserialization errors), or requests from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with high-entropy payload indicators.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via TeamCity Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution' — post-exploitation phase requires detection of command execution spawned from TeamCity JVM process, particularly unexpected child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by TeamCity java.exe/java process: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, wget, curl, nc. Especially suspicious if spawned without prior build job context or from unexpected build stages.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Outbound C2 Connections Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After RCE succeeds, attackers typically establish C2 or exfiltration channels — need to detect unexpected network connections initiated by TeamCity process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound network connections from TeamCity process to non-whitelisted destinations, especially on unusual ports (4444, 5555, 8080, 443 with anomalous TLS handshake patterns). Monitor DNS queries from TeamCity context for C2 domain patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires active scanning — basic hygiene is to match vulnerability scanner output for this specific CVE against managed asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CVE-2026-63077 matches from vulnerability scanners with asset management database. Escalate any matches immediately; cross-reference patch management system to confirm remediation status and patch application date.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Error Spikes in TeamCity Logs
suggestion.rationale: Failed exploitation attempts will generate deserialization exceptions in application logs — error pattern can be early warning of active scanning/probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity logs for sudden increase in java.io.NotSerializableException, InvalidClassException, or ClassNotFoundException errors, especially clustered in time or originating from single source IP. Baseline normal error rates first.

suggestion.title: TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 Exploitation Attempts Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol'—this is the primary attack surface. Pipeline generated zero use cases for the known-exploited vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity /RPC2 and agent polling endpoints for serialized object payloads, POST requests from unusual sources, and error responses consistent with exploit attempts. Track HTTP 500 errors and exception logs coinciding with malformed requests.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Registration Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation via agent polling allows attacker-controlled agent registration. Article describes 'agent polling protocol'—agents are the execution primitive after compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new agent registrations with mismatched hostnames/IPs, agents from unexpected networks, and sudden spikes in agent build queue activity post-vulnerability window (2026-08-08 patch date).

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies widespread internet-facing TeamCity installations being scanned. Article describes 'public-facing application'—asset inventory is the prerequisite hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all public-facing TeamCity instances (default ports 8111/8112) and cross-reference against patched versions. Flag instances still running builds post-patch-due-date (2026-08-08) without confirmed remediation.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'deserialization of untrusted data'. Pipeline missed the serialization-specific attack surface—standard HTTP monitoring won't catch crafted binary payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling traffic for Java serialization magic bytes (ACED0005), unusual ysoserial gadget chain indicators, and ClassNotFound exceptions in agent logs during exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Creation from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE will spawn attacker commands. Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution'—post-exploitation command execution is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity JVM (java.exe), especially shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or lateral-movement tools. Baseline TeamCity process behavior and flag deviations post-2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Scan Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal remediation by 2026-08-08. Pipeline should have produced a compliance-hunting template—zero UCs means scanning strategy is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-validate vuln scanner detections for CVE-2026-63077 against actual patched versions in asset database. Identify scanner false-negatives (claimed patched but exploit still functional) and validate all TeamCity instances ≤2026-08-08 show remediation evidence in patch logs.

suggestion.title: Redis Public-Facing Service Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links TeamPCP to 'Redis Attacks' — initial access vector should have been reconstructed. Expects detection for CVE exploitation or unauthenticated Redis protocol abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to TCP 6379 (Redis default) from untrusted IP ranges; flag successful commands without prior authentication handshake; correlate with known Redis RCE payloads (e.g., MODULE LOAD, SCRIPT commands).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis Authentication Credentials Cached
suggestion.rationale: Redis supply chain compromise often involves credential harvesting or hardcoded auth tokens. Article mentions 'Supply Chain Campaign'—credentials are the pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for plaintext Redis credentials in process arguments (–requirepass, CONFIG SET password), environment variables, or config files in suspicious locations; correlate with package installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Modification or Metadata Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Later Supply Chain Campaign'—pipeline should detect repository poisoning, package signing violations, or deployment of modified package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package version downgrades, unsigned or revoked-certificate packages, packages delivered outside normal CI/CD, or hash mismatches against official repositories.

suggestion.title: TeamPCP C2 Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: Redis compromise is an entry point; article dating back to 2020 suggests persistent C2 infrastructure associated with TeamPCP. Should detect known TeamPCP C2 domains, IPs, or TLS certificates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network egress from Redis-compromised hosts against known TeamPCP OSINT (domain registrations, ASN patterns, certificate CN/SANs); flag anomalous outbound protocols or suspicious TLS renegotiations.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Redis Command Sequence (Lateral Movement)
suggestion.rationale: After Redis compromise, attacker executes reconnaissance and lateral movement. Article timeline (2020+) suggests multi-stage attack; pipeline should detect suspicious Redis KEYS, SCAN, or data exfiltration commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis command logs for KEYS *, SCAN 0, AUTH attempts with common/weak credentials, or unexpected DUMP/MIGRATE commands; correlate timing with exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Malware Dropper via Compromised Redis Data Structure
suggestion.rationale: Redis module loading (MODULE LOAD) or serialized-object deserialization can execute arbitrary code. Supply chain context implies packaged payloads; should detect suspicious binary or script storage in Redis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Redis MODULE LOAD followed by child process spawning; detect unusual script or binary serialization in Redis key-value pairs; correlate with supply chain artifact timestamps.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes self-propagating npm worm; worms typically persist via lifecycle scripts. Article body should detail install/postinstall hook execution. No UC generated despite this being core malware behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/uninstall operations preceded by unexpected child processes spawning shell interpreters. Alert on env vars passed to postinstall scripts, especially those accessing secrets or making outbound network calls.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Environment Variable Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states worm 'extracting GitHub Actions runner secrets.' No UC maps credential access from CI/CD secrets. This is the attack's high-value vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes reading GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, or other CI/CD secrets from environment within npm module code paths. Flag data exfiltration via DNS TXT records, base64 in HTTP headers, or blockchain contract calls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ethereum Smart Contract Interaction from npm Module
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Ethereum smart contracts for C2 routing.' Pipeline generated zero C2 detection. This is anomalous network behavior—npm modules should not initiate blockchain transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes making HTTP/HTTPS connections to blockchain RPC endpoints (infura.io, alchemy.com, etherscan.io) or resolving Ethereum contract addresses. Flag payload encoding within contract call parameters (0x... patterns in data field).

suggestion.title: npm Module Self-Propagation via Dependency Graph Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Self-Propagating npm Worm.' Worms must replicate. No UC detects malicious dependency injection or package.json modification during install. This is the propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json modifications (additions to dependencies, devDependencies, or version downgrades) and npm registry auth token usage from non-privileged accounts. Flag npm publish operations from compromised package contexts.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from node_modules with Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Worm must execute malicious code post-install. Article provides no specific detection hypothesis, but npm malware signature is child process spawning from node_modules tree with outbound network calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation from node_modules/.bin or node_modules/<package>/lib paths with subsequent DNS/TLS connections to attacker infrastructure. Baseline legitimate package binary usage; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Disclosure in Logs or Temporary Files
suggestion.rationale: If secrets are exfiltrated, they may be staged in logs, environment dumps, or temp files. No UC maps this ex-filtration pattern specific to CI/CD secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm install output logs and temp directories for leaked GitHub tokens (ghp_* patterns), AWS keys, or Ethereum private keys. Cross-reference file modification times against malicious package install timestamps.

suggestion.title: Vishing with Passkey/MFA Update Pretexting
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'UNC6671 operators typically contact employees on their personal mobile phones while spoofing corporate help-desks and claiming that workers need to enroll in passkeys or update their multi-factor authentication settings.' No detection use case for inbound social engineering calls followed by credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound calls claiming to originate from corporate helpdesk (via caller ID spoofing detection) with failed or successful SSO authentication attempts occurring within 30 minutes from unusual geographies. Alert on patterns of employees reporting helpdesk verification calls followed by credential-reset or multi-factor-authentication enrollment events.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Kit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Victims are then directed to domains impersonating the targeted employee's company that host adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits designed to steal credentials and session cookies in real time.' No UC for detecting credential harvesting via lookalike domain hosting or session cookie interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains similar to corporate identity (typosquats, subdomain spoofs). Flag SSL certificates issued within days for domains impersonating known corporate infrastructure. Correlate failed authentication attempts to legitimate SSO endpoints with proxy traffic to lookalike domains in the same time window.

suggestion.title: Bulk Automated Cloud Data Exfiltration via Compromised SSO
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'After stealing Microsoft 365 or Okta single-sign-on accounts, the attackers log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account... hackers then use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to.' No UC for detecting automated enumeration and bulk exfiltration across linked cloud platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSO sign-ins from new geographies immediately following vishing campaigns. Flag rapid, sequential API calls from a single compromised account accessing multiple cloud services (>10 apps in 15 minutes). Detect automated downloads of large numbers of files or calendar/mail objects from OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, or third-party cloud apps within minutes of SSO compromise.

suggestion.title: Security Notification and Password-Reset Email Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'delete security notifications and password-reset emails from compromised inboxes.' No UC for detecting adversary suppression of security alerts or password-reset communications post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk email deletions (>50 emails in 5 minutes) or rapid moves to deleted items, especially emails from security teams, helpdesk, or containing password-reset or MFA-verification keywords. Alert when security notifications or password-reset emails are deleted before being read or within seconds of arrival by a user who shows no prior email deletion patterns.

suggestion.title: Multi-Platform Lateral Movement via Stolen SSO Session Cookies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'After stealing Microsoft 365 or Okta single-sign-on accounts, the attackers log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account.' No UC for detecting lateral movement across multiple cloud platforms using session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to SSO dashboard consoles from new/unusual IP geographies within hours of initial credential compromise. Flag accounts accessing >8 distinct cloud applications (Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Slack, Workday, etc.) in a single session. Alert on session tokens used to authenticate to multiple platforms from a single source IP without corresponding user-agent diversity.

suggestion.title: Automated Cloud Resource Enumeration Post-SSO Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should detect the discovery phase implied by: 'use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to,' indicating system enumeration of available cloud resources and permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid enumeration of cloud application catalogs, Okta app lists, or Azure app registrations (>20 API calls in 2 minutes). Detect queries for permissions, roles, and group memberships via Graph API or Okta APIs immediately post-compromise. Flag when a single account queries cloud resource tags or metadata to discover what data is available before exfiltration.

suggestion.title: KVM Guest-to-Host Privilege Escalation via Hypercall
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'privileged L1 guest code escape to Linux hosts' — escape from guest to host kernel requires abnormal hypercall sequences or KVM instruction emulation exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequences of unusual hypercalls from guest VMs, particularly those attempting to access host kernel address space, modify VMCS structures, or trigger unhandled page faults at host privilege level. Alert on nested VM contexts (L1→L2) attempting cross-level escapes.

suggestion.title: KVM Memory-Mapped I/O Escape Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: KVM escapes commonly exploit MMIO mishandling between guest and host; 'Zapscape' likely leverages improper MMIO boundary checking to read/write host kernel memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or sequential MMIO operations from guest context targeting host-reserved address ranges, or MMIO operations that correlate with subsequent kernel privilege checks being bypassed.

suggestion.title: Host Kernel Code Execution from Guest Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful escape must result in code execution at ring-0; expect kernel panics, privilege escalation syscalls, or unexpected kernel module loads correlating with guest VM activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate guest VM process activity with host kernel panics, BUG() macro triggers, or oops messages. Flag sequences where guest syscalls are immediately followed by root-level code execution on host or unexpected kernel module operations.

suggestion.title: Nested Virtualization L1/L2 Boundary Crossing
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'L1 guest code' — this is nested virtualization. Attacker escapes L1 context to L2 or to host; L1 implies guest-within-guest scenario not typically monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of nested VM configurations where L1 guests attempt to allocate excessive memory, trigger rapid VMEXIT rates, or perform operations inconsistent with normal nested virtualization workloads.

suggestion.title: KVM Kernel Parameter or Data Structure Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Escapes often involve overwriting guest-accessible kernel structures (e.g., modifying KVM pte flags, vCPU state). Article's severity suggests memory corruption vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to kernel virtual address space from guest userspace, or modifications to page table entries via guest-accessible mechanisms. Flag use of mprotect/mmap on /dev/kvm or /dev/mem with CAP_SYS_ADMIN-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Hugging Face Model Repository Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states model repositories as attack surface: 'model repositories execute arbitrary code.' Pipeline missed initial-access detection for reconnaissance-phase downloads from untrusted Hugging Face accounts or newly-created repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git clone or curl downloads from huggingface.co to local directories; flag repos created within last 30 days or from accounts with zero social signals. Alert on Python processes invoking git/curl with homoglyph-variant model names (e.g., diffuser-s vs diffusers).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via Pickle/Safetensors Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'execute arbitrary code' during model load. Diffusers library deserializes model files (pickle, safetensors, pt) during import—standard vector for code injection. Pipeline produced zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Python processes import diffusers.DiffusionPipeline or transformers followed by unexpected child-process spawning, network egress, or file writes outside expected model-cache directories. Inspect for pickle.load(), torch.load() on untrusted paths.

suggestion.title: Model Weight Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Flaws enable code injection 'in model repositories'—attackers can poison weights. Pipeline ignored persistence/supply-chain technique mapping (T1195.001, T1195.002) entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check downloaded model artifacts (model.safetensors, pytorch_model.bin, config.json) against SHA256 hashes published by Hugging Face or verified sources. Alert on mismatches. Monitor ~/.cache/huggingface for unexpected file modifications.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Poisoning via Model Install
suggestion.rationale: Loading Hugging Face models triggers pip installs of diffusers and transformers; malicious repos can hijack dependencies. Article implies supply-chain code-execution vector; pipeline provided no dependency-hygiene detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pip/poetry/uv installs spawned by Python data-science or inference processes. Flag typo-squatted package names, external registry URLs, or installs of packages not in pinned requirements files. Correlate install timestamps with model downloads.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from Model Inference
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'execute arbitrary code'; this manifests as process creation. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detection entirely, leaving subprocess spawning unmonitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal process trees for Python inference workloads. Alert on deviations: parent=python.exe, child=bash/powershell/cmd/sh spawning with suspicious args (curl, wget, nc, reverse-shell markers). Correlate with model-load timestamps from logs.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from Model Inference Process
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution can lead to C2 or data exfiltration. Article emphasizes execution risk; pipeline produced zero command-and-control or exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected DNS queries or TCP/TLS connections from Python processes running inference. Flag non-standard ports, known malware C2 domains, cloud-storage URLs, or pastebin/Telegram endpoints. Baseline legitimate model-download traffic (PyPI, Hugging Face) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Vulnerable TeamCity Instance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-08'—no asset-exposure hunt generated despite template callout in 'Recommended hunts' section. Must detect unpatched or internet-exposed TeamCity instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for internet-exposed TeamCity instances via port enumeration or certificate transparency. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-63077 presence. Flag any instance not patched by 2026-08-08 deadline.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Deserialization Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly 'via the agent polling protocol' with 'deserialization of untrusted data' as root cause—no protocol-specific or payload-based detection generated. Deserialization attacks leave traces in application error logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent polling protocol (typically port 9090) for unauthenticated connection attempts from non-agent IP ranges. Alert on Java deserialization exceptions, ClassCastException, or InvalidObjectException in TeamCity logs correlating with agent polling.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article guarantees 'unauthenticated remote code execution' outcome—no post-compromise execution detection generated. Successful exploitation grants arbitrary code execution on TeamCity server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity JVM process (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl). Flag execution not initiated by TeamCity service account or not from expected build agent subprocesses. Baseline normal TeamCity child processes first.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from TeamCity Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation implies active exploitation in wild—attacker with RCE access will target stored credentials. Article context ('federal agencies required to remediate') suggests sensitive pipeline/code access. No credential-hunting detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthorized file access to TeamCity configuration directories (containing stored VCS/cloud credentials), .ssh keys, or agent properties. Monitor for extraction of stored secrets from TeamCity credential storage or access to build logs containing sensitive data.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised TeamCity Pipeline Access
suggestion.rationale: TeamCity controls build pipelines and deployment credentials across development infrastructure—post-compromise, attacker pivots using captured CI/CD permissions. No lateral movement detection generated despite high-value target profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track TeamCity user logins and VCS credential usage from compromised agent. Flag unusual git clone/push/deploy operations, credential usage from non-expected IP/agent, or activation of dormant/service accounts after initial RCE window.
